title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference 8.3.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: You said you were going to give us maybe a quarterback rotation today, preseason. >> Uh, give me one more day. We'll we will announce it uh tomorrow. Um, that'll be that'll be, you know, public knowledge, but you guys will you guys will hear. I I just the focus is this practice. This is a uh from just a a rep standpoint and just kind of how we believe we're doing business in terms of, you know, coming off a day uh an off day two days ago a little bit lower and then today building this thing up in that third block. um their focus solely had to be on on on this day and not you know what's ahead in in Canton. >> In general, when you approach the preseason as a whole, where has your philosophy come from in terms of do we play these guys, do we not play these guys? Do we rest? >> I I've been I've been across all of it. Um San Francisco, we played our guys, played our guys quite a bit and LA, we didn't play hardly anybody. 23, we played Puka in the first like two series and that was about it and we saw what we need to see. So, it's a case- by case basis, and it's going to be the same here. Who needs it? Um, you know, everyone needs to play football, but there's that that, you know, uh, cost, risk, benefit, if you will, in terms of guys that have played a lot of football in this league that h, you know, what they can do on Sundays and you just want to get them there because the last thing that you want is a guy going down in a game that uh, in the win loss record does not matter. At the same time, each guy has their own little deal of getting getting ready for that first game. So that's that's all the conversations that happened behind the scenes. >> One of the few absences yesterday was Trey Benson. Anything going on with Trey? >> It just just a little discomfort, a little flare up in the left knee. It was unfortunate because uh it was feeling so good and I thought he was really getting his legs underneath him. I thought he strung together pretty, you know, uh some good days. It was it was good news today that he was feeling much better. Um, you know, it was obviously anytime you're coming back from injury like him and he just wants to be out there and he could feel everything going up and then all of a sudden out of nowhere it just kind of flared up on him a little bit. But with that being said, doing much better today. Um, you know, we'll be we'll be very cautious with him though, at least in the in the, you know, kind of dayto-day if you will. >> You expect this to be a multi-week thing for him? >> I I don't expect to be a multi-week. I would I'd be it's I I wouldn't say shocked if he goes in Canton, but but I wouldn't be surprised if he doesn't go. So, >> when when you look at that running back room, we've talked so much about it. We talked about Tyler and where Jeremiah was and where James is, but are you still confident that everybody's going to be able to come together when it needs to be to be as deep as you want it to be in terms of the health and >> I mean, I'll you know, you're never going to be that uh confident and and because of because of how this game is. I mean, it's it even though it's not um you know, live practice, if you will, um there's still it's taxing on their bodies and some guys are coming off these injuries like you've alluded to. So, um, again, you just kind of take it one day at a time with each guy with each position group because there, again, these guys got to go. They got to get themselves ready to go play real football, whether it be in the preseason or obviously the games that count coming in September. So, like, you got to push it. You got to tread. You got to go. Uh, but at the same time, every guy's in a different, you know, spot in their careers and, you know, with their injury history and stuff like that. That's why again there's there's so much more that that goes beyond the scenes as you guys know in terms of you know uh each conversation individually. >> We saw Chase Bantis yesterday get I think one series in with that first team offensive line. Where is he at in his progression and what's kind of the thinking of working him in a little bit there? >> Yeah. Um Isaac just came out for a minute. Uh he was fine. He's a he's a tough dude. You know, he's played a lot of ball in this league and um so and then obviously finished out practice. So when he came in, um, you know, moved moved Chase into into the right side right there. So, uh, moved Isaiah over to the left and, um, you know, kind of next man up right there. And so, I mean, if that happens in the game, that's that's the direction we'll go as of right now. Um, and then, you know, the progress, like I kind of said a couple days ago, I think it's just every single day just getting a little bit more and more comfortable. I alluded to the fact that in in OTAA1, I don't know if he came off the snap one time correctly. Day two, it felt 50%. Day three felt maybe like 60% and then it's just continued to got better and then obviously when that ball's been snapped just continuing to improve understanding the speed of this game u he's got the right look in his eye he's got the right approach um you know he's going to be a good player [snorts] >> that it's just cadence in the NFL as opposed to just clapping and that's the snap com >> I mean every you know something uh it can be quarterback to quarterback too that's why you you know make sure you're you're talking to these quarterbacks whoever the starter is everyone needs it's no one's going to be the exact act same, right? But as close as you can be within the rhythm and in timing of that cadence. So, um, but yeah, I mean, you know, a lot of these guys are are, you know, getting off on that clap right there in college and and that's not the case in the NFL. So, definitely could be part of it. When you get to a preseason game, um, and you have a young quarterback like Carson, let's say, um, as an offensive coach, what kinds of things are you looking for in the preeason to say that guy's made steps forward even though all the game planning might not be there or the, you know, >> clean operation and make the right play for the Cardinals in that time. Um, we're not overly game planning. um you you you go into this game with um you know, you could say just plays that that no matter what they bring are going to be protected both in the run game and the pass game. Uh it might be hot and stuff like that, but you're always going to have answers. You're not going to have game plan gimmicky plays. So, it's it's plays that, you know, all these guys have ran multiple times, whether it be OTAAS, training camp walkthroughs, all that. all the time that we put. I know you guys aren't out there at all the walkthroughs, but we put Carson with the younger guys down in the turf area during that so that they're not just watching the ones for 40 minutes. They're getting their work in. So, I mean, all those reps just continue to add up. But, hey, go out there, operate that huddle. There's no coaching behind you right there, which I have no no question that he's going to do that. He's done a great job with the operation. He's super smart. Um, he hears it well. He says it well. He visualizes it well. And then when that ball uh snap, like I said, just make the right play for the Cardinals. the right sound quarterback decision. Might be ditching the ball, might be throwing to one, might be ripping through a progression, it might be protecting it if we get a quick beat, you know, whatever it might be. So, um, take it one play at a time and and we'll we'll, uh, grade it as such. >> That, how do you balance all of that with him going against a vanilla defense and no game planning from the other team? >> Yeah, I mean, so it like I just said, I mean, it's you're never going to put too much stock into it. You just, hey, this is the play that we gave you. this is the defense they gave you. Did our did our 10 guys do all the right stuff? Carson could be doing everything right, but two guys messed up and then it's going to look like Carson made the mistake, right? And so that's just the price of playing quarterback. So again, you just take it one play at a time and grade it as such. >> It seemed to our eyes like he had a really nice day of practice yesterday. Is that how it looked to you on tape and then where has he developed over the past two weeks here? >> Yeah, I would say uh I I thought he'd had a nice day. I mean, he had hit some explosive. I thought his accuracy is on point yesterday. I thought it was probably the best. Um, and I thought I think our second and third groups have operated at a pretty high clip thus far. Um, probably the best that they have operated in terms of just, you know, getting set and going. Um, don't want to say toned it down, you know, a ton, but but a little bit like they were mimicking the plays that we're going to run uh on that on that Thursday night so that they uh they have a good feel for it. >> Starting [snorts] defense was able to force a couple interceptions in practice yesterday. Is that a product of them making plays? Is it stuff that you see? >> Yeah, it's both. It's uh man, it's it's one of those things that uh you know that used to just bring you to your knees as an offensive coach and then you have to remind yourself like man, if we're getting some takeaways, we have short fields and now it should be easier for the offense. Got to kind of look at it both ways now. So, I'm training my brain right there. But you think about um SMB's pick right there. Um there's stuff that we could have done better on offense in terms of just, you know, the rhythm and timing right there, throwing it on the plant right out of Mike's break. Um first rep that that Jacob's ever had at that play. Uh, and that's why we're out here doing that. And it was cool cuz right after he knew it. He knew like something was off. He didn't even need to see the tape. It was just the timing aspect. I like Mike's route. And honestly, if that ball gets out there on that on the plant um like he'll do next time, that could have been a big one for us, but we're a little bit off and and SMB, you know, reaps the rewards from that and getting that pick. So, awesome right there. And then I thought, uh, Cody Simon did a great job. It was it was weird because I was right behind Jacobe. Obviously half the size of him, so I can hardly see. Uh but because I'm further back, I do have kind of a vantage point that those guys have. And the way that Cody Simon uh buzzed under our scout route right there, it looked like he started to level off at a distance where you could kind of put that ball up and over him. And right when he went like he almost he almost corrected himself. I haven't even talked to him about this where you could see he ended up getting a little bit more depth. And because we put a little bit of air on it, he was able to turn his head and the ball was right there. So, it was a great it was a great learning op u you know for for Jacobe and and the quarterbacks for that matter. Um I thought M Wilson was awesome on that one too because even if it would have gone to the underneath route and KB Mack was ready there to jump just kind of playing off a quarterback's intentions. So I thought that was just you know high quality execution from the defense. before camp, a few defensive players said like they appreciated how much you were in some of the defensive meetings and, you know, talked about different things and I guess how involved are you with a lot of the things and when you see something like that, do you go right over to them and and tell them kind of what you see? Hey, good job beating our offense and this and that. >> Yeah, I mean um absolutely. Uh you love chopping up with the defense. I mean, just cuz I I haven't been in in this seat, you know, in in LA, I loved hanging out with those guys and um you know, being in the defensive meetings in the offseason, stuff like that, and really, you know, getting to know those guys. So, um that's not really, I would say, anything new. Um you know, and uh yeah, I I I really enjoy that part of it for sure. >> We talked a little bit yesterday about Josh Swed at this point. Do you expect him to be on the field for you guys in week one? >> I do. Yes.

Uh take a shot at the end zone. Um our responsibility is to not let him in the end zone. Offense responsibility get the ball in the end zone. Uh obviously taking care of the ball in that situation is, you know, the priority. Uh but like I said, simulating those game reps as much as you could, you know, obviously without the without the contact, you know, helps helps him and me as well. >> Where's he ranking one of the quarterbacks you can chase some speed? Uh >> he's up there. He got some wiggle to him for sure. He can throw the ball at any angle, so you can get rid of it at any time he get ready to. Is there a part of you that kind of relishes that opportunity to mature speed against his and his ability to wrigle out of situations? >> 100%. Uh like I said, he's he's super agile. Um, and that's just with Kobe or without Kobe. We just had to be better. Uh, with with Kobe, uh, you know, exiting. Um, like I said, another guy got to step up. Um whether that be whoever's in the safety room, whoever backs them up, as well as on uh the all 11 on the defense. Uh the leaders got to step up and everybody got to do their part. >> Just going back to that last play against Luther that hit, did did you get any feedback out there like immediate positive or negative? >> Um no, not really. I mean, it's practice. Um I mean, I was I was going for the ball, so it was nothing malicious or anything like that. Uh so, that let me know right there he trying to score some points. How you feel, Luther? >> I'm okay. That >> hit catch you off guard a little bit, knock the wind out of you. I mean, I couldn't see like the people who hit me, so I mean, I just know it was a bang main play, so those >> How do you assess the camp that you've been having so far for over the first week? >> Um, I feel like camp's going good. How tough is that as an offense when everybody knows you need to get in the end zone. There's three seconds left and in the pass to get through your way. Is that a ball you expect to catch more often than not? >> Yes. Yes. Yes. Definitely. I expect to catch every ball. You know, whatever it looks like, however, I expect to catch everything. >> What was off? Was something a little off at the beginning of that possession in that period? You guys had I think back to back false starts. Yeah, I feel like um we had bad operation um coming in um in out the huddle um so we got to clean it up. >> You talked with uh Rome earlier last week about the competition for you guys to become that number one wide receiver. Do you look at that sort of as a as a friendly competition between you two? >> Um not really. I just, you know, come here, do my job, you know. What does that mean to you and what do you expect of yourself this season individually? >> Um, I expect to have a, you know, a good explosive year. Um, um, I feel like it's going to be fun to watch. So, >> how So, what what do you think that's going to look like? >> Um, high explosive plays, making people miss, scoring touchdowns, um, winning games, having a lot of fun out there with my teammates. Um, >> yeah. >> What What quarterbacks answered the phone the most when you needed somebody to throw to? [laughter] >> Well, Caleb was out of town, so it was um Case was here for most of the time, then Ty came at the end of the week. [snorts] So, >> where can you give us some insight into where you're at as far as just mastering the playbook. Like how far you've come from a year ago in that? >> Um I feel like I'm way more confident. Um I'm able to play more faster than I was cuz last year I was just I was getting I got out there late, you know, cuz I missed the spring so I was already behind. So um you know, being able to attack the spring and um it translate to camp. So um yeah, just being more confident um being able to play fast. Where are you at on it now? >> Um, I feel highly um good about, you know, the playbook and um where I need to be, how I need to get there, you know, stuff like that. And uh I'm good. >> So, expanding off that, how do how do you describe the sort of increased trust that you and Caleb have built over the last four months or so? >> Um I feel like, you know, you just got to go out there and practice and make plays. Um be in the right spot, know what you got to do, know how to do it, you know, the detailed up, you know, stuff like that. um you know that that'll uh earn your trust. Earn his trust. >> How much more polisher do you feel now compared to what >> um I feel confident? No, I mean I always felt confident, you know, any route. Um I would just say it was the opportunities I was given. >> Luther, what are some of the things you're learning from Khalif? >> Man, Khif's like he's amazing. Um he's really like a coach out there. Like he's so >> [snorts] >> like he he he's a great guy on and off the field. Like you can learn from him. Like just his release package is freaking sick. Like he's a great guy, man. Like he's out the roof, man. Khalif is a great leader for the team. Um he's the guy, man. >> What do you appreciate about the way he attacks practices, >> man? I I don't know. But he just it's like just watching [clears throat] film on him just like everything just look the same. Like you don't know what he doing. You don't know if he's snapping up, breaking out, breaking in cuz he's just running at you so fast and he's so little. So it's like like you got to do something. So but it's fun to watch um Lee go out there make plays and um I'm happy he's a part of the team. >> What have you seen from Tyreek uh when he's been guarding you here the last week or so? >> Um he's been you know challenging us. um you know um making plays out there. He had a a great interception today probably for six. Um it was great to see uh see that out of him and um you know I'm expecting a big year out of the whole defense. So >> going back to the play of the goal line, are you are you in general not expected expecting to get hit like that in training camp or is that >> No, not typical cuz I mean you know like but it's football man. So >> but you you feel that's inbounds like And then well just part of it or is that like how maybe a little over the top? >> I don't know. I haven't watched the film on it like I I haven't seen it but I heard it was multiple dudes around me who hit me. So >> Luther, those goals that you set out for yourself, what do you want to prove this season? What's your internal drive to to go out and showcase that and what the type of player you believe you can be? >> Um can I say that again? [clears throat] >> The goals you have for yourself this season, what you're hoping to prove out there. What's your internal drive to to to become that player and everything you envision for yourself? >> Uh I'm just trying to prove to myself I'm the best. Um cuz we can attack you different ways. Yeah, I just say it was more of a gradual just, you know, getting out there, getting more opportunities. Um, being able to, you know, showcase what I got, what I can bring to the team, what I can help the team, and, you know, show my skill set, what I can do. title: Dennis Allen says adversity brings great opportunity | Press Conference
text: What are the first steps in sort of, preparing to be without Kobe Bryant for >> Yeah, hey, listen. Um you know, obviously it sucks to lose a guy like that um for any any particular time. Um and he's [clears throat] a big part of, you know, what we um have planned to do and will still be a big part of what we have planned to do. Um but in all adversity comes also opportunity and so it'll be another opportunity for some other guys to step up, whether it be somebody in the safety room to step up and take on that role or some of our other guys in the room to step up and become the play makers and the leaders for the defense. And so um you know, I mean it just it's part of it's part of football, it's part of what you deal with and and you move on, you know, so um hopefully he'll be on the quicker end and we'll get him back sooner rather than later. >> A year ago, a year ago Jaylen got hurt before camp even started. [clears throat] And yesterday it's an hour into your first padded practice and you lose a guy. How much of your job is problem solving? And at this time of year having a little extra time before the season start, think there's a benefit to that? >> I mean I I think that's I think that's all of our jobs. I think that's the the coach's job. I think that's the player's job. I mean, you know, nothing nothing ever goes exactly how you plan, right? You have to be able to adjust. You have to be able to uh you know change course when needed to. Um and so it's just part of what we do and and you know, this is just one of those things we'll have to deal with. >> Dennis, how does this change >> Cam Lewis's reps? I know he was playing some nickel in place of Kyler. >> Yeah, I think he'll focus a little bit more on the safety position now. Yeah. >> How does this change what you asked the trajectory of Dylan and what you're going to ask of him? >> Yeah, I I don't think I I think that's going to change a whole lot, you know, um I think our expectations for him, you know, as a rookie is that each and every day he learns a little bit more and he gets a little bit better. Um you know, there's a lot to learn um in the National Football League. It you know, there's a lot going on. The volume of what we do is more than what most rookies have ever done before. The volume of what they're seeing from our offense is going to be more than what they're used to seeing, you know, so I don't think I don't think any we put any higher expectations uh on him. I think our focus is, man, you just be you. You do what you do. You continue to come in every day and work the way that you work uh and he'll continue to get better. >> Has he exceeded [clears throat] your expectations? >> Say that again. >> exceeded your expectations? >> Well, listen, I mean, we're we're one padded practice into into training camp, so it's really hard to say. I mean, you know, he's done a nice job um and and and yet there's every day there's things that you see that you're like, "Okay, he needs to learn from that experience." Uh and he will. >> What attributes can uh Cam Lewis bring to the safety position? >> I think he's just he's he's smart. I you know, I I don't really like to get into the comparison game and yet I I think of a guy that we had in New Orleans in P.J. Williams, you know, who was really a versatile type player. We drafted him in the third round to play corner. He played outside corner. He played in the slot in the nickel. He played at safety. So, guys that, you know, are smart and instinctive that can play multiple roles are really valuable um you know, within the team. So, I think, you know, he's played safety. He's played a dime linebacker. He's lined up at the nickel position. He's He's He's lined up outside before, so um I just think his his his experience and his versatility I think is uh you know, something that this is why we have a guy like this. Is so that if you have injuries in certain spots, we have guys that we can plug in that aren't just one-spot players. They can play multiple positions. >> What what >> [clears throat] >> What can you guys uh get out of Cal Moore there in the middle? >> Um yeah, I mean, I think it still remains to be seen a little bit in terms of exactly what we can get. I think all of those guys inside um have really been taken to uh the coaching and been taken to the the emphasis on how we're going to play in there, the fundamentals and technique that we're going to use. Um he's a big, powerful guy. He's got a little bit more suddenness and quickness maybe than what I originally anticipated. So, I I I think we've got I think we've got a good group of defensive tackles that um I don't know that anybody has separated themselves. Again, we're only one day into padded practices. Um uh but I think there's going to be a lot of competition in that group. >> With Cam focusing more on safety now, how does this impact your short-term contingency planning at nickel? well, we'll we'll see uh a lot more of uh Jaylen Jones, uh Josh Blackwell, Malik Muhammad. We'll see a lot more of those guys inside, you know, in the slot. >> What do you want to see from Malik when he gets to to take some reps in there? I mean, I want to see him go out and and perform. I want to go out and see him compete. I want to see him play physical in the run game. I want to see him be sticky in coverage, you know, like um I just want to you know, everybody What do you want to see out of this guy? What do you want to see out of this guy? What do you want I want out of this guy? You know what I going to see? I want to see 11 freaking dudes on the field competing their ass off. And if we all do that, you know, then I feel pretty confident that we'll get them to the right spot. Um but that's what this time of year is all about. This is about, man, developing the culture and the way that you're going to play. Um and that's That's what I want to see out of all of them. I want to see it out of the freaking 10-year vet. I want to see it out of the rookie. >> What is the biggest challenge of the coaching point on for guys who haven't played nickel? I mean, you mentioned Blackwell, Jones, they don't have a lot of snaps at that position last year. And Muhammad, too. What is there one coaching point you focus in on if somebody is playing a brand new position who might have to start for a while? >> Uh I don't know that there's one coaching point, you know, in particular. I think the thing that you have to understand inside at the nickel, um things happen faster. So, your reaction time has to be better. So, if I said, "Okay, what's the What's the biggest thing?" All right, the biggest thing is anticipation and eyes. All right? If you put your eyes in the right spot, you'll have a chance to be right. Um if you're looking at the wrong thing, it's hard to be successful. So, I think just what they see inside at the nickel, I think is a uh a big deal. >> What is Ky- How is Kyeler Gordon progressing? >> Um look, he's he's working his tail off. Um he's doing everything that we've asked him to do. Um I think we got a good plan for him. Um and then, you know, we'll just see where it goes. >> What does Braeden Braeden Bliss bring the speed that you wanted to bring in here? He doesn't have the height or the length that you had at that position last year. How does that >> alter how you call the defense and how you attack offenses? >> Yeah, I don't think that's going to alter that, um you know, a whole lot. I mean, obviously, you know, size, length, those are things that we uh that we value. Um and and yet, you know, speed and athleticism uh is something that we value also. So, I don't know that that really changes, you know, what we do as, you know, far as calling the defense. Um I do think that that that he's going to bring some coverage versatility that that, you know, I'm excited about. >> How have you looked at balancing getting guys ready and then when you have an injury like you had yesterday, like trying to balance like I don't want guys to get hurt, but I also have have them ready for week one. >> Uh you know, really honestly, I I I don't know that we That didn't sound right. I mean, we we pay attention to that and yet there's a way that you have to practice the game of football to get yourself ready to play the game of football. You know, I think you're just as likely to have injuries if you don't push yourself and get your body acclimated to and develop some calluses to the the speed and the physicality of the game. I think you have to practice that way. Um and yet there is a delicate balance. So, you know, you you you have like today we're going to have, you know, some some live stuff going on today. Um a lot of team periods. Um what we do the next day may change based on how everything goes today, you know, so um I think you just got to try to keep a balance of that as best you can. >> Hey French question for you. Hall of Fame weekend this weekend. The six years you spent around Drew, what what ways did he impact you, leave an impression on you? >> Oh, man. Um I think I think this. I think, you know, when you think about, you know, a Hall of Fame player and what makes those guys special um it's usually not the physical attributes. Um a lot of it is and most of it is the competitiveness and the work ethic. Um and just to have the opportunity to By the way, I think it was more like 10 years that I was around Drew Brees, but just the opportunity to watch him and how meticulous he was in his preparation. and how every day he went out to practice and competed and he wanted to win everything and you know watching a guy um play the game the way that he played the game and you watch him after every throw that he made okay, he went through the rest of his progression. Not once not a few times during practice every time during practice. And if they had a play that he didn't like [snorts] the outcome, he didn't like the timing uh or where or the placement of the ball or whatever the case may be all right, the moment we had the next break he had whoever that receiver was and he was working that play again. And so to me that's what makes Hall of Famer special is they're willing to do things that not everybody else is willing to do. Um and a lot of the lot of my success in coaching and and being where I'm at today um you know, is attributed to the success that we had in New Orleans and he was a huge part of that. >> Dennis, are you are you going to be able to attend any of those festivities this weekend and if so, what will that just mean to you to be there? >> Yeah, I am. Um uh I'll be there. I'm going to leave out of here. We have a day off on Friday. I'm going to leave out of here on Friday night. I'll be there Saturday, so I'll miss Saturday's practice. Um and then we'll be back in time for uh Sunday morning Sunday morning practice. Um I think you know, I'm humbled that you know, he thought enough of me to invite me to to attend the Hall of Fame uh ceremony. Um you know, it's it's not often that you get a chance to be you know, around Hall of Fame players um offensively, defensively, whatever the case may be. And so um I think it's a real honor and a real privilege that you know he asked me to be a part of it. >> Eli Eli's been able to step in Eli's a hit and run. He's been able to step in since he's been here whenever he's been called upon. What's the expectation for him getting back and how will he factor in once he comes back if he's back before >> Well, I before we get into where does he factor in all those things, I think we just got to get him healthy and get him back out on the field and then we'll let him get out there and go compete and you know, see uh see where he's at. >> With uh Cinnamond knowing how important the communication aspect is for that safety position, how much falls typically on a rookie versus the vet that you likely have next to him? well, I'd say a lot. Um you know, I I think obviously when you play the safety position and a lot of the things that we do you know, there's communication that's happening on one side of the field that may be different than the communication that's happening on the other side of the field. So the a lot of that safety communication is independent of each other. Um and yet having a veteran back there that's a little bit of a calming influence, I think is is um is usually beneficial, but um you know it's not always the case. >> Coach um lastly, you're obviously focused on the defense. You have such a good feel for what other the opposing offense is doing. How much further ahead does it feel like the offense you're facing with Caleb? >> Uh well, I I think it's night and day from where we were at this point a year ago. Um you know, I I think and and that's the thing that's you know, it's it's challenging for us and at times can be frustrating for us and yet we also know that, you know, this is a a team game and so, um you know, if our offense is operating at a very high level, um then that's going to allow for us to be a little bit more successful on defense and and it's a huge challenge for us every single day. The things that we see, the speed that we're seeing, you know, with the skill position, um you know, the challenging things schematically that we're seeing, I think all of this, uh um you know, helps us get ready for the regular season. >> To that point, what is particularly challenging about Auburn's running game, particularly from 13? >> Well, I think today we'll get our first real look at what 13's going to look like, um but uh I I think he does a good job of trying to create uh the formations and the angles and the blocking scheme to try to gain advantage on the defense. Um and I think they do a good job of mixing in zone schemes with gap schemes um and then their ability to give you the same look and then have play-action pass off of it. You know, I think it's uh yeah, I think he does a good job.

title: Atlanta Falcons players and coaches speak following practice at AT&T Training Camp
text: Uh Brian, first what's it what's it been like these first few days of practice getting to know all your teammates, getting to know this running back? >> Oh, it's been great. You know, um you know, I always love, you know, just combining our group back together and just coming out here and grinding and getting back to work. So, um you know, the last couple days been pretty fun for me. >> What's it been like to work with Michael Petri? >> It's been great. You know, he's very, you know, high energetic guy. You know, he's been great for us. Um he's a great teacher. >> You know, I love just being able to ask him questions. So he's, you know, open to just continue to teach us. >> I'm a I'm I'm a great learner. You know, I love to learn, you know, so I got questions all day long and he don't have a problem with just making sure that he's continually like, you know, answering the questions that I have. So I appreciate Peter. >> He did say you're a student of the game. What can this change of scenery do for you in your career? Uh, I think it can really elevate me and um, my game, you know, not only with, you know, just coming being so close to home, but, you know, being around guys like Petri and B, you know, um, you know, I think they they really help keep me motivated and actually motivate me more than I was when I got here. So, um, you know, I think it's just going to um, help me elevate. >> Okay, you talked about Bejan. What's it like being around him? >> Uh, great guy, you know, um, even better guy, you know, than he is a no football player. So, um, you know, I appreciate, you know, how he comes to work every day and know uh know our plan to compliment each other and, um, you know, he's he want to win, you know, and I love being around winners. >> How do you think you can compliment Bejon in this offense? >> Uh, just not not letting anything fall off, you know, from the time he comes out of the game, you know, no, there's no fall off, you know, when I when I step on the field, u same standard, you know, I expect to make the same amount of plays, you know, you know, be just as explo as as explosive. >> Yeah. So, you know, I don't really have expect to have any type of fall off. You know, whenever he comes out the game, you know, same standard. >> What have you learned about him? Was it nice to have him out on the field today? >> Yeah, it was definitely nice to have him, you know, uh for a little while that we did have him, you know, with his son cooking like the way it is, you know, so definitely a blessing to have him back. Um, you know, always good to have, you know, all of our guys out on the field and, you know, you know, putting in the work and competing because, you know, at the end of the day, we got to win or lose together. So, um, you know, it's good having him back out there working. I know what happened with Jaylen. It's part of it, but how uh bad a note was that to end the day? >> Um, you know, obviously it's very unfortunate. We don't want to end a day like that. Um, but at the end, you know, this part of the game, you know, this football, it happens. And, um, you know, if it's 10 minutes left in the fourth quarter, we got to go win a football game. You know, we going we going to keep him in our prayers and, you know, um, you know, show him the love that we, you know, he deserves, but we got to, you [clears throat] know, be professionals and stay locked in on the task at hand. and we got to go win a football game right now. >> You have a long history with Tua. >> What's it like being back with him on a team? >> No, it's been great. You know, just re reuniting with one of my um really close um college friends and um you know, we we were really good boys back in school, so you know, be able to meet back up at this level, you know, it's been fun. It's been exciting. We locker mates as well, so um you know, we we extremely familiar with each other, so it's like it's it's been just like home for real. >> What do you feel like is underrated about the way that he approaches the quarterback position? Uh what's underrated about it is um he's actually very very studious. He's smart and he he he understands the game very well, you know. So um not only is he's a phenomenal, you know, person, phenomenal athlete, you know, he uh he puts time into his craft and um he wants to get better. >> What's it been like interacting with coach Defansky, learning this offense under Tommy Reese as well? >> Uh it's been great. You know, it's been interesting. you know, uh, you know, they've been doing a great job of just, you know, you know, coaching us up on all the details cuz at the end of the day, it really doesn't matter about the plays. You got to hone in on the details that that it takes to make the plays work. So, um, I appreciate, you know, how, you know, they've been coaching us, you know, so far. >> What was it like being around Van while he was kind of holding in? The game was insane obviously, but that was really one of your last memories in that building, >> right? Uh one of those that moment was one of the greatest moments of my life. And he comes back and he no looks him and left arm throws a touchdown to win a game. So, I would never I would never forget that ever in my life. So, how's it been going for you out there in Mason? >> Um, you know, it's been fun, man. Just getting somewhere new and just kind of getting a fresh start. Um, being around one of my best friends and the teammate, Harold Perkins. Um, it's been fun, man. Um, and yeah, it's been a great it's been a great transition and, you know, I've been having a great time. >> What did you see during the play where uh, Jaylen went down? You know, I've had to endure, you know, my own um knee, whatever his knee, calf, whatever. Um, I've I've had to endure those type of injuries before, man. And you don't wish that on nobody. So, uh, you know, not knowing what happened, uh, you know, just prayers up to and sending him positivity. >> You obviously haven't been around Jaylen too too long, but you know enough about him. What What is he like as a player and a person in your opinion? Um, he a great dude. I actually just went to his house not too long ago. Um, probably like two days ago on an off day just to hang out with him, chill with him. Uh, you know, I'm a little older than him, which is not all, you know, it's not very much that I'm older than somebody. So, you know, when I could try to give him some knowledge or some game I always do, but that's like my brother. Um, you know, just being here. Um, after OTAAS, you know, I thanked all the guys about just taking me in and, you know, welcomed me with open arms. Um, and he was one of the guys that, you know, just kind of made the transition easier. Uh, and I I you're right. I I haven't known Jaylen for a long time, but I've always knew of him, you know, in his football industry, you kind of know um even going through high school and stuff like that, you kind of know guys um you know, different guys through the recruiting trail and everything coming through high school. So, but he's a great dude, man. Great dude. Even better person. Um great player. Um and yeah, >> what do you enjoy about the vision that this staff has for the defense this year? >> Um I just I just like playing hard-nosed football, man. just being able to get off the ball and, you know, let the guys up front make plays with, you know, their abilities and what they do best. Um, and just letting everybody else just kind of just cover and, you know, how Brick says it, just be just be the hammer, not the nail. And, you know, uh, take the fight to people and not let the people take the fight to us. Um, and just attack and play physical, play fast. Um, and not too much thinking. You know, my coach always say, if you think, you stink. [laughter] You played with Harold in 22 and 23. Is that correct? >> Um, one, what do you remember about playing with him? And two, what do you think he can prove out here this year as a rookie? >> Um, you know, I think he has everything to prove. Um, you know, being picked in the sixth round, uh, knowing what type of caliber player he is, um, you know, I don't think nobody ever expected that. And, uh, I don't think he really got to prove nothing to nobody but himself. You know, I feel like it's a battle within itself. Um, and, you know, I think he going to do great this year, man. I think he going to prove a lot of people right. Um cuz I don't think nobody doubting him in a sense. But you know, everybody going to always have something to say. But I mean, if he keep his head down, it'll be good for him to show. >> When you left in 23, he he was viewed as a really elite guy at the time. I mean, how how similar is he now? Does he still look kind of he was then? >> I mean, he he been the same exact guy, you know, since the beginning, since I met him. Um it ain't, >> you know, football is football, man. So, I mean, what he did back then, he can still do now is just where he where he was at on the football field of something else. But, you know, he going to do I I have all hopes in the world and all the praise in the world and I have I'm excited to see what he does this year for sure. >> This has been kind of a >> What kind of goals and roles uh do you envision for yourself entering camp? >> Uh, man, really, I wouldn't even say I had any real goals, man. I'm just trying to progress and get better each and every day. Um, I know if I maximize my ability and um the sky's is the limit. So, I'm just trying to get better each and every day, man, and put on for the organization, put on for myself, put on for my family. >> Change of scenery, I'm sure, has been a little bit of a breath of fresh air for you. How you talked about the transition being smooth and everything like that, but just the fact that you get a different opportunity with a new team. How refreshing has that been? >> Um, it's been very refreshing. Um, you know, my first interview when I got here, I I just said, you know, it's good to be to not feel tolerated, but to be feel celebrated. Um, and you know, coming from LSU, coming into the league, um, you know, just coming through coming up through high school and everything like that, I've never really been one to, um, you know, not have people on my side or, you know, deal with something, you know, that I not necessarily could control. Um, so coming here, you know, it's just kind of a comfortability thing like, you know, like I said, um, they believe in me. Um, so it's easier to do your job when you know that somebody believes in you, somebody has your best interest at heart. Um, so I mean it's been, like I said, the transition's been going good and you know, I can't wait for the season. >> You got a chip on your shoulder a little bit? >> I definitely do. Um, you know, last year wasn't definitely not my best ball. Um, for a lot of reasons. Not to name not one of them, but you know, just, you know, I'm just getting back into it. I'm ready. I'm ready to go. Uh, this off season put the most work in I ever have in my life. Um, you know, never I never really since I've been in the league, I never really had a plan in the offseason, but you know, talking to my former vets and everything like that, I kind of put together a plan. kind of stuck to the plan and uh it's been going good. So, I'm excited. >> How how comfortable are you? How does that feel, I guess, for you early on? >> I feel I feel the same every day. I'm just taking it day by day on trying to build trust with my teammate and my coaches. >> I think Devon mentioned yesterday that you're just way ahead of where he thought you'd be now. I mean, do you feel like you're ahead of kind of the scheme, the playbook? Do you feel like you're kind of on top of it all? >> I'm just my feet at every day, bro. I'm just trying to do good for myself and my teammates and my coaches. I'm just trying to work as hard as I could to get them to trust me. Do >> you have an idea of what your role might end up kind of ultimately >> picking I believe it's going to be on ball be off ball. Like where do you think you'll kind of play a lot this >> We got to wait. We going to see. >> We going to see. >> Can you describe kind of the end of of that practice and and what the feeling was like as everyone kind of saw Jaylen Walker there? >> Um to be honest, I didn't really see uh the whole situation. and um it was kind of in the moment in the play, but um my prayers and my thoughts go out to him. I hope he good. >> What have you enjoyed about working with this defense so far? >> Everybody hardworking. Uh we all want to be great, not just as a defense, but as a team, as a coaching staff, and um every day we building our future, creating our future. So, that's what we doing. >> You've been getting to know Brick a little bit. What is it like to learn from someone like that who has such a clear vision for what this defense wants to accomplish? Uh, strong strong person, strong mentally. Um, and I'm just learning every day, every every day from from and about him. >> Kendall said you're helping him catch him up after he missed a lot of OTAAS. What's your relationship like with him? >> Uh, KD, that's my dog. >> And uh, I be helping him, but he be helping me too. We be helping each other. Don't let him don't let him g me up like that. [laughter] What's your what's been your biggest adjustment to I know you haven't really played in the game yet to the NFL versus what you did in college. >> One thing >> I don't really feel like it's no big adjustment. I've been doing this my whole life. I've been balling my whole life. So I don't really feel like it's a big adjustment. Um it's just football to me. >> Coach Rude said you're a little bit more polished as a pass rusher than a lot of the rookies he gets. I'm assuming that's because that's kind of your background from LSU, right? I mean, you you know, that's sort of your that was your home to begin with. >> I got to thank God for that. I ain't going to lie. That's just something that God gave me. I'm just natural with it. I can't even explain it. Um it's something I could just do. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. God giving. >> What do you want to prove to everyone in this training camp? >> I don't want to prove nothing. I'm proving everything to myself. I don't got nothing to prove to nobody. I know I know [snorts] what I could do. So, I'm just really proving everything to myself. >> And what can you do? whatever I put my mind to. >> You got some outside linebacker snaps in you still? I mean, is that is that still, you know, enough of your nature? You feel like you could scoot out there if you need? >> Oh, most definitely. If need be. Yeah, most definitely. >> Yeah. No, I think it's huge for uh the Falcons, you know, being able to have all our guys out there um and be able to continue putting this thing together as an offense and as a football team is huge. >> Are you excited to kind of not have to think about it and talk about it and now that it's done? Yeah, I think it's there's peace that comes with that, right? Because it's just something else that can be a distraction. So now our focus can just be on, okay, hey, let's get better today. Focus on what the install is and how we can improve watching the film. >> You've met Coach Bejon for a couple years now. What part of his game do you feel like has evolved the most? >> Um, it's a great question. I think, um, obviously all aspects of his game has evolved, but I think like him and I talked about when we drafted him, there was going to be a point where the game slowed down for him. And I think the fact that the game slowed down, obviously he's a natural runner with the ball in his hands, but I think as a in the pass game, specifically pass protection, um he he does that at a really high level. Takes a lot of pride in it and ultimately that protects the quarterback, which gives us a better opportunity to win. So I think that part of his game has evolved the most. >> Cool stuff. Coach, how is his uh acclamation program? How will that look like here over the next week as y'all ramp him back up into things? >> Yeah. Uh Jake and Griffin, those guys, they have a great plan put in place for him and they'll let me know what we can do and what we can't do. And so I'll just follow the rules and follow the protocol and when we can use them, he'll be out there and when we can't, he'll be getting his work in. >> Was that the least contentious hold in ever? Just [laughter] out there every day smiling, you know, cheering up his teammates, encouraging people. >> It's my only hold in I've ever been a part of. So I guess to answer your question, yes. [laughter] >> Was he aggravating to you? He looked like he was about to come out of his skin attached to your hip. you want to tell him to go away at? >> No, I think you know the biggest thing is just he's a guy that loves football. He loves football. He loves his teammates and I think the biggest thing is the fact that he's back out there with his teammates. Um the energy, the enthusiasm that he brings um is infectious. And so ultimately again that just helps us continue to be a better football team. >> We know that Bejian is a great leader and he's evolving in that aspect as well. But what's he like in a meeting room? >> Very intentional. Um, you know, he again his his football mind is is better than most people understand. And so there's very in-depth conversations about pass protection, the run game, kind of what he sees as a runner, what I see as a coach, and then we just put that all together um in order to put him and put us in the best position as a football team. >> Talk about the importance of him and and him being back on the field as you look to settle in a new person at quarterback position. Yeah, I think the biggest thing is just being able to have um the 11 guys out there continuing to play and get in uh in sync with each other, right? And so be it V-Rod, TG, Bjan, whoever's out there, we need to be able to have those guys out there, be able to play at full speed and be able to play and be on the same page in order to give ourselves the best chance to be the offense we want to be. >> Talk about B Rob really quickly because we haven't asked you a ton about him. What's his presence been like and what has he been doing so far in camp that you're impressed with? >> He's a big human. He he really is. You don't understand how big he is until you see him. Puts those pads on. Um and he he's another one, man. Just a student of the game, great teammate, uh brings great enthusiasm every day, loves to compete. Um but at the same time loves being coached and wants to be coached hard. And so as a coach, you love that. And I think that's really the entire room. You know, it's a good bunch of guys that work really, really well together. And I think obviously having um Ryan and Bjon out there, it's been really really good getting them out there together because I think because they're naturally competitors, they're going to bring the best out of each other. >> What kind of role do you see for B- Rob going forward? >> I think it's too early to talk about roles. I think the most important thing is he's going to have a role to help this football team win. You know, I think as we this thing keeps evolving and coming together, all those things will figure itself out. But I've been very very happy and impressed with how he's learning the playbook. um his urgency to get better every single day and then most importantly the leadership role that he's kind of embraced um being in the room. >> How good of a compliment is he for for just physically and and their styles of build? >> I think he has a chance to be a really good uh complimentary piece, but again I think it's hard to say until we actually get out there and we're playing real football with pads on and some of those things. So right now I think it looks really good in you know t-shirts and shorts and those things cuz that's the only time we've seen those two together. But I think once we get in there and we see, you know, see these guys playing pads together, um I think we'll see a lot more of his physical [music] presence of, you know, being a 6'2, 230 lb one man. >> Uh yeah, Coach Goodson, how's he coming along? Uh trying to get looked really good on the screen out there in shorts today. >> Yeah. No, TG looks good. Again, he's another one that's come in um veteran, fifth year in the league, so he's got the right mindset, extremely competitive guy, and um takes a lot of pride in his in his craft. And so we've been very very happy with him and everything that he's done up to this point. >> How's Cash been? Thank you. >> Cash has been good. Yeah, Cash has been good. He's getting better every single day. And I think the biggest thing for any rookie is just continuing to get comfortable with um just being continuing to get comfortable with um the speed of the NFL game, right? Yeah. Georgia is high level football, but being in the NFL is a completely different thing. And so I think the more reps he gets, the more comfortable he'll continue to get. But I've been very happy with how he's learned everything up to this point. >> With Bjan, if you could, obviously he was an elite prospect, top 10 draft pick. You knew he'd be good. When he got here, how early on do you think you could tell that he was really unique and just how good he is? >> Yeah, [snorts] that's a loaded question. Um, I think when you take someone number eight, you're you have pretty good idea that you think they're going to be really good. um how good they're going to be I think is up to how much work they're willing to put in right to maximize the abilities that he's been given and when you look at Bjon he's a guy that works endlessly to maximize the talents and gifts that he's been given and so I think up to this point he's done everything that he's he's done everything he could do to get himself into this position but I also think there's a lot of room for him to continue to grow and so that's where our focus goes on now that he's back out here is like how can we continue to get better. How do we get better with our ball security, some run game things and those things? >> One more question right here. >> Who's your favorite daughter? >> I wouldn't say I have a favorite. I think uh my oldest is my favorite oldest and my youngest is my favorite youngest would be. Yeah. >> Thank you, [laughter] >> coach. I mean, highest paid running back in NFL history. Is it warranted? And two, how do you think he can handle the pressure of that label? >> Yeah. Um, I think that question is really it's one person's opinion, right? Like the fact is, yeah, okay, they say he's the highest paid running back ever. That's awesome for him. It's awesome for the Falcons cuz that means we have him for three more years, right? But is it warranted, not warranted? That's one person's opinion. I think the most important thing is like how do we maximize the things he can do to help the Falcons win? Because one person may say it's not, one person may say it is. Again, everyone has an opinion and you respect everyone's opinion. And I think the focus has to be on how do we maximize the things that he can do to help our football team win and then how does he help the other guys around him get better and elevate the guys around him. >> How much has his mind matured from 23 to now? Like is he asking harder questions? Like is has he reached a higher level questions that he's asking? Do you how much has he grown in that aspect do you think? >> Yeah. No, I think for anybody comes in, right, rookie year, second year, third year, now going in his fourth year, there's been constant evolution, right, and learning because he's learning what the NFL game is, right? He's first time he sees something is no longer the first time he sees it anymore, right? And so, like we talked about earlier, the game is continuing to slow down for him. So, he's able to anticipate certain things happening now within the run game and pass game because he's seen some of these things. And so yeah, I would say he asked a lot more, you know, we call like instead of 100 level questions, it's two or 300 level questions now because he's now a two or three 400 level player because of the amount of reps that he's had in this league up to this point. >> How does he elevate as a player? I mean, he led the league in scrimmage yards last year, I believe. Obviously now he's highly paid, extremely well compensated, welld deserved. I mean, how does he level up? Um, I think if you were to ask him, he'd say there's a lot of things he's got to get better at. And I would say the same, right? I think, um, when we watch the film, we don't spend too much time worrying about the good things. We'll watch, okay, what allowed this play to be good, but any runner is going to tell you a good run play happened because of the other 10 guys on the field that allowed that play to happen. And so for us as we watch it as runners, um we're looking at what are the plays that we didn't make and how do we make those plays because to me and to him those are missed opportunities for explosive plays or for plays that help our football team win. And so that was that would be the biggest thing is I would say how do we continue to be more efficient in the run game to allow ourselves not to miss some of those plays that are there. >> Last one I got for you. Um obviously been wide zone heavy here for a while. Maybe a little bit more gap concepts now. I mean how how much does that change how you have to coach or explain things? things like are you explaining more this year do you think in that regard? >> That's a good question. I'll say we're going to run the football. [laughter] We're going to run the football.

title: Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa on growth through first week of AT&T Training Camp | Press Conference
text: Healthwise, how are you? Healthwise, sorry. >> Doing well. Doing well. Yeah, it's not like this is a longevity thing. Um, you know, I'm just happy to be out there with the guys, take more team reps. I think it's the progress has been really good and hopefully by tomorrow we'll be able to be a full go. Mhm. >> How'd that feel just kind of getting more reps? It felt like this was by far the most action you had with the heat and everything like that. >> Yeah, I mean it it feels good. Like I said, feels good to be out there. Um, you know, you you sort of want to go through, you want to be able to go through more of the practices just so you could get into a flow. Um, you know, with the guys, with how practice is going, get a better feel of the rush, with the defense, things like that. >> How good it feel to see Bean back out there today? >> Oh, that felt good. That felt good. That was really good to see uh be be back out there. I remember last year before you guys played Atlanta, I think Rick mentioned that when you're on time and in in rhythm, you're extremely good. How how close do you feel like you are to being at a point here where you're in rhythm on time with everybody? >> I think that just takes reps. Reps with the guys, reps being able to to go out there in the team periods, feel the rush, as I said, uh maneuver through the pocket and and kind of find the guys. >> You feel like it it hurts to not be out there now? like obviously you got a lot of time still, but is it a hindrance at all? >> I wouldn't say it's a hindrance. You're able to take mental reps. You're able to see how guys are running their routes. Um, and then you can kind of gauge the timing off of that. >> Yeah. Following up on that, what are you doing now when you're not able to get out there at full at full go? How are you spending your your days out there? >> Yeah, just take mental reps. Um, can't go out there and and and do it. So, just visually seeing yourself in there in the play. what my drops would be, uh, what the read is, what things like that look like. >> So, how do you get through the tough moments as you went through last season that put you into a position now kind of a new start? How have you mentally gone from that spot to where you are now? >> I think for me, it's the word. It's it's it's the Bible. Being able to get into my Bible, being able to uh draw myself closer to God within prayer um helps center me. And I would say outside of being able to feel centered, um, it also gives me a lot of perspective on life, on what's important in life. Um, and football is just what we do. It's not who we are. >> What's your comfort level within this offense as they're asking you to go under center movement? I mean, you've got a lot of time in your career, but what's the comfort level so far within this offense? >> Yeah, pretty comfortable. Um, I wouldn't say there's anything that we do that I've never done uh playing um in Miami. So, pretty comfortable. >> To your old teammate at Alabama, Bro now teammate again here with the Falcons. Just talked about how much of a student of the game you are. How has that evolved throughout your career? Clearly, you've done this for a long time, but how have you changed the way that you approach these mental reps that you're talking about? >> Yeah, I would say as a rookie, it would be harder. Um, early on in my career, I was more of a I have to do it. Um, sort of go out by myself, walk through them. Um, but as I've, you know, been able to play a good amount of years and and play a good amount of games and whatnot throughout those years, um, you can kind of, I guess, encompass the closing my eyes, the imagery of of what what things look like. So, emotion timing, um, what we would want the protection to be if we're in certain looks, and then, as I said, watching the receivers, the timing, if I'm taking a three-step drop, a fivestep drop of what that route would look like and when I would need to get the ball out for them. >> Speaking of Bjun Robinson as a teammate, you haven't been teammate with with him very long, but you've been around him. What is he like as a teammate, and how much of a joy is he to be around? He's a he's an amazing person. Um I would say he is very rooted, very grounded in his faith and I would say he's he's a very humble person. >> So how much has uh so many guys who are helping you in the position have played the position? How big a help is that to have those guys around you every single day around you that know what it's like to be on your spot? >> Yeah, it it's it's a big help. Um you got Al who's played in the league for about 13 years maybe. um you know back in back in his time and then you know you got Tommy who's played quarterback as well at Notre Dame um and you got Matt um you know Matt Ryan comes into our meeting rooms as well uh whether it's to help give us you know what whatever it is for whatever that play looked like or whatever. Um, you know, it it's really helpful uh because it's hard when when you're being coached when someone hasn't played that position um and they're telling you things to do when you know it's not as easy as saying it. Uh so it it it does help because they understand. >> So you know as a veteran injuries are part of this game. How would you describe practice today? >> How would you describe the end of practice today? >> You said sorry I couldn't hear the first part. as a veteran, you know, injuries are part of the a part of the game. Just how could you describe the end of >> Yeah, the end of practice definitely not what you want to see. Uh, but as a football team, the guys that that play football and have been playing football from from a young age, we understand that injuries come with the game. Um, but at the end of the day, I'm no doctor. Um, I'm no medical guy, so I I can't say what's what's going on or or or what's not what what's not going on. Um, so from there, you know, I I would say all we can do is is just pray for for Jay and, you know, just just with our fingers crossed, hope that he's going to be okay and he can play with us this season. >> With your recovery over the last week, how would you say that you've kind of dealt with it? Have you been kind of anxious, antsy to get out there or have you been a little bit more calmer because you've kind of you know what this process is? >> Yeah, I would say I've been I I've been more antsy to get out there. Uh just to be able to play football again with the guys. Um struggle with the guys through the heat. Um being able to hear the the play call. Just just all of that. >> Anything else? >> All right. >> Thank you. >> All right. Thanks, guys. >> Thank you. time. >> I'll try the Hawaiian thing for you this weekend. >> Yeah.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | August 04, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: Go, guys. >> Okay. Uh, good day out there today. Um, we're in shells. Can't be in pads back to back just yet per the rules. So, we'll be in shells there today. title: Haynes King: 'Making the most of my opportunity' | Carolina Panthers
text: Hey, Haynes. Um, team Reed's had a lot of success catching the ball from you and Kenny. What have you seen from him and why has he been so successful this summer? >> One of the reasons, I mean, he's he's just a consistent guy. Just the small little details of of what they know that, you know, I I don't know yet or I haven't been through yet. >> You talked to us back in the spring about how despite the mobility in that part of your game, you wanted to be here as a quarterback. How do you feel like you progressed and what part of your games have you been able to improve the most since then? I felt like I've been developing pretty good. Um, a lot of it is, you know, transitioning through progressions, whether it's, you know, second, third, or or check down. Um, when you're moving smoothly through those and knowing where everybody's at and and how things progress and how fast things progress as well, uh, I I feel like, you know, you you get better as a quarterback and your completion percentage gets up because you're finding the right guys at the right time. And you know after that it's just about accuracy. >> How excited are you for Thursday? Are you nervous? Like what how are you feeling head? >> Yeah, I mean I'm very excited. You know, I I hadn't played at this level yet and just to go out there and showcase my my ability and to do it with the guys that, you know, we we've been working hard uh whether it's training camp, OTAAS, all that stuff. and just getting to know the guys and to finally go out there in a game setting is is going to be pretty pretty exciting. >> Uh do you feel comfortable taking steps from both Sam and Nick at this point having worked with them for a few weeks? >> Yes. Yes. Uh each and every day it gets better. You know, the more experienced, the more reps you get, the more comfortable you're going to feel. >> How's the communication been with them calling you and them calling protections? >> It's been pretty good. So far so good. Uh, you know, we we've had limited reps on certain things, but for the most part, the transitioning and the in the operation aspect, it's been really good. >> Building off Ashtai's question about Thursday, you this may end up being like the most preseason reps you get uh over the next month, how important do you think this opportunity is for you on a personal level as as you try to make the 53? It's very important, you know, uh, and it's not just 53 as as well. All the teams get to watch this film. So, it's almost kind of like a cool little try out for for everything. You know, whatever you put on film, it's it's going to be there forever. Uh, and you know, the eye in the sky don't lie as everybody says, but you know, I I feel like it'll be fun, but also at the end of the day, like you say, it's important. uh it's important for me and you know whatever is for me in the future. Do >> you have any pregame rituals that you go through? >> Um you know pray uh pray to God and then other than that I I kind of just hit check marks, you know, hey, did I warm up or did I do this? Uh do I have this? rather than, you know, I I'm not kind of not real anal about things like that. I I just kind of go with the flow and, you know, because at the end of the day, how you feel going into the game is is what's going to happen. Sometimes that changes. Like sometimes you have to do a little bit more to get ready. You're not feeling as good or sometimes you have to do a little bit less because you're like, I'm feeling ready to roll, you know? And I think that's probably going to be what it is Thursday, you know, ready to roll. Do you have like a pregame playlist or a stack like you have to eat before you go out there? >> Not really. Like I said, it just kind of depends what's going on. Uh like I like I said, if I feel down or whatever, it might be a little sugar, might be uh you know, some carbs, some protein just carry you through. And then snacks during the game is snacks during the halftime really. Uh, but at the end of the day, it's like I said, it whatever it is that I feel my body needs in order to to get through the day. >> The events around this game are a little different going into the Hall of Fame. How much of that is on your mind? >> You know, I I didn't even think about it, honestly. Uh, but I just kind of go with the flow and, you know, go day by day. Uh, and that's just kind of how I've been been living right now because at the end of the day, you know, I'm just trying to be where my feet are and and go from there. >> Did will retiring like change things for you in practice like snapwise? >> I've gotten a couple more reps. Yes. >> Have you noticed the difference just having those couple extra things? >> Um, I mean, yes, I I guess you'd say that. I mean, you know, getting more reps, obviously, you feel good about it and, you know, especially if it goes good and you execute well, um, it it's going to, you know, boost your confidence. >> You you obviously talked about wanting to go through all the questions, but are you anticipating making some plays with your feet uh, Thursday, it's something you do anyway, but a lot of times in the exhibition games with different off combinations of offensive lines and so forth, that ends up being a reality. Yes, just like you said it. I mean, your your legs are going to be one of the answers in preseason games with a lot of different groups, a lot of guys rotating. Stuff happens and uh you know, I'm not prepared to take off and run every every play, but you know, I'm going to go through my progressions and just kind of play football, play smart football, and if it, you know, means for me to take off and run, I'mma do it. or if it means for me to, you know, extend the play and try to get a big pass down the field, then I'm going to do that just at the end of the day and try and play quarterback. >> Anything else? >> Thanks. >> I know Keley spends a lot of time around this facility. Have you had a chance to meet him going into Thursday? >> I couldn't hear the first part of it. >> I know that Luke Keley spends a lot of time just around this facility in the building with the guys. Have you had a chance to meet him yet? And Are you excited to maybe be able to do that on Thursday? >> I'm very excited to do that on Thursday. I have not met him yet. Um I know he's he's a big part of of this place here and his name, his p pictures are are everywhere. Uh and I'm excited to meet him for sure. >> I know this is a business trip, but do you know if like the coaches are going to give you all a chance to go through the hall and all? >> Have no clue. I have no clue. All I'm doing I I just know we're playing Arizona. Anyone else? >> Thank you. >> Thank you. [music] [music]

You mentioned the practicing earlier and and extra did you anticipate maybe that you would have this sort of emotion at this point in the camp. Like are you rethinking maybe the practice schedule down the line? Well, just because of the numbers of practices that we've been able to store up, you know, the more that we go against each other and, you know, guys start learning each other's rush moves. Um, the double moves, the things, the different things that come uh out of the concepts, you know, and so the tighter it gets to guys anticipating, the harder they try to compete. title: Jesse Minter: ‘Can’t Wait to See Zay Flowers Thrive in Our Offense’ | Baltimore Ravens
text: Great day for the Ravens. Um, shout out to Zay Flowers. You know, when your best players um are just the right type of people and they bring the right just mentality and everything marries together, like those are the type of guys it's such a great thing when when uh stuff like that happens for them. uh nothing better as a coach and to see those guys get what they deserve and um you know so really happy for Z uh and excited for him and just again I can't wait to see him thrive uh in our offense and then uh second day in pads I thought there was a lot of good back and forth uh started off with a drive thought the offense started off really strong made a couple really key plays had it a third and long uh that they were able to convert and then uh some really good back and forth the rest of practice which we love to see so uh Good day. Open it up for questions. >> Did you find out about Zay just out there? >> Um yeah, on the right about you know that it was getting there, you know, maybe towards the beginning of practice and so uh again really cool really cool to see. Is that why you didn't practice or >> Yeah, it was um you know I think it was towards the finish line you know and I think that there's uh just you know being in that position um and then when something like that happens where it's really like you know lifech changing to I think to be smart for that particular day knowing the emotions probably running through Z. Um so I expect him to be out here back and ready to roll tomorrow. Jesse, I know it's you you can't compare to last year, but do you feel like since you've been here, he's really sort of embraced that mantle of being the number one receiver, one of the veterans in the room, all that stuff you expect to go along with a deal like that? >> I really do. I do think he takes great pride in being a leader in that room and and um you know, wants that room to be great as a whole and not just him. uh which you love for your for your key players. Now that you've been able to see their onfield chemistry, their off-field chemistry, I mean how important is is that for your team to have in place? Yeah, I mean I I think uh any quarterback would certainly want like um you know it's one thing to have chemistry off the field and then it's one thing to have it on the field and I think when you have both it makes it really really special and it and it has the ability to go to like a ridiculously high level. Um so they they do a lot of things together. They train in the offseason. Yeah, I mean that that's, you know, we talked a little bit about yesterday with the guys just like being able to bounce back and um you know, like a second and long turns into a third and long. Um and then somebody has to make a play and sometimes just keeping your head down, going to the next play, making a play can change the momentum. Um and so that was a great play by Jacobe. He's continued to flash and make those type of plays. As anybody, you know, you're always searching for consistency and down after down. Uh but again, talked about it like the more uh he shows Lamar that he's making those types of plays, the more trust they build. He's really good in the slot. He's really good on the move whenever whenever he has the ability to motion. Um he can beat press. He can beat off coverage. Um, so he's he's uh tough to prepare for and certainly glad he's on our side. >> What is a wide receiver one mean in modern night? >> I mean it's it's like um I I feel like there's and especially the trend right now on offense I would say I don't know maybe over half the league is is obviously doing some more under center some more like condensed formations. Um, and so I think it's like the ability to take that guy, put him in a lot of places to get him the ball. So it may not be that guy that lines up outside and it's every play is a one-on-one situation, but it's a guy that, you know, affects defenses by motioning, affects defenses by being on one side versus the other. Uh, he has that ability because he can he can not only take the top off the defense, he can catch the underneath stuff. He's elite with the ball in his hands after the catch. There's so many different ways to uh have him affect the game and uh you know that's what he is for us. >> Hey >> Jess, speaking of one-on- ones, the one-on-one matchups, wide outs and DBs and the individual stuff, what are you what are you as a coaching staff looking for? >> You know, I think uh it's it's just the competitiveness. It's making plays in front of everybody. Um so it was it was uh again just fun to see those guys compete and match up. It's it's one-on-one pass rush. It's sometimes really challenging to, you know, if it's not a quick quick win, like there's the pocket push and all that. You just get the we knocked out of him basically. >> Yeah, that's that's uh you know, he made a great break on the dig route. Made a great play. Another guy's breaking on the same ball, which you know, you you hate to see, but obviously happens. Uh when knocked out of him, took a minute to to kind of recoup and ended up coming back in later in practice. >> Two more for Jesse or what's your thoughts on training camp fights?
