I mean, to me it's um if in a game if you fight you get ejected. Uh look, like there's there's times where, you know, tempers rise and competitiveness happens. Um, I think there's a level that it can stay at, you know, a little bit of back and forth where we can get the guys back from each other, but to throw a punch or to uh do whatever that we're not going to have that, you know, that person's not going to be in after that. Um, but again, like you know, you know that stuff like there's a there's a realness to it. There's a competitiveness to it. You don't you certainly don't want to tone down the competitiveness, but at the end of the day, it's like if it's something that in a game gets you ejected from the game where you're no longer able to help the team, then to me that's not how we want to operate in practice. >> Is that something you would um talk to the team about before the like joint practice? >> Yeah, definitely. Definitely. Um and I think those things, you know, we're going to have a couple great opportunities there. Um it really comes down to to both teams having the mentality that we're there to make each other better. Um, it does get competitive. You get a chance to go against other people. How you see that as your responsibility to most often play in the back of the game? >> Uh, for sure I see that, man. you know, as long as I can, you know, stay on the filmwork, uh, see the formation recognition, you know, I'm going call out what I see. Uh, that's just always been my game. That's just always been me. And, uh, you know, I'm going to use my smarts and what I know to get everybody aligned and on the same page, you know, that helps everybody make plays, that helps us win, you know. So, those things are very important. Two more. Good. >> Thanks, Jamie.

Um, you know, [snorts] spending as much time as we can. um sitting next to each other in meetings and you know going through how we see things and talking it out day by day. We talk before we go to walk through of what, you know, the expectations are and, you know, how he feels like the system is being built and what we're going to, you know, major in. Um, but it's been it's been great. You know, I think him having that background as a former player and kind of understanding, you know, what we're going through and, you know, the the challenges of what we do. Um, I think that's a big help. You know, I feel like he understands, you know, our mindset and then obviously he's been coaching for a long time now, so he understands that aspect of it, too. Um, so he's been he's been great. How >> about the system itself for you? >> Yeah, the system's been good. You know, I think we're still in the early phases of learning it. Um, you know, we had OTAAS and then throughout the summer and then now the first, you know, week and a half of training camp really putting the pieces together and understanding how everything fits together. I think we're still building the identity. Um, but you know, for me, I feel like, you know, this is a system that I can thrive in honestly. Um, whether that's at Mike, whether that's, you know, we go to five down and you're playing the solo backer out there. Um, I think it's a it's a great opportunity um for myself as well. >> We spoke to Daltton yesterday and just spoke about how he feels like he found something this off season and how he approached lifting that is going to help him with his health. Have you tapped into anything different this off season that you feel like is going to help you stay on the field or help your game? >> Yeah, for sure. I think every year you kind of learn um you learn things and you know me and Dalton actually talked about that the other day. You know, changing up some things in the lift of what he's doing. Um, for me, I think it's my recovery and being open and honest about how I'm feeling, not just, you know, pushing through pain and pushing through injuries all the time. Um, you know, that's a that's a tough thing for me because I grew up just, you know, if I'm good enough to go, I'm good enough to go. Um, but, you know, as you get older and, you know, it's it's weird to say, but I feel like I've been in the league for a while now and I kind of understand, you know, I have to take care of myself and I have to take care of my body to make sure that I'm out there on Sundays. Um, so that's kind of been, you know, more of a mindset, you know, change for me is being open and honest just about how I'm feeling. >> How did that come about and how tough was that to get accustomed to? Actually, I need I need to open up about how I'm feeling because it's going to help me later in the season. >> Yeah, I think uh just just through the the season last year, you know, there were some things that I was dealing with from previous injuries that, you know, I didn't I I was addressing them, but I wasn't, you know, putting it out there about how it really felt. And um you know it kind of backfired a little bit. You know I wasn't healthy towards the end of the year and you know that's a a hard pill to swallow but you know I think I had some good communication with Joe in the offseason with Jim and just telling them you know the truth about what's going on and if you know there's a day where I don't feel right or something's not feeling right then I got to I got to be open and honest about that. Um which and you know before I would just power through and uh it wouldn't be uh it wouldn't be super productive. So, I think that's just something that I'm learning as I'm getting older. >> You talked about being grateful to be back out. What do you feel more I don't want to say re-energized or what is it like to you have something kind of taken away to now be able to be back out there? >> Yeah, I think like you said it is um kind of just being re-energized. I think, you know, you work so hard and, you know, when things don't go your way and you get, you know, you have to sit down for a little bit and, you know, you can't perform, you can't do what you want to do, um, it forces you to kind of take a step back and, you know, sit there and and think about it. And for me, you know, I I went back and what I talked about earlier, I went back and figured out a way to, you know, [snorts] really help myself and help the team, but then, um, you know, really just appreciate while I'm out there. And, you know, at the end of the day, things are going to come up. You know, stuff's going to happen. it's it's the NFL. Um, but you know, I just don't want to take the opportunity for granted and I don't want to take, you know, being out there with my teammates for granted and I think that's something that I learned last year. >> D, it feels like, you know, when the pads come on, you're going to get, you know, physicality and all that. I mean, from your perspective, what's the balance of I'm sure you want to see guys get physical, competitive, but also the ability to re it back. So, I guess from your perspective, what's the balance between that kind of ride? >> Yeah, I think, you know, the first day, um, obviously everybody's, you know, kind of flying around and and doing things. I think you got to figure out how to practice as a professional. Um, but at the end of the day, you know, we talked about it at at the end of practice here, like you'd rather be telling guys to pull it back than than to go. Um, so we'll go back, watch the tape, and see, you know, things that are acceptable, things that aren't acceptable, and move on from there. But, you know, in my my perspective, I'd rather I'd rather have guys going and, you know, flying around and doing the thing than having to tell somebody to go and do it. So, >> Joe has kind of adopted the mantra at least talking to us like put the ball down and go ball down and play. What's that mentality mean? And how have you seen it kind of play out practices? >> Yeah, for sure. I think, you know, that's that's our that's our motto. Um, you know, to me, put the ball down means whenever, wherever, whoever, um, whatever the situation is, we're going to go out and play. So, if it's practice at 8:30 in the morning when it's raining and it's cold outside, that's what we're doing. If, you know, we're in the middle of practice and we switch a period and, you know, it's best on best, that's what we're doing. Um, I think it's just the mindset of always competing and, you know, regardless of the situation, regardless of, you know, circumstances, that's what we're going to

title: Jeff Rodgers Addresses The Media | Buffalo Bills
text: Jeff, have you read a a situation like you have this year with with Tyler where you have a kicker who established to some degree who misses a whole year and now is trying to to get it all the way back. And and how do you approach trying to get him back to where he was? >> Uh I'd say there's been times in my career where there's been something either at the end of the season with a specialist or um you know an offseason procedure, whatever, guys coming back. Uh I I think you just go step by step with it and try and put them in the environments that they're going to be in. Kind of build from there. We've we've done some individual stuff. We've done some some team things so far. Uh hadn't worked out for us to be on the field quite yet. That'll happen later on this week and then again at the stadium. Um but I I don't think he skips steps. You know, it starts starts from ground zero and getting guys um you know, he's working with two new holders right now. You know, that's a part of that uh comfort. So, um, it's going to be a rep thing and, um, but he looks like he did on tape and, you know, everything's going well so far. >> Jeff, is that by design or just weather related that he's not been on on the field during practice? We've not seen him kick. I'm sure he's been kicking. >> Yes. >> Um, yes, your question, yes, he's kicked. Um, it has been by design. Not because it's like don't let him kick just yet. It's been, you know, there's a finite number of things that we can get done on the field and whether you are doing it amongst your team or in a joint practice, field goal protection is not going to be as combative in practice as it is in a game. You can get things like kickoff, you can get things like punt, um those kinds of phases. So, we've taken advantage of the walkthrough time because of the tempo that it requires uh or doesn't require and getting in that team environment, but at some point guys got to start working on that stuff. Uh so, this will be Thursday will be the third time that we do field goal protection as a team. Um but the first time we've done it in pads and we wanted a pad a day, so uh hopefully we get that worked out. Jeff, what are some of the challenges that Tyler faces kicking in an entirely new stadium and having it be his home stadium? >> Yeah, it's a little bit different because it is the home stadium, but NFL kickers are used to going to a stadium that they're not really familiar with, you know, when they play on the road. Um, you know, there's going to be things that that guys are going to acquire knowledge over time. We're fortunate we're going to be able to get in there on Saturday. We're going to get in there next week. We're going to get in there uh a couple of times and there'll be some times once we get back to Orchard Park where, you know, maybe the specialists can go over there at certain times during the day um and work on their craft. Um you know, maybe if it's a day we're doing kickoff, return, you know, those guys can go over there and kick. So, um we'll figure that stuff out as as time goes on, but it's you know, it's everybody. It's the returners, it's the kickers, it's the punters. So, um I' I've been in the stadium. I I've I've observed some of that stuff. Uh, it's really cool. Um, it's a great place, but as time goes on, you know, the things that you're able to say we went over there at 9:00 in the morning. Well, that might not be the wind pattern when it is at 7:00 p.m. or 8:00 p.m. So, we'll be looking for times uh to get over there and check it out. >> Tyler was saying he's wishing for a real windy day just to get an idea of what what it's going to be like in November, December. Is is that I mean, a real windy day to get in in practice and get a get a feel for that stadium. you're doing in the stadium. Yeah. Yeah. >> If it comes up, I mean, obviously if you know that real windy day happens the day before we're going to play a game, we're probably not going to go over there and kick, but uh we'll be looking for those opportunities to get over there. >> You're looking for a punt returner. Um how challenging is it to manufacture the opportunities you need to see from them in the preseason setting knowing you're completely at the mercy of game situation? Like in an ideal world, you'd love to get each guy three reps. sure >> over the course of the preseason, but that's easier said than done, right? So, how do you evaluate that when opportunities might not be ideal? >> Some of that stuff uh gets taken care of in practice. I mean, obviously, not obviously, um ball security and decision-m have a lot to do with the guy's success as punt returner. The skill set athletically, um you know, is what kind of makes a guy ascend, but if you can't catch it or you make bad decisions, you're probably not going to be out there and get, you know, a whole lot of chances. So, uh, the game situations mean more than what the practice stuff does. Um, I would also say there's a couple guys, couple candidates that we have who have game tape. You know, you take that into consideration, whatever their past successes are. Um, but we are looking for those things and there are a number of guys competing for that job. So, um, you know, look forward to seeing how it all shakes out. Yeah. Through uh Stephen Turner Gate through through your career, have you had more situations where you kind of knew who your guys were going in or is it like this where it's kind of a freef fall and you had to figure out what you have? >> It's a good question. I'd have to really think back. Um I would say it's probably 50/50. You know, if somebody was on your team and did a good job the year before, had took the bulk of them and then uh returning versus, you know, we do have to figure it out. So, um, you know, it just it doesn't always come down to like who has the best skill set as the return job. You you hope it does, but your roster's got to be able to accommodate that. Sometimes it's, you know, is is this roster spot worth, you know, this player if that's only the only thing he does. Um, you know, maybe he's a wide receiver, maybe he's a DB, maybe he's a running back, and if that guy's a contributor, it kind of saves a roster spot for not having to allocate that stuff. But the bottom line is that guy's got the ball in his hands a lot, especially with the new kickoff rule. Like there's not very many touchbacks. So, um I don't know what the numbers are, but you know, you need to have people back there that you trust. Um in the kickoff return game, you know, you need two. Um the chances of Ray being back there the first time we return a kick, pretty good. Um but who's back there with him, right? And who's the punt returner? Um and there's a bunch of guys who are competing for that job. and um you we'll see how it shakes out over the next month. Have you had conversations with Joe about for the punt return job? I want to I'm looking at this guy, let's just say Keon, he may be heavily involved offensively. What is what's that dialogue like of I want to kind of save you for offense and kind of manage that? >> Yeah, we've had some of those conversations. My job as a special teams coach is to try and figure out regardless of where anything goes, like I got to have answers. like the worst thing I can say is you know I I don't know you know once we've had a month and six weeks or whatever to figure it out. So, um, you know, Keon's been back there. Khalil did it obviously last year. D has, uh, return history, uh, with a previous team. And then, you know, there's Micole. I mean, there I'm not going to go through all of them, but I mean, there's another six, seven, eight names that I could I'm sure you guys are charting it during practice who's catching it. But, um, there's a bunch of guys there. So, at the end of the day, when we get to, you know, Labor Day and have to make those decisions, you just present the different options of here's what a guy's role is offensively, defensively, and, you know, can he return? Um, some of stuff may happen situationally, but there's going to be a time, and I've never been through an NFL season, you know, where it's not like, man, that other guy has to go in, you know. Um Patrick Peterson was the backup returner and got some burn uh when I was in Arizona. I mean, there's there's guys that are going to have to contribute at some point. So, um you're just trying to build the foundation now and however it shakes out on Labor Day, you kind of just uh figure out guys roles and what they're able to do. Uh after that, >> Jeff, going back to Tyler, he acknowledged there's going to be some nerves, some, you know, because he's not kicked, he's not kicked in a competitive setting for a while. >> How do you approach that? What how have you seen him kind of like work his confidence and mentality back to where it needs to be and knowing that that first kick is going to be his first kick in a while? >> Yeah. I mean, I I just think you try to simulate it as best you can in the environments that you're allowed to have. um team settings, you know, in the stadium, in preseason games. Um you know, generally speaking, those guys, there was there was a first kick for him in college, there was a first kick for him in the NFL, there's a first kick, you know, throughout the season. Um guys have ways of of getting themselves mentally and physically ready for that. Um, I'm just trying to coach the guys in front of him, you know, make sure he's protected, you know, snaps good, holds good, those kinds of things, and just let the natural talent take over when uh when he puts his foot on the ball. >> Tyler's had a lot of different holders throughout his career. What are your conversations like with him and building that trust with both of the punters here? And like how do you evaluate that? >> Um, it's a good question. I I do think that the more time goes on and the more guys that he's had to work with in the past that helps him helps all of us say, "Okay, here are the things. Here are kind of the check marks that like the non-negotiables, right? The ball needs to be down here so we can see it and you know, snap and like all of those types of things." Um it is a rep thing and when you have uh two guys working with them at the same time. What we've tried to do, what I've tried to do is um at least so far is today's Tommy's day to hold, today's Mitch's day to hold. Um and try not to, you know, get both guys involved as we can. um that may change as as time goes on where we'll have to mix in. But um I try to let them solidify that part of it cuz they both do a good job. But um you know it's different. You're working with a different person. So um you try and make it as similar as you can between the two guys so that Tyler's reps are the same all the time. >> Hey Jeff, what is uh Tommy's biggest challenge in transitioning from college to pro and everything the mentality that goes with it? Yeah, it's another good question. So, um, trying to answer your specific question, I would say this with a lot of college guys, the NFL punt play is different than the college punt play. And with the way that they punted at Florida, which is common for a lot of uh, college teams, like the field spread, it's a different formation. and you got three jumbo dudes sitting like five yards in front of the punter. It's just it's a different feel, right? Um [snorts] the same factors that go into success rates in college go into success rates in the NFL, efficiency, getting the ball off, hang time, directional uh placement. Uh he's going to do some of those same things here is what he did there. Um he's just got better guys, more consistent with the, you know, waiting on the ball. So, um, it's it's not a night and day difference in terms of what we're asking them to do, but receiving the ball, it just looks and feels different because where guys are allocated in terms of formation, that part of it is different. >> Coach, every uh, head coach has their preferences for what they're willing to allocate their special teams coordinators in terms of, hey, I I can give you four core guys for your big four units, etc., etc. Depending on lingo, >> what has Joe communicated to you in terms of what will be available to you in terms of 53 man rosters? >> We've talked in very general senses and we had a conversation during the walkthrough yesterday um in the office, you know, the other day. It is a long time till opening day. And what I've learned is it's not really worth talking about specific situations now because whether it's two or three injuries or a guy that you weren't expecting really ascends. I just keep talking about the puzzle that you got to put together and kind of how it all fits together. When I'm talking about roster makeup, um we had a meeting with the personnel department. I did uh sometime last week and they had me talk about, you know, some of the things we look for in players in roster comp and and and those types of things. I look at things in you have perimeter body types and you have kind of interior body types. So, it's how that I keep using the word puzzle. I've never said puzzle this many times in five minutes, but it's how do the tight ends fit in with the outside linebackers and the inside backers? how the wide receivers offset the corners and the safeties. Um, you know, some running backs are kind of tweener guys, some safeties can be tweener guys, but it it's just it's so long. You try and get as many guys reps, so you can say, "This is what I think this guy's strength is. This is what I think he struggles with. Um, if we make this decision, this is where this has got to come from." Um, so we have had conversations, but I would tell you it's been pretty general. It's not like, "Hey, dude, you got four roster spots. Do with it what you want." >> So, the short answer is TBD. But the when, I guess, do you and Joe want to have those answers in concrete form? Can you push it to Labor Day? Because you want to also get reps with the guys you're going to have, if that makes sense. So, is there like a point in time like, hey, by the time we get through that second preseason game, we want to feel pretty good about who our people are and then just hope they stay healthy. I think it's it's pretty close. by the time we get done with the joint practice, I I think it's pretty close where you can kind of see it's not 12 different roster battles. You know, it's it's kind of coming down to three or four in terms of uh not necessarily who make the team, but you know, the game day roster for us on fourth down means more than the 53man roster. I want as many good players. We all want as many good players as we can to to have on Sundays, but if the guy's inactive, you know, that's not really helping, you know, anywhere for that particular week because he can't play. So, um, that's where, you know, as you get down to the end of training camp, some of those roster battles have sorted themselves out after about four or five weeks. Um but then the game day roster decisions um you know are fluid throughout the season.

title: Bills President Pete Guelli! | Always Gameday in Buffalo
text: BILLS ON THREE, 1-2-3. >> HEY BILLS MAFIA, we know there's one thing on your mind every day. Your team, the Buffalo Bills. So, Matt Bove and Sal Capaccio are here to bring you the latest news, notes, and opinions straight from the source, right here, right now. Because it's always game day in Buffalo. >> [music] >> Welcome to a special edition of It's Always Game Day in Buffalo. Sal Capaccio, Matt Bove here at St. John Fisher University. And Matt, we have a very, very special guest joining us on the pod. >> Well, it's a Hall of Famer. We have a Hall of Famer. Now, how many Hall of Fames are you in? >> A handful. >> A handful. When you have more than one Hall of Fame that you're in, I feel like that's like very upper tier elite status. >> I'm not I'm not sure what it means, but honestly, [laughter] I'm always honored if they put me in anywhere. I'm happy that I'm in. >> Well, Pete Guelli joins us here. He is the president of business operations for the Buffalo Bills and the Buffalo Sabres. We had a lot of topics we want to discuss with Pete, so we're going to get right into it here at St. John Fisher University, the last week of training camp for the Buffalo Bills before they head back for the return of the red and blue. And it's stadium week, Pete. I mean, we have been talking about the stadium for years, and now it's finally here. Tell us a little bit about the preparations, what you have planned, and how excited you are for Saturday. >> Yeah, I mean, it's been a long road. Obviously, it's a massive project, and to think about people coming in there really for the first time, a lot of people on August 8th to see the building, see how it functions. It It's going to be hard to put into words. Um I think seeing it through the fans' eyes is going to be really cool, but then also, you know, operationally, just making sure everything is exactly the way we hoped it would be. There's so many different pieces. I guess traffic control and ingress egress and technology and game presentation, how it works for the football team, how it works for the fans. It's going to be fun to see all that, but um it's still a lot of work. You know, we're going to come back, recap what happened. I'm sure there'll be a number of things that we have to work on. But it's going to be cool to get that first big project under under our belts. >> What are the emotions? You nervous? You excited? What should we know about that work that that Gton did in the offseason to maximize what he can do out here? >> I mean, I think it was all inclusive. I mean, I think it was dieting. You know, I think it was recovery. I think it was the way he trained, like cross trainining, all those different things. I think, you know, it was more than just, you know, maybe I'll eat better during the week or more than just, okay, maybe I'll stretch before I go to bed. Like I really think, you know, he took a step back and like saw what he needed to get better at. He truly attacked that on all fronts. >> Does that kind of clarity from coach ease your mind a little bit? >> I mean, for sure. I mean, you know, just having that clarity. I don't think, you know, we should ever um you know, we should we should ever ease our minds cuz anything can happen. You know, guys go up, guys go down. Ultimately, you got to be ready and play in many different positions. But, you know, I do think, you know, just knowing what he wants, that definitely helps me out. >> What's the next step for this offense as a whole? >> I think just getting better every day. I mean, you know, I think you do great things and like you have you have good days, you have bad days, but, you know, let's keep stringing together those good days. Let's let's just get really consistent in what we do and how we do it and ultimately consistency will stand the test of time. >> Let's talk about the disappointment driving last year, not getting in the red zone very good. What needs to be done to reverse that? I mean, like I said, I think just playing more consistently. Like those drives are talking about whether it was self-inflicted wounds through penalties [music] or just, you know, getting in the red zone and stalling out and not being able to complete drives. I think us just being consistent with how we attack those situations and attack those parts of the field is just going to make us that much better of a team because, you know, you can win games like, you know, scoring every time with field goals and, you know, having a great defense, but let's just score six and make it easier for ourselves. >> Thank you. >> I promise you. What's the first camp in a new place like for you? >> Uh, it's been fun. You know, definitely getting uh, you know, to know get to know the new guys and kind of [music] just seeing what the culture is and you know, how to fit myself in and kind of, you know, bring my knowledge that I learned from, you know, the other organization. I'm going to help them out. So, it's been fun overall. >> What do you think of the setup here and the fact that you got more people along the fence line than in your hometown? >> Yeah, I was actually talking to Demo earlier today. I was like, it's like a movie every day. So many cameras everywhere. But, um, it's definitely been fun and, you know, I think it makes, you know, us compete a little bit harder when, you know, the cameras are out. So, I think it's a good thing. I mean, I think they're doing a really good job. >> How much have you guys bonded over? >> Yeah. >> Uh, I mean, we talked a little bit about it. Um, you know, he's into, you know, cattle and horses and stuff like that and I grew up doing the same thing. Um, but he actually came to me, he was like, "Dude, you only got 300 people in your in your hometown." I'm like, "Yeah." He like, "I'm only 800, so it's not that big of a difference." But, uh, yeah, we kind of bonded over that a little bit. And, um, It was like a good way to kind of get to know each other which was good. I >> think you two typify that talent can be found anywhere, right? >> What's that? I'm sorry. >> Talent can be found anywhere, no matter how big the town. >> Absolutely. If you know, put your head down and work hard, they'll come and find you. No doubt. >> What's your impression of how Christians built this defense? >> Uh, you know, you know, I think, you know, he's doing a really great job, especially with these blitzes. Um, you know, just the knowledge that he has and, you know, the scheme that he has behind him. I think it sets us up for success. And, you know, as a player, that's what you want. You want you want to play fast and kind of, you know, know the ins and outs and I think it does a really good job of that. >> When you play with Quinn Williams and Kenny Clark, how much easier does that make your job as a linebacker, especially when you're filling gaps in the run game? >> Yeah, it makes it really easy. I mean, you see a gap open, you can just shoot it because you know those guys are going to hold it down. Um whether that be, you know, single blocks or double teams, you know they're going to do their job and you just got to trust yourself to go do yours and I think that's, you know, what we're trying to do here. So, um, everyone can trust each other. >> Did you grow up a fan of the Cowboys? >> Uh, I had favorite players growing up. um not necessarily a Cowboys fan, but um whenever I would go home uh to my grandma's, she would never watch any other team except the Cowboys, so that's what I got to watch growing up. So, >> how does she feel about you being on the Cowboys? >> Oh, she's excited. Um she talked about it not too long ago and uh you know, I'm just grateful that I get to put a star on my head. >> How much easier did it make the transition being familiar with North Texas so much? >> Yeah, it made it really easy. I mean, like you said, I knew the ins and outs already. So, just um it's funny how God worked out. Like, I just bought a house in Arlington, so it was a smooth transition and it was just, you know, getting into the building, getting to know the guys, and kind of picking it up from there. That's the really the biggest thing that I wanted to do. >> Shotty was saying that the battle between Quinn Williams and Kenny Clark and the interior offensive line that you guys have has been a battle and a good one. How would you have a good viewpoint for it? How has that matchup been and and what's it like just to see it from your perspective? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I'm really not paying attention on what they're doing really except for, you know, whenever they're when they're running stunts and whatnot, but I'm more focused on like doing my one 111 and so I'm not strictly just looking at them and seeing who's winning or who's not. So, >> got you. But do you kind of as a linebacker almost anticipate sometimes like, okay, I got Quinnon Williams in front of me. There's a good chance if they try to double him, I know how I'm going to respond. Like, you know, like >> absolutely. Yeah. I mean, if Q's in there, I can play a little bit faster and then, you know, if Kenny's in there, you know, I know I have this gap, but I also can have this gap. So, it's just playing off each other, you know. Um, they do two different they can do two different things, so it's just playing off one another. >> What's your impression of Bar? >> Uh, J Sean's been amazing. Uh, just he's been a sponge just soaking up all the information and, you know, coming in and asking questions. I think, you know, where I messed up when I came in is I didn't really ask questions. Jan's just coming in asking questions. Um, even in walkth through, you know, he's stealing reps. He's always, you know, willing to get looking to get better and um, you know, I'm definitely excited to see what he can do this year. Is there a question that's been haunting you that like you wish you would have asked? >> Um, no. I feel like I got them all out my second year. So, um, I just told myself, um, that I want to, you know, get more involved and kind of ask dumb questions even though there isn't a dumb question. So, um, I pretty much asked them all at this point. So, >> one of the dumb questions you thought, >> uh, schematically, it's some basic things that I would ask that would be considered dumb, but um, something like that, like in quarters or something. And if I was the quarter flat player, even though I knew it, I just wanted to be, you know, sure. So stuff like that. >> How does this scheme fit you, especially coming from the 49ers coming? >> Yeah. Um, this scheme fits me, uh, pretty good. You know, I think it allows the linebackers to flow and play really, you know, fast. I think with my athleticism, um, you know, I can just play fast football and, you know, kind of react and just go play ball. So, >> yeah, absolutely. >> People that were familiar with Do you think your games maybe evolve or styles involve a couple years? >> Um, I think I'm more running hit. Um, in college I was more kind of thinking passing downs majority because I was a star. So, a nickel position. Um, but now that I've gotten NFL, just being in the box and kind of having a little bit of experience with that. I feel like it's helped me elevate my game and, you know, just just continuing to get better at it. Um, and stopping the run. >> Arlington to the star every day. Yeah, during OTAAS I was making that hour and 15 every day and it sucked. But um >> yeah, during the season I'll probably get some midway. Um that'll be a little bit more helpful. So excited for that for sure. >> Seems like the communication's been really effective through the defense through these first couple weeks. Why have you guys been able to implement that part of the the so well? >> Yeah, I think CP's just done a great job, you know, talking to us and communicating. So, um I think whenever we get out here on the field and guys know what they're doing, they're able to communicate. All right, we got this. Look, we're going to communicate this and I think it helps every all 11 players on the field. So, um, just communicating and, you know, trying to help each other out is essentially what we want to do. >> Thank you, man. >> Y, >> thank you. Yep. You >> talked about how you're a different person right now than [snorts] you were this time last year. Uh, what does that mean specifically and how are you putting that into play as you're stacking these good days out here? >> Yeah. Um, just being more intentional. Uh, like I said, man, you know, this offseason, my main priority was just, you know, making sure that I, you know, stayed in the playbook and was doing the things that the the coaches was asking me to do. And, you know, I I took that uh, you know, to the heart and, you know, like like like as you said, you know, I'm having a great camp so far. And, you know, I didn't want to, you know, come in here and start slow, you know, like I did last year. You know, I wanted to make sure, you know, I came in here and started fast and and proved myself. Now that you've kind of dug deeper into the playbook and and kind of you're studying it more and more and more, has the game started to slow down for you in your second training camp? >> Yeah, absolutely, man. The game is slow down a lot to me. Uh, you know, it's it's kind of coming easy to me now. Like I said, man, I probably know the playbook like the back of my hand now. So, you know, once I know the playbook like that, you know, I can I can play fast. >> It sounds like you took constructive criticism and did something about it. >> Absolutely. You know, there were some I knew that there [music] was some, you know, constructive criticism that was going to come with it, but you know, that that's all a part of it. And you know, I you know, I took that as motivation and I also looked myself in the mirror like I got to be better, you know, if I want to be where I uh want to be. >> How key has Derek Foster been in your growth just, you know, from year one to year two? >> Yeah, man. He's, you know, everything for me, man. Like I said, man, we we have a very good relationship. You know, he he calls me, you know, almost every day and and make sure I'm good. And, you know, when we here, man, he's standing in my ear. You know, he's he's teaching me the things that I need to know. And, you know, he's he's always pushing me to be the best version of myself. What do you feel like your best moment at camp has been so far? >> Uh man, really just the, you know, the explosiveness, you know, just the big plays. Uh, you know, just showing that, you know, I can not only the vision, but, you know, that I can also, you know, be explosive and in a running pass game. >> How do you earn trust with people, >> man? Just making sure I know what I'm doing. Uh, making sure that I'm, you know, not making mental errors. Uh, making sure I know my assignment and mainly just, you know, you know, performing on the field. You know, I think that's the main thing. But you know the first thing is just you know making sure that I know my assignment so that you know I can gain the trust of Dak you know the coaching staff and and my teammates. >> At the end of the day you came in with Phil. I assume you all have a good relationship. How do you all balance that with all also the competition element? >> Yeah. Um like I said man we have a really good room. Uh you know we all you know love that you know we we push each other you know to to be our best every day man. Like I said we know it's a competition but at the same time you know we're trying to uh help each other make each other better. Shotti's talked about the battles between Quinton Williams and Kenny Clark in the interior that you guys have. Obviously really good interior as well. You have a good viewpoint of that. What are those battles like? >> Man, those are probably, you know, two of the best, you know, D linemen in this league. Uh, you know, it's very tough, but at the same time, you know, it's good for us, you know, for us, you know, as running backs and offense to be able to go against, you know, two guys like that, you know, in this league, you know, it only makes us better. >> How much do you have to be aware of them, too, as a running back? Like, hey, if Quinnon's here and I know I'm going there, he might beat that gap. Might have to bounce off that. Like I said, man, a lot of that is just, you know, trusting our, you know, preparation, you know, taking from what we've been coaching in the meeting rooms and translating it to the field and, you know, just having good eyes and and and knowing how they're going to play it. >> Thank you. Pleasure.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: "I Would Follow That Guy Anywhere" | Press Conference
text: Let's go. Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. Uh, any update on Princeton Fant after he left practice? >> Yep. Uh, yeah, Bull did suffer ACL. Um, got a, uh, partial MCL. Um, really disappointed for him for everything that he's put into this. Obviously, he was very, um, disappointed. Um, but I told him, "Hey, look, your story is far from over. uh he's been through this injury before and uh the doctors feel really good about the chance for him making a full recovery and uh so he'll have surgery here in a couple weeks once the MCL calms down a little bit >> uh after that first pat of practice. What were your thoughts on on what you saw? >> Yeah, I thought it was really good uh back and forth. You know, I thought uh you know, defense did some really good things. I thought the offense responded in the red zone, couple touchdowns. Uh I thought the padded work was really really good. There's a clip I showed the guys of the very first play. You know, GP comes down. He cracks Maris Bell. Uh Demo and and Hunter Lepkkey kind of collide in the hole. Uh as a rock who's folding off the edge, he's unblocked. Tags off, doesn't take a side shot. Uh I thought it was really really good work for the first time. Got the threes more work, which we wanted to do that. You know, we need to get these guys ready to play, you know, some real football. And that was good for them. And uh it helped us kind of figure out who's up to speed with our system. Uh so overall I thought it was really really good >> playing the LLS Cowboys look like Rebel had the best day of camp you know and certainly made plays when the ball was talking about him his confidence in the second year. >> Yeah I think you know when you talk about Von Clarence I mean you know when he puts his hands on people he's strong he's got great length uh I know there's a reroute he got Sidi in the cover two that was really cool to see uh and and that's kind of what he's focused on right now. You know he knows he's at his best when he puts hands on people. Uh there's still a time clock. I'll use that example with CD. Like, you know, great reroute on CD. Once you get the reroute, now you have to start the second part of the coverage. And at some point, you got to let him go, you know, because he was still jamming CD six or seven yards down the line of scrimmage, uh or into the secondary. But u I thought it was a very, very good day challenging things, putting hands on people, couple good PBUs. Um I thought you felt his confidence. also, you know, been pretty good since the start of camp, but one play yesterday he kind of cut off his man and snuck underneath and got intercepted from the deck. Was that him knowing the play or just him diagnosing the play and just his smarts as a veteran? >> Yeah, I think you saw his instincts, you know, his instincts and the ability to feel things and, you know, you're playing different coverages down there and um, you know, he's he's been around this system for a while, different places, playing with the Rams, a lot of similarities with what they're doing. Um, but you know, I asked him, it was a great play. I said, you know, did you score? Did you get caught at like the 30? And he said, Shotty, hey, check out all my interceptions. They usually go the distance, so we'll see. But it was a hell of a play by him. >> Brian with ESPN. You talked about Quinnon Williams a couple times, but I'm wondering what do you think is the benefit for him of, you know, you come in middle of season, you're kind of figuring all these things out of just being around you guys and he can be how that will impact him on the field. had more time around everybody even if it is a new defense. >> Yeah, I think number one uh Quinn and I at the end of the season we had some really cool conversations. I'm not going to share everything we talked about, but just, you know, talking about different things and, you know, the importance of winning and, hey, what philosophy of defense we think we're going to get into. And, um, we talked and, um, you know, discussed a lot of things. And, um, [clears throat] you know, he said to me the other day, he was telling me how excited he was about this system. He's going to get a bunch of one-on- ones. He's going to get a bunch of situations where he's, you know, having to get blocked by guards and with him and Kenny working in there together. But, you know, I see his leadership style now. You know, Todd, I mean, I feel him. Quinn's, you know, he doesn't speak a lot, but boy, the way he works, the way he practices impressive. Um, but, uh, he's a grown ass man and there's some leadership things that that we see that you guys probably don't where there's some things maybe going on that need to get kind of shut down and he's the first one on the spot, uh, to get it shut down. I just think he's he's he's he's finding his voice with us and with this team and this defense and it's hard. I mean, you ask any player that's ever been moved mid-season and then our circumstance were unique with losing Marshon. Um, but I would say way way way more comfortable with with what we're doing schematically, but also in finding and using his voice, which is a very very strong voice. >> Is he a guy as an offensive play called like people have always said, hey, you got to know where number 11 is when Mike goes around. Oh, >> yeah. Is he a guy? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I mean, yeah, he's a guy that if you if you try to single him, it's going to be a long day for wherever that guard is, even as good as our guards are. I mean, the battles that they're having right now are are awesome. But, uh, yeah, he's he's a guy you you have to know where he is. And, uh, what that does, it helps guys like Kenny Clark and Tito and guys like that eat a little bit. >> Show was athletic after your first p of practice. What are the conversations like, if there are any between you and Christian Parker? Is there trash talking or does that not probably come until a little bit after you get some more? >> No, you talk trash on the field. I mean, it's no different than players on game day, coaches on game day. I mean, the energy of playing in the moment, there's always good trash talk. Like I said, I thought yesterday was a really good back and forth day, uh, John. And, um, you know, I went in and watched the film with the defense yesterday and again, like I said, it's just it's really cool for me to see how all of this fits together. You know, we're three installs in. Yesterday was review day. I kind of know where we're going now and um yeah, it's uh it's it's been awesome and uh like I said, he's very convicted on what he wants and I think he and his staff are doing a terrific job of of teaching the scheme but also not losing the fundamentals. >> What's the process with the Guardian caps? Like who wears them? Is it players choice? Is it up to the team? >> It's league mandated. Um the guardian caps are serving a purpose. Uh, if you're in certain types of helmets, you don't have to wear them. There's rankings for the helmets. I won't get into specifics of it. It's color system, but if you wear certain helmets, you don't have to wear the guardian caps. Uh, if you're in helmets that don't meet some of those specifications, then you have to wear the guardian caps. And then kickers and uh quarterbacks don't have to don't have to wear them. >> For start, I think overall for the DBs yesterday, it had to be positive to see on y'all's end. Just overall the physicality and the first day from the secondary specifically. Yeah, >> you know, when you play this quarters type system, you know, Nick, I mean, you're going to have to crack these safeties. They're going to show up fast. Jaylen Thompson, PJ Lockach, he'll work back into practice, by the way, today. Um, you know, Maris Bell, Julius Wood. Uh, so the corners have to be able to tackle. That's a big part of it. So, you got to know how to crack replace. You got to know how to be a leverage tackler. You got to know how to shimmy to take your shot. All the things that we teach in our tackling circuit. But, uh, overall, I I thought they competed really, really well in both the run and the pass. Um, and you can see the the communication is at a very very high level for this early in camp, especially in some of the red zone work that we did. Uh, the communication I think is um is um exactly where it needs to be, but maybe even farther along than we thought it might be after three installs. >> Catching the end zone yesterday and just kind of speaking to how different things are this year for him compared to this time last year. >> Yeah, you know, you guys ask about Flo every now and again. I mean, I think, you know, he's one of those young players going into year three. We talk a lot around here about year three kind of being not the only time it can happen, but usually it happens around year three. Uh we've got some other guys on the team going into year three that we hope have those same strides. But the confidence, the clarity, he's, you know, everything with with Flo is, you know, guided by his faith. I mean, his faith is incredibly strong. He's very open and speaks to it. And um it was funny because uh the way we built the the concept yesterday uh it was going to be CD. We got stuck with a different motion and movement and um you know Flo got the matchup that we were looking for on Don and uh it was uh cool to see those two guys battle. >> Tommy Yarcowboys.com. in those periods yesterday where you let Clayton and Christian call the plays. Maybe more so with Clayton. But as a play caller, do you watch what he calls and say, "Oh, that sequence, I didn't think about it that way." And maybe try to pluck some ideas from how he does it for yourself. >> Uh, no. Great question. Um, no. I was more on the defense. You know, when I get a chance to be over there, I want to know what the the call is and kind of test myself as I'm learning some of the language and understanding the adjustments and things like that. Uh, I thought both guys did a great job what I told them both. And this is something that, you know, was was, you know, said to me a long time ago was, you know, when they went in yesterday in their quiet moments, which late at night, whatever, just shut your door and just list things you did well. They did they did good things, right? Things you felt you could have done better. And then, of course, come up with a plan of how to do that. But, uh, I thought both those guys did a good job. You know, Clayton mixed the personnel up. You know, he moved the pocket some, which was really good. Uh, played ourselves in some third and long situations. Uh, and I thought, you know, CP was really good. He threw some pressures at us. He He did some things from a front standpoint that we weren't um expecting, but you I'm giving those guys chances to do it, but they have to maximize that by taking the time when they get back to their rooms to sit down and and list those things, and that's the only way you're going to get better. >> When you're getting into one-on- ones today, I know players typically get excited for that. What do you look for when you turn the film back on later on today? Yeah, again I I obly want them to compete one, but again, I want to see these guys, you know, with receivers's DBs, can you get open or do you get gloves? You know, offensive lineman, can you block a defensive end or an outside linebacker or a defensive lineman? And, you know, running backs, can you win on your routes? It's all route based today. There won't be any pass protection uh for the skill guys. The O line will. Um, but you really, you know, these are well thoughtout matchups and, um, I think that's, uh, you know, something that we'll watch and we'll watch it with the guys, too, cuz they they do love it and it's part of using, you know, can you go out there and in a one-on-one situation where there's no play given and be thinking of concepts, schemes, coverages, and then use your proper technique. A lot of guys just go out there and say, "Okay, I'm going to cover Todd." Uh, but it's more than that. Am I outside leverage? Am I inside leverage? Am I nearand jam? Am I a replace? Am I a bail corner? Am I a patient corner? I mean, there's all kinds of things that you have to figure out. >> Brad Sham, Cowboys Radio 1053, the fan. As you're trying to uh build your depth in the offensive line, what about Cornelius's skill set made you look at him and see a guard? >> Um, we love his length. I mean, he's got length, Brad. You know, um, you know, AJ's a guy that obviously we, you know, liked enough to draft. Uh, we like his length. We like his the way his brain works. He's got the ability to play from a mental capacity in inside and outside. And you know, quite honestly, after the first two days, we just kind of he wasn't getting enough reps. You know, we've got a a battle going on and different combinations were working at tackle and um so we, you know, we feel really good about the football player and he's been really, really good in there. You know, he got out on a screen pass yesterday that was really cool to see. Um, and it's different, you know, and uh, sometimes you move guys around and you figure out, hey, they're a little bit better inside than they are outside. And, uh, you know, um, he's a fine young football player that we're just trying to figure out and give him the most opts to see where he fits. >> Joe Hoy, Dallas Morning News. We talked so much about Christian Parker scheme, but obviously he kind of cut his teeth helping Pastor Tan, Cooper Deene, these guys get elevated there. From just an onfield perspective with his hands-on teaching, how have you seen him kind of help some of these corners try to elevate? Well, he's a great teacher. One, I think I've been very open about that. You know, he he he simplifies it into a good way. He's excellent with fundamentals and techniques. Um, but, you know, that's the way I used to coach quarterbacks. You know, I wanted to be hands-on and and receivers be hands-on and demonstrate. And as I get a little bit older, I get get out of that now. I mean, my heart rate gets up a little high now over 50. But, um, I think he's awesome. But, again, I don't want to make this just about CP. Derek Ansley is an elite football coach and we are so fortunate to have him. Ryan Smith, the way that secondary is built with, you know, Rob Muschamp being there and and and DA and and Smitty along with CP. Um, we're loaded for bear there. And I think that's important. I really do. I think, you know, in my opinion, you know, what you're seeing now is the evolution of secondary coaches becoming uh coordinators. Why? If you can't stop big plays and if you can't figure out why the ball is getting thrown over your head for 40 and 50 and 30 yard big plays, uh, you're going to have a long day. And so I think you're seeing the evolution that there's going to be a lot more secondary coaches that are defensive coordinators in the league. You >> talk about the battles in the interior between Quinn and all the guys in the interior with their play strength, just what they're able to do at the point of attack. How much does that help from giving a look for these interior guys? Just >> Yeah, it's invaluable. But it's not just the play strength. They're obviously incredibly powerful. you look at them, you know, from the waist up and uh the size and power that they have, but don't be fooled. Kenny Clark might be the most fundamentally sound interior defensive lineman in the league. Now, he's got the built-in advantage of leverage, you know, but uh I mean, his hands and his ability to replace and his ability to shed and all that stuff, but there were some really cool plays yesterday. I'd be remiss for not mentioning Tito where you know Tito's playing gap and a half which we're playing now and he gets great extension and he's reading his keys and he falls back and um you know it's uh it's fun to watch those guys compete but um fundamentals make a difference inside. >> Hey coach Patrick W at dallascowboys.com a little bit ago you spoke about thirdyear players that you need to make a jump obviously Tyler guy falls into that mix. Uh biggest uh red flag on him is availability. Time will tell that story. But yesterday, first p of practice, acquitted himself very well. What are you seeing from him? What do you need to continue seeing from him? >> Yeah, I I think he's doing some really great things. I think his sets are very uh compact. You know, he's in control. He's not over setting. He's playing the leverage game. His punches have been good. Uh but I don't think that that's anything new to the pads, Patrick. I think that started with him being one of the first guys back in the building. I think February, whatever I saw him, um he was an offseason award winner. Uh, I think you feel confidence. Um, you know, obviously we're allowed, we have the right to, you know, adjust some things and so we're going to keep him at at starting left tackle right now. We talked to Nate and said, you know, Nate needs to show us a little bit more consistent play to push for that. And so, um, you know, I know we had told you guys about the rotation, so Tyler will stay at left tackle. Uh, excited to see how Nate handles that challenge. title: Campanile & Walker on Day 2 of Pads, Competition & Goals | Press Conference | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: All right. So, you guys got some pats working. Just kind of What did you see over the last two days? >> Um, I thought today for us defensively a little bit better than yesterday. Um, but that's what you're trying to do. You know, you're trying to build a callous and uh and just honestly entering blocks the right way, you know, entering tackles the right way, all the fundamental things uh that are important to winning and playing good football. Certainly playing good defense. Um, and we get a great look at it because, you know, I think our offensive line coaches do a great job. There's got, those guys are really firm in the front. They play with great pad level. Our backs run with great pad level. I know Chad's all over them about that every day. So, uh, that's, you know, more of that will continue to make us better. The >> the standard that was set with the run defense last year, have you seen the guys come in wanting to build off that and be even better? >> Yeah, I I think so. I think, uh, I think we know we can be better. You know, there's definitely some meat on the bone there with left on the bone. And um they're all pretty bought in to the process. You know, some of you guys who I've been around here to practice, you see Coach Jenkins here and uh you know, Pete Jenkins here in individual drill and he's kind of been everywhere I've been since uh I was in Miami and like he's the goat. You know, he's uh so much of what I believe uh comes from coach and and uh he's honest. You know, he's come here and, you know, comes in here and he's ripping my ass and ripping. I mean, he's you know, he's just telling the truth. So, um, we got him, uh, in here kind of just watching everything, making sure we're doing a great job with the drills and training the guys the right way and, uh, he's done a pretty good job for all the teams in the SEC the last 10, what, 20 years, 30 years. So, uh, hopefully, uh, having him here and I know it is going to help us. >> Do you count some bad days? >> Say again. Do you need some off days, bad? You know, you got to tell the truth and uh you got to see around corners and see what the problems lying ahead are. You know, it might not get you here, but uh my college coach, Coach Yaniano, used to talk about that all the time. you know, gets you when it gets you. And um you got to be on that and I think that's a huge part of of coaching. So, um never as good as you think it is, never as bad as you think it is, but you got to be honest. It's the only way for anything to get better. It's the only way anything improves. >> The impact he can make, >> Rrook, >> the impact he can make. >> Um I think he can make a great impact for us. Um he's playing really, really hard, learning our system. A lot of the fundamental things that he's learning every day, it's, you know, it's new to him. Um, so in that regard, a lot of this stuff is fresh and now you're starting to see him apply it and I think he's doing a good job with it. But like everybody, you know, he's got uh a gap to close, you know, on where he wants to be and uh that's true of everybody out here. But I think he can help us. I think he's done a really good job in the rush and he's done a good job on early down so far in camp. Personally, I try to watch the game from the middle out. And I think the more you do that, the more you can see there. You know, the better you get at doing that, the more you can see. Um, and you got to really, in practice, in my opinion, if you can relax your eyes, you can see a lot more. Um, you know, if you're staring at one particular spot, you don't see the whole picture. Um, but I think our coaches do a great job of anything I miss, they're constantly filling me in. every time I ask a question like all our guys are watching their guys um and where they're standing in the drills and where they're standing in the practice. Um that's by design. So we talk about that a lot and they're doing a really good job of that. Watching the players eyes, you know, watching their entry and all that stuff. That stuff is important I think for them to get better. >> Bryson Collins has kind of looked like he's off to a good start, isn't it? >> Yeah. Yeah. I think, like I said the last time I was up here, that's a a heated competition in that room. And um, you know, I think competition breeds competitors and Liam did an unbelievable job of that here last year. Like you know, Matt Dickerson played his ass off on uh, you know, scout team last year and we ended up bringing him up and he did a great job for us out on the field. So that's real here. You know, our head coach believes in that. He believes in competition. Uh, and if you're doing a great job and you're producing, you're going to get an opportunity to play. So that's what it's all about. It's about stacking days and and continuing to produce. But the guys in there are in a good competition and they're all playing hard. >> You're a coach that consistently brings that fire and that intensity with the pads coming on. Want to be the want that to be the culture of the room? You know what I mean? um that when we get together, we unit meet, we're going to call that out when we don't see it, you know, and uh just going to be honest. If it isn't up to the standard, uh and we're not doing that and we're not performing physically and we're not violently finishing, you know, trying to whoop the other guys' ass on every play, it's going to get called out and if you are, it's going to get celebrated. Um and I just think that that's a good culture to have and and hopefully we're trending that way. But our players believe in that. um from the defensive backs all the way down to the D line, they all believe in that and they're great guys to coach honestly because of that. They're they're great. title: Detroit Lions players meet with the media | 2026 Training Camp Day 6
text: Dan said to us that on Monday defense won the day. What the challenge to you guys today? It's going to be defenses good for a few days and offense is good for a few days and it's just kind of that flow of thing and riding the wave and trying to stay consistent through the whole thing. How do you see different from this offensive line just a year ago? Obviously, there's a little acclamation period, but with some new pieces and the way guys moved around. >> Um, I think the attitude as a whole, the physical attitude, the mindset in the meeting room and on the field is is different this year. I'd say it's it's a lot better. Um, and just the way we attack every day at practice. >> Last year as a rookie, I assume you were drinking water from a fire hose. Now that you're in your sophomore season, how much more comfortable do you feel? >> Yeah, drinking from a fire hose to to say the least. Um, you know, a lot more. I had a lot of learning experiences uh last year. So, trying to build on those and not let those things happen again. Um had, like I said, a lot of learning experiences from last year. >> What was the biggest takeaway that you got and what was the biggest thing that you would take from that? >> Um first off, how long the season is? Um you always heard it coming out of college and all that, but you you never really think about it until that you're actually in it. And I was in it last year, so kind of being able to expect that and then how fast and how physical the game is through all 18 weeks. So with new faces and also new guys in new places, how long do you think it takes to really gel and feel like you're focused? >> I mean, that's what we're out here for. We get reps at it every day, whether that's passing off stunts in the pass game, the run game, fitting up on combos, learning the guy next to you. That's what we're out here for to do this every day. So hopefully as camp goes on, we keep getting better and better together. >> How do you I guess how do you gauge that or how do you feel that when you're out there? >> It's just reps. Like >> I was playing next to Paneet last year. P is one of the best tackles of football. Obviously things felt weird next to him at first, certain ways he plays it, but once you get used to it, it flows. You have the the benefit of having Kane there. Now you've got a rookie on your side. Um he is picking things up very well from what I can see. um he's never looking at me really asking questions and when he does it's I try to help him out as much as I can but I think he's doing a phenomenal job so far. >> Do you feel like there's still maybe a little more additional pressure though with you given that you have two new pieces between you this year? >> I mean I wouldn't necessarily say more pressure. It's just like we just talked about building those reps and getting cohesiveness. How much uh I mean is it an emphasis to kind of reestablish I guess you know that that I guess veerity with the run game that you guys uh you know kind of were known for. >> Yeah. Yeah. I think that's a big emphasis we have to be able to run the ball. Being able to run the ball opens up everything else in the offense and being able to run the ball against somebody's will is demoralizing to another team. So that's our goal to get back to that. >> Um I mean what what gives you the confidence that like with this group that you know you can reestablish that? >> Um the mindset. Um, I think everybody on offensive line right now has a mindset that we're going to go out there and be more physical than the guy in front of us. And right now, we're going up against a really good defense and a really good defensive line. So, it's really testing us and building building us up. >> What What does that edge do, you think, you know, to to opponents when you when you do have that kind of >> I mean, if you can run the ball at will, it's demoralizing. I mean, I think if you ask any defense out there, if somebody's able to run the ball on you at will, it's there's not much you can do. when you talk about the attitude maybe working differently than we do. How how much wicked is you for that concept guys? >> Very much so. I mean, we have one of the best backs in the league. Uh there is should be no reason we should not be able to run the ball on people. Um I think Cade fits in well. He's I think he's a very good run blocker feeling. Our double teams, you can tell. Um but I think he's coming along great in this offense. >> How much of a difference just in mentality does two make for you? >> A lot. Everything's a lot clearer. like I'm seeing the big picture now, not just my assignment, what's in front of me. I'm seeing things coming before before they happen. So, I don't know. Just how hungry, how eager are you to try to prove them right this year two, three years later? >> I feel eager because a lot of, you know, things been happening off the field, but I feel eager. I I got to step up big this year. I mean, just for my last name and and the Lions name, you know, first I get all the bad rep for, you know, the media sometimes. And then for my teammates, like they depend on me. They see the work I put in and it's a lot of stuff that people don't see in the inside. So, I just got to piece together so when it's time to show, I can show. >> Dennis, when you get those that work against Jingle when that that one-on-one work, I mean, obviously didn't get a lot of it last year just cuz Andrew, I don't remember what you got as a rookie. What does that mean for you? What does that do for you? Your confidence, your ability to guard top receivers? That helped me out a lot cuz it's not always like in a game you ain't going to win every rep and you ain't going to lose every rep either, but it's about competing for the ball and then he won one and I got a punch out. I mean, keep getting better. He going to get better on the punch out. I'm going to get better on the fade. Just it just keep getting better. That's all I can do. >> You slip on the one that he won, too. >> I slipped on it, but it's football like it's it's going to happen next play. We got into team segments. Didn't allow nothing next play. That's why I keep saying next place. Things going to happen in here. They get paid a lot of money, too. You know what I'm going to happen. >> And I don't know that punch out. Is that something you've been you >> I mean punch out I always been a punch out guy but it's go it got to uptake here. title: Daniel Jones looks sharp in 11-on-11, Cam Bynum leads the defense
text: Day six from Colts training camp here at Grand Park is complete. We head into an off day before night practice on Thursday. A lot going on today in today's 90minute practice. We'll break it all down here. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star here with Joel Ericson. Um we got a chance to see the Colts air it out a little bit more on offense today. Um great catches by uh tight end Tyler Warren. Um uh Ashton Dan I think had a couple we got to see the kickers. Um what what was your biggest takeaway from what we saw in day six of Colts training camp today? >> Well, the biggest one is that a lot of those downfield plays came with a little bit of a caveat that the pass rush was there for at least one or two of them. Um and at least two of them that there were definitely would have been a sack. There were two more that it could have been a sack. It was tough to tell if it would if he would have hit him as he as it got off. But that there's this is a pass rush that's under fire. This is a pass rush that most of us don't think is going to be good enough to carry its weight. It looked good today though. some some good moves from Layatu Latu in one-on- ons. Uh he beat Jaylen Travis pretty badly. Um but you've also seen some other guys. Ardan Key beat Bernard Ryman today for one of them. Uh you've seen Jaylen Tuol show up a little bit. So you're seeing a little bit from the pass rush. That's encouraging considering what we kind of thought coming in. >> I know we hadn't seen the Colts aired out a whole lot through the first five days of practice. Um, I think it sounded like from talking to Jim Bob Cter and Daniel Jones that what we saw today at the end in the 111 session was maybe a little bit of situational work, third downs. Um, so we were seeing a little bit more passes. I think Daniel went five for five if uh if I remember my notes there on that session. So you you saw a lot of what you would want to see from um a connection standpoint. Daniel um just spoke with us, said he continues to feel great as he's coming back from that torn Achilles. uh just about uh I think we're a couple days short now from 8 months ago. Um he's taken all of the ones reps. Um so solid work there. One thing I saw or was looking out for and we saw to start practice today um a little bit more of an update on the kicking competition. Blake Groupy kicked yesterday. Spencer Schrader kicked today. He missed a couple. One from 45 and one from 57. Both um to the left, which is the same direction we saw him miss from on Friday last week. Brian Mason, the special teams coordinator, told us um that there's a little bit more work that we don't see going on behind the scenes. They're kicking before practice and so he's got a little bit more of a broader idea on where each guy is and what they need to work on. Um but it does feel like even from that work that he was telling us about that Blake Groupy has a little bit of an early lead through the first week or so of camp. >> Yeah, understandable with Shraider's uh understandable with Shrader coming off the injury. My one play for the day. Uh I'm actually gonna zag a little bit and go with Jonathan Taylor kind of giving CJ Allen a rookie moment on a screen. He got out in the open field. Allen thought he had him lined up. JT uh had a little stutter step and then into a spin and I don't think CJ Allen touched him. I think he just grabbed air. >> Yeah. Uh C little CG Allen tidbit. We've seen Cam Binham working into uh that green dot role with the defense the last couple days. Lou Inarumo told us that that's not necessarily something that they have um officially taken away from CJ Allen. They're just experimenting a little bit with having um that veteran safety presence in Camb. Um I don't even I'm not even sure I saw CJ Allen at least out there too much with the ones. They've are continuing to rotate through that deep linebacker room that they have there. We'll see how that um that decision pans out over the next couple weeks um as you know CJ Allen gets a little bit more work in camp. if he missed the first couple days. Um, and so he's still kind of working his way back um in into it. I think that's all we've got. Day six of Colts training camp over here. We get uh Wednesday off. The Colts will be playing under the lights for 2hour session at 8:00 p.m. at Graham Park on Thursday night. We will have several stories today and tomorrow. Please check out indiestar.com for all of those. just go check out our YouTube page where all of our videos along with interviews from um either our interviews from camp, videos from practice um will all be housed there. We appreciate you guys checking us out there and following along. I'm Nathan Brown. He's Joel Ericson. Thanks for following along with Indie Star. >> I don't know if you've uh seen the news around the NFL today. John Robinson signed a three or 75 million deal. Were you uh how do you react when you hear that number? >> I man I'm happy. I'm happy for him and his family. The guy works hard. Um, and I haven't been with him in the offseason, but like the guy works hard to be at his best for his team. So, it's awesome to see that for him and his family. Like, it's a special moment. So, I I hope he enjoys it and really really soaks it in. >> I guess is that a testament on where you feel like the the running back market is headed. I know just a couple years ago you were fighting for your deal and he signs something that's significantly higher. You guys are both among the top backs in the league. What What does it mean to see that kind of trending upward? I think it's a testament to how hard, you know, not only myself, but guys like Bejian, like a lot of the other top backs, they work really hard to put a great product on the field in order to reflect that value. So, um, obviously still more work to be done, but man, um, that's awesome for Bejon, man. Shout out to Bean, man. You you earned it. You deserve it. >> Look at that number at all and think, okay, well, maybe I'm next up to get a deal done. >> Well, obviously you want to always be secured and locked in, but he deserved that for sure. like what him and his agent did with Atlanta. So I think when you start looking at the draft, you start to see kind of the the projections going forward. >> Jonathan, did you think the John domino was one that needed to fall for your talks to pick up? >> No, I think everybody's situation is different.
