No issues at all. >> And with Kim, I mean, he's he's been in a complex Brian Forest defense before. Does that certainly help, you know, kind of being able to speak the same language? >> Yeah, you can see his um mental focus. you could see his football awareness show up on, you know, play actions and things like that where most young guys will be up into the line. He kind of sees it before it happens. So, and then in terms of the, you know, the system at Georgia, uh, is a great one obviously and, uh, he's had no trouble at all picking stuff up. >> What have you seen from Bryce Ber so far? >> Um, you know, tough tough tough guy. Uh, again, another guy that's got good football instincts and IQ. Hard worker. Um, you know, he kind of doesn't flinch either, you know, so he attacks today like he is a veteran. Um, now he'll still make some things that shows you he's a rookie. Uh, but at the end of the day, I like where he's at, like what he's about, and he's going to help us this year. >> Seemed like the edge rusher had a really productive day today. What did you see from your vantage point? >> Um, you know, I just think we've got some veteran guys now. You know, uh, Ardan's played a long time in this league. lot two now uh going into year three, right? Um so that's good for him. Uh JT's done some nice things. The young kid Gums has showed up some. So uh I think that whole group overall is was good and they're working, excuse me, working together well and coach Hobby's doing a great job with those guys. >> I know we're only a day or a week into camp, so we still got a lot of time for you guys, but we've seen a lot of linebackers rotate through there. I think maybe six of your guys on first team reps. You guys still feel like you're early in that um observational phase trying to figure out who will stay out there or what have you seen from them? >> Yeah, I think it's super early, you know, as far as we're concerned. Football started yesterday when the pads came on. So, you know, we're going to just keep rolling those guys and and they all need to. It's a competitive situation, so we want to see how it all plays out. >> You feel better about that group this year than last year? Last year was kind of a revolving door, but now it seems that real competition. Yeah, I mean I think we had a good group last year. Um, you know, certainly with Z with all of experience and then followed up when Germaine came in with all his experience and you had two big grown men in there playing linebacker. Um, so I don't want to say anything negative about that cuz I was pleased with those guys all year. Um, but yeah, this is a bunch of young kids uh uh that that uh are vying for playing opportunities. >> With gums, with gums, you can really see the speed sometimes. Is that what stick sticks out so far? >> He's got a good get off. He's got some things obviously he's still young. He's got to work out in terms of how to rush by the quarterback, you know, can't get behind the quarterback, things like that. But, uh, so far so good. He's doing a good job. >> With not playing the last couple days, AJ kind of led to that spot on Thursday. What's impressed you most about him last? >> Um, AJ, you know, again, really puts the time in. uh he has uh done a really good job communicating as well as uh you know I can't you know he hasn't had a mental error to my recollection here in the in the first set of practices. So if he keeps that up that'll be good for him in his favor. >> How rare is that for a young guy to not have any mental errors this much? >> Yeah, it's pretty rare. Yeah, I mean there's going to be a bust here or there. I think he had one in the walkthrough. I don't count that. But out here he's been he's he's done well. That doesn't mean he's played um perfect because he should have helped Mooney on that deep ball today, but uh but uh but he was in the right spot. He just got to get there a little quicker. >> All right, thanks. >> All right, guys. Thank you guys. >> All right, how's everybody doing? I would assume that we're probably going to get a bunch of kicker questions. So, I'm just going to go ahead and talk about the kicking competition just big picture wise, like where everything's at. You know, as you look at things, um obviously everybody's able to view the live kicking sessions, which we've had two, and Blake's been 12 for 12 and Spencer's been nine for 12. So just looking at that piece of it. Um and obviously the live kicks are what we're going to look at the most important right now. Blake would be in the slight advantage. However, we're not going to be judged by anyone rep or any one day. We're not looking to I know that everyone wants immediate gratification or to name a starter soon. Like we're going to be looking at like the big picture. Who gives us the best opportunity to kick the best in preseason games? Who continues to get better and looks the best and is progressing the best to be the absolute best in regular season. So to be expected, there's been some little bumps in the road. As we've worked through the progression, we're going to try to kick these guys as much as we possibly can. For us, that's three times a week. We kicked on Wednesday on our own last week, the very first day of practice. That's the only day we would do it on our own. Like, we want to get them in front of the team as much as possible. That's intentional because we want to give those guys a day to kind of work with Luke and Rigo in the operation, expecting there's probably going to be some rhythm and timing things that they need to work through when they first get back. They both had a couple misses. just kind of working on her own, trying to feel things back out because it's been six weeks since they'd worked in a full unit. Friday then, hey, we want to see them make improvement from Wednesday to Friday. Um, you know, I think they both had one miss on Friday. Overall, they both kicked really good on Friday. Spence just missed one before practice. Um, and then he missed one or excuse me, groupy missed one before practice. Spence missed one in practice. As a whole, you know, I think they improved from Wednesday and that's what we want to see like keep progressing from day to day. I thought um you know groupy hit the ball really well on Friday throughout both sessions was hitting the ball true. He was a little bit quick and led to a miss early in the day, not in the live session, but then clean that up. I thought Spence hit the ball extremely well in pre-practice and was hitting the ball true, but wasn't necessarily doing that in practice, which we just we look at both of those different segments. So then we can see like overall how are they kicking and then is there a discrepancy between pre-practice and practice that we can isolate an issue, which I think we have with Spence. It's kind of like we saw with him last year in training camp. He got better as everything went on. I think he'll get more comfortable and smooth as we've gone on. He We came out this week, Monday was groupy, Tuesday was Shrader. They'll both kick Thursday, and then we'll split them both kicking Saturday and Sunday. So, that'll be their three times throughout this week. Groupy has been highly consistent. He came out um yesterday, looked really good again. Made all of his kicks in practice. Needs to get continue to keep building off that. Did not hit the ball as true. I think there was some variation in some of the kicks that he had yesterday. And you know, as part of the process, that's the first day we've been in shoulder pads. That seems like a small thing, but as the kickers put on the shoulder pads, does make them a little bit more topheavy, which can mess with their rhythm or lean into the football. I thought we had a little bit of variance at some of our kicks, even though we did make all of them on Monday. So, we'd like to see us take a step forward on Thursday with the shoulder pads on as we keep working to get smoother and better through that. Today, I thought Spence as a whole has kicked the ball well. He does have one little issue that we're kind of working through that he pulled two kicks similar to how he pulled a kick um last Friday. to be expected. Like he didn't kick for eight months. So, we're expecting there's going to be a little bit of stuff that he's got to feel through here in training camp and now he's just got to use his talent, use the really good mental makeup that I think he has to kind of work through some of those things being that he didn't kick for eight months and kind of progress through camp to be the best version and kicker of himself that he can be, which I expect to hopefully see some more progress into that on Thursday. >> How much do you take that injury into account when you're evaluating where they're at now? Well, as we evaluate it now, it would make sense that he's going to have some rust or some things that he needs to feel through, but by the end of training camp, we're going to be evaluating who's kicking at the highest level and going to give us the best chance in the regular season. >> How do you see your return of return? >> We have a really good for a 90man roster, we have a really good depth of returners, right? And we're just trying to get those guys, especially some of the younger guys, as many reps as possible so we can put them under fire and get them to progress forward. like um a guy like Dion Burks has not does not have a lot of return experience. We know there's going to be some hiccups. We're trying to get him as many reps as we can in practice, which no doubt will lead to some drops. He dropped a kickoff um yesterday. He dropped a punt yesterday but looked a lot better today. Like we're just going to get him as many reps as we can so they get more comfortable tracking the ball, playing with a square base, watching it all the way in. Um, but you know, we've got guys in addition to Dion that have a lot of experience doing it between Hagens and you got Gould and Coleman Owen and DS and Duelan. Like all those guys have really good experience doing it. And then we also in combination with that have some young guys like a Seth McGowan and Dion Burks that we just got to get more experience out of. But we have a really good crew of guys there that have experience and young guys that don't that we think we can develop. >> With McGawan, is it the decisiveness that kind of lends to him being your return? Yeah. So, I think he has really good instincts and feel like I think he'll be a guy that can set things up nicely. He has shown the ability to naturally track the ball, which some guys don't naturally have the ability to kind of track punts and kickoffs. He's done that. I think in the new kickoff model, sometimes it becomes a little bit of a rugby scrum. And you've seen the running backs because they are more physical to run through contact or run through the smoke have been a little bit more successful um throughout the league. So, I think you know him being a running back could fit the new kickoff model. You see Ashton Doulan's a little bit bigger guy with power that can run through contact. Amamira Abdullah last year for us, same thing. So, you know, running backs do have an ability to fit in this new model. >> Brian, how do you anticipate handling kickers in the preseason games? I mean, will it be sort of each guy get the game? Is it quarters or I don't know if you have >> Yeah, so in the past it's been halves. So, like one guy will get the first half, one guy will get the second half. Um, you cannot make that perfect. So, like in the first game, one guy's gonna get the first half, one guy's gonna get the second half. as we move to the next game, if one guy got a drastically different um number of kicks, we will then try to make it, you know, even out the kicks as we move forward as best we possibly can. And then we'll evaluate, you know, where they're at in the competition on whether or not it's going to be even or not from there. >> You're working in new guys at Protector and both gun spots, it seems. What are you seeing there? >> Yeah, so we we need a new PP. Last year's PP was Rodney Thomas, and Rodney was a first year starter for us last year doing it. But we feel confident that we have a a a number of guys that we can end up working in a personal protector, which is the guy that really kind of runs the show for the punt team. He stands in front of Rigo. Um calls to protection, somebody you have to, you know, count on to be smart to make those protection calls and checks, but also somebody you can hopefully get like as kind of a third gunner to release into coverage. Um that's been Trevor Denbo for us, that's been Rodney Thomas for us. We have six to eight guys that we've been repping. Uh Jonathan Owens has quality experience. He's a really good addition for us. um being that he's a nine-year vet that's played a lot of special teams, played defense, he's kind of a vocal leader, he's kind of the guy that's been running the most with the ones right now. And then there's a number of other guys that have been competing well with him. Hunter Waller being one of those top ones um that unfortunately just got banged up recently, but we'll certainly get back into that competition. Gunner-wise, it's pretty open-ended. We're trying to get as many guys reps as we can. Um I think Jonathan Edwards is really good. Obviously, Duelan, if he's playing more on offense, we got to develop and find that next guy. I think there's a bunch of different candidates between the receivers and the DBs that can do it.

title: Nakobe Dean, Jack Bech, Kwity Paye and Rick Dennison Presser - 8.4.26
text: All right, guys. Whenever you're ready. Rico, your starting offensive line's been pretty static the whole time. Same. Are is it just the ones are doing that well or is it everybody competing? What's your thoughts? >> Everybody's competing. We're just starting out. I mean, this second day in pads, uh, you know, for offensive line, you can't really tell how they're going to be in shorts. They need to have pads. They need to work together. So, in in our drills, we're working everybody with everybody, but uh we're just kind of starting out right now. And everybody's really working hard and competing, trying to get uh you know, the calls right, the derbiage, and then obviously the technique. So, we're we're not even through our install yet. So, we still got a couple more days of of putting our base stuff in and then we'll pull and and and keep moving guys around. Is there a level of importance with you on the offensive line to identify that group just in terms of communications and confident cohesion? >> Uh really I would hope they would all know it and they'd all work together. I mean it's certainly the uh the two next to each other working in combination have to feel pretty good, but like I said, we're mixing and matching them in the in the individual drills anyway. Um I think it's all tied with the center. The center ties both sides. He's got he's the biggest piece and we feel obviously really good about Tyler. So, he's done a great job as far as leading him uh not just by example but making calls and getting everybody on the same page. >> What would you say is the biggest challenge is picking up this offensive line blocking scheme right now. >> Um just just the feeling of the speed, right? We're trying to run off the ball. We're trying to get things going. Uh make the defense feel our speed and threaten all aspects of the field, right? We want him to carry all 55 sideline to sideline and we're just getting used to that right now and then feeling the speed. The second level guys we got on defense are fast. They can run but that's the way the NFL is so we got to get there. We had some guys that kind of reshaped the bodies in the offseason. Did a good job and and uh I think we're matching the speed pretty well. >> Just what's it been like seeing you know Clint Kubak you know run his first training camp as a as a head coach? I know you guys spent a lot of time together when he's an assistant, but seeing him in this role, what's been like seeing him operate? >> I think he's done a great job. I think he's got a clear message. There's no agendas. This is we're all trying to get better. Uh it's going to take all of us. I think he's done a really good job, but I kind of expected that when I decided to come here. That would that would be the only reason I'd come here because I felt really good about what Clink's going to do. >> We see Trey Zoo moving around a lot on on the line. How much of that is is wanting to see him play a lot of um see how versatile he is and how much of it is trying to find a spot for him specifically? >> I think it's just versatility. I think you guys got a a good skill set along with a lot of them. All right. I think a lot of guys can move around. Uh and we're just trying to see, you know, let him use all the skills he's got and see what looks best. And we're trying to find the best five. You know, I don't know what those are going to be right now. It's it's way too early to figure that one out. We got to play a couple games in my mind and when we do, you know, it's good to say, you know, Trey's played this spot or that spot. He's played a lot of spots. So, but I've had other guys play as many. You know, guards have both our guards have flipped back and forth. We have tackles flip back and forth. So, I think everybody's done a really good job of um kind of working their assignments in different sides. It it's it's not as easy as it as it looks. Just saying I'm going from the left to the right. Footwork is a lot tougher than you think. So, but he's done a good job and so the rest of them. >> Do you feel DJ Glaze still has, you know, untapped potential going to year three? >> Yeah, I really think DJ's really working hard. You know, every day is there's there's little things. I tell them all to, you know, work on one thing a day. Get one skill that you get better and, you know, we keep pointing out things that DJ's got to work on. And he does have, you know, great [snorts] length. I mean, he uses his arm arm length really well. Um, and he's working really hard at it. he's made some progress and he's, you know, but just like the rest of them, there's there's things we got to get better at. And I think focusing on those things, which each one of them doing, they're really they're really doing a good job of saying, "Hey, I need to be better at that." I mean, ask them after what' you do bad, what'd you do good, right? And it's never as good or as bad as you think it is, but as long as they're focused on getting better. That's all we're worried about. >> You're you're a tough coach. You don't play around. And DJ likes that. He wants that tough coaching. He when you How enjoyable is it with your experience to coach a young player that wants to be pushed? >> Well, uh, I don't think we have anybody in the room that that doesn't want to be pushed. That's why they're here. If if they were that way, they probably wouldn't be here, right? So, I don't know if I'm tough or not. I'm just me. If I told them, I tell them all the time, you know, I'm I'm gonna be mad at you make a mistake. If you make it twice, I'm really gonna be mad, right? And I'm going to have to give you and I I kind of lost a little bit today, but you know, it's important that they know that their jobs are essential for all 11 to do right. It's not just one guy. All 11 got to do something right. So, uh you know, we can't we can't just say, well, we're successful because one guy did it right. We all got to work together. That's why the five of them got to work hard. >> You're just kind of talking about how much Tyler really helps kind of the combinations getting everything set. When you look at those two guards next to him, you know, Jackson Powers and Spencer, how much do you think they've benefited from Tyler? >> Well, I don't think anybody won't benefit from Tyler. I mean, I think he's done a really good job. He's athletic and again, he leads, you know, he does all the drills and and uh but I think everybody on there has worked their tail off, right? I really do. I think they came in with a great attitude. We're going to get we're going to do the best we can. We're going to improve and get better every day. And uh you could see him strive for it right there. I was just talking to Richie. I had Richie in Buffalo and he said, "Man, those guys are working hard for you." So, good guys. >> What have you seen from Colton, especially coming off an injury or him stepping on the field now? >> I I think he's really, you know, in the spring you could tell he was just getting better and now I he looks like himself. He's using his length well. He's such a patient guy off the edge. He he does a really good job. So, uh like I said, he's got little skills that we keep working on. Hey, you got to get better at this and very receptive to that. They're all really open-minded and they and they do what you ask them. >> Coach, you mentioned yesterday that there's a lot of people in this building that want to get things turned around, change the culture, and you just mentioned you wouldn't be here if it wasn't for a certain expectation. How have you seen people in this building, team players in the locker room, try to change this around? >> Everybody I've come in contact is very positive about, hey, we are getting better every day. And that's that that was our reproach when we got when I got here in March. Each day signs for free agents, we got better. We got guys in the meeting room and taught them, saw how they learned. We're getting better, right? So, we went to the draft, we got better. So, we're getting better every day and we got to keep that pro uh process. >> What have you seen from JPJ? >> Uh, I've seen a guy that's very receptive. He wants to learn. Yes or no, sir. Tell him to do something, he does it the best he can. If he and and he corrects mistakes. >> He's been a great teammate. How do you manage building a consistent five with that chemistry while still rotating guys to find that best? >> Uh they they're they're all trying to be the best they can be for the team, whatever role there are, you know. Uh I think that's the big thing. It's a big we in our in our um our meeting room. They all talk about we watch individual we watch team I correct them they talk to each other you know the leaders like Colton and um you know he'll say with this is what I would have done you know you should think about this so those guys are have shared information uh I think they're just trying to get the best team out there >> couple more guys play and then maybe some roller coaster moments a little bit have you seen some consistency out of him >> I have I think he He's done a really good job in the offseason. Um, he studied really hard. He's one of the first guys to answer any question I I say in there and he's just, you know, consistent. I, you know, I wasn't here. I couldn't tell you what happened the last couple years. I know I evaluated him when he come out in the draft and I think he's done a great job. He's working hard, getting better every day. >> One more point. It looks like you're nose tonose with these guys on on the refs. I was talking to Colton about it and he said how much the the guys love just how right there you are. I guess where did that come from for you? Where has that always how it's been for you in your coaching career? >> Yeah, I mean you you I don't know how to do it any different, right? I mean, if you don't put your hands on them, if you don't, you know, you're not in and and I learned the game from from Alex, but I also look at it perspective. I played defense. What did I see on the other side? And I know what my vision was. I looked at, you know, just the gaps in in between in the backs and as a lineman, you know, there's not much they see past a 300 pounder sometimes. So, you know, you got to get in it. You got to understand what they're looking at and then talk to them. You know, shoot, even, you know, Tyler, he's had experience. Colton has all kind of experience. You know, I've done things a certain way, but if if they have a different way, I'll listen to it. If I like it, let's let's give it a try. If I don't like it, like I have some scars. I've tried it that way. It's not going to work. I don't like it. Right? So there's a lot of give and take with them, but you know, as long as we're all trying to progress. >> So, thanks. >> You bet. >> Hello. Hello. >> How's everything going? Two days with the pads on. You're a physical guy. What kind of What did this do for you today? >> Yeah, finally can play some real football. You know, finally put the pads on. Um, you know, a lot of the physicality of all the you know, that's one thing coach stresses a lot. you know, offense, defense to all the players. So, for all the for all of us to be able to come out here, really put pads on and play football for the first time as a unit and as a team, uh, it's been a lot of fun. >> What kind of growth do you feel like you've made from the leap you have from last year to this year so far? >> Yeah, just I think I should just shut off with the coaching staff and all the guys that have come in uh, you know, especially a guy like Kurt Cousins, you know, who brings so much knowledge uh, into the offensive room. you know, he comes in and he's such a good mentor for all of us. You know, just the knowledge he has of all the years he's played in the league. You know, he's seen every look a hundred times. So, he's really able to coach us through different looks, different reads of what he sees, how he wants us to do different things. Um, you know, the players to the offensive coaches, you know, we're all on the same page with everything he's saying. He wants us to see what coach Kubiaak and uh coach Noko are talking about. So, uh, you know, it's been really great to just have, uh, you know, some really awesome guys in here really leading us, you know, not only as players, but as men. >> What do you have to do to take that next step into that starting lineup and get planted? We know you've got the skills. Just curious what you think that next step for you. >> Yeah, you know, just keep fulfilling my role, you know, whatever that may be. Uh, you know, being a physical blocker in the run game, uh, you know, catching balls over the middle, making contested plays. Um, you know, that goes for everybody. you know, everybody got has to do those things. Everybody has to play their role. Uh, you know, so we can as a team take this team where we want to go. >> You fit well into this Clint Kubak style offense. So, what are kind of your activities, I guess, so far as you're still doing installs? >> Yeah. No, it's been awesome. You know, Coach Kubak, uh, you know, I love the offense that they run, the whole system that they have, you know, the different ways you can see different things and make changes throughout the plays. Um, again, like I said, just the knowledge that they have to be able to do all the things and all the run all the plays that they have, uh, has been really great. Uh, you know, I'm really excited for this year and it's going to be a really fun year. >> How do you go about just handling your business, not worrying about any kind of outside noise being a former second round pick, obviously high expectations. >> Yeah, you know, I think it's just day by day, you know, coming here, uh, you know, you listen to what the coaches say, you know, the good, the bad, the indifferent. you know, you go and uh each day you come in here with the mindset of growth to get better. You know, it doesn't matter. Uh you know, if you have a great day, if you have an okay day, whatever it may be. Um you know, just each and every day, you just got to come in here, you got to put your head down, you got to go to work. Um and again, you got to put the team first. >> Seen Malik Benson make a lot of plays so far in training camp. You know, as a year two guy, seeing a rookie come in, how have you been able to help him kind of splash on the field so far? >> Yeah, no, uh for sure. You know, Malik has been great. Um, you know, he's super fast, super twitchy. Um, you know, he's come in here, he puts his head down, he works super hard. Uh, he's super talented, he makes really good plays, he makes the big play. Uh, that's what we're counting on him to do, to come in here to push all of us. Um, you know, everybody in that receiver room to just push each other to grow and to be the best we can be each and every day we get out here. >> You talked about, um, the coaches have talked about the competition within that receiver room, specifically during the spring between you and and Dante. How do you feel the two of you have kind of pushed each other going into year two? >> Yeah, I think it's been great. You know, we were in here all off seasonason in the building. Um, you know, throughout the, you know, the the breaks that we've had, uh, you know, not only putting in the physical work, but the mental work and the playbook and all these things just so whenever we get out on the field, we can play as fast as we can. So, it's been really great. Um, you know, we continue to push each other. Like I said, everybody in that receiver room continues to push each other. Um, you know, we just can't wait to see where we can take this thing. >> What have your impressions been of of Fernando so far? and and playing with him. >> Yeah, he's awesome. You know, what you get is what you see. You know, he's a super good guy uh on the field, off the field. Has a super talented arm, super strong arm, super smart. Uh you know, one of the first guys in, one of the last ones to leave. Uh you know, always just trying to soak up as much information as possible. Um and it's just been really awesome to play with him, to get to know him. Um and again for to just keep seeing him grow each and every day. We're it's your second year playing alongside Brock, but we're seeing a lot more of those heavy set personnels with this Kubiaak scheme. Just how do you feel that helps your room and you specifically in the receiver? >> Yeah, you know, I think it helps everybody. You know, I think these coaches are really good at, you know, getting the guys and their abilities to really show what they're good at, to show out on the field. Um, you know, you just got to put your best guys out there, whoever that may be. Um, and go out there and let them make plays cuz, you know, that's that's what is going to take this team to that next level. Uh, like I said, the coaches have been amazing. Um, you know, I think the big sets, especially with Brock in there being like that tight end receiver. Um, you know, I think it gives defenses trouble. Just don't really know how to play Brock. So, again, I just can't wait to see where we can take this thing. >> We've seen you and some of your other rookie classmates, you know, going into year two being called upon um for bigger roles this season. Just as a group, do you take pride in being able to make that next step and and play a part? >> 100%. You know, it's a lot of hard work put in in the dark. Um, so and we have, like I said, a lot of great, uh, coaches who come in here and who push us each and every day. You know, they're not scared to call you out on the good, the bad, or the ugly. Um, you know, they just want you to be the best player you can be. So, this team can be the best team that we can be. Um, and again, I think that, you know, coaches have from top to bottom, really the whole building. Uh, you know, everybody's on the same page with that. And like I said, we just can't wait to, you know, we have we have a mission and we can't wait to go and accomplish that. Sorry if I missed this, but what kind of culture would you say Clint Kubak is establishing here and how much the players are buying into it? >> Yeah, definitely a team first mentality, a team first culture, you know, taking the eye and me, you know, out the building and just really focusing on a team first, you know, whatever coaches need from you, whatever that role that may be. Um, you know, you got to go fulfill that role. You got to give it everything you got. You got to give shocking effort. You got to come out here. How does this benefit the Chargers to come on down here? just wanted to, you know, just really wanted to and uh and did um the the organization wanted to, you know, the Spanishes wanted to. >> A lot of us, a lot of us, as I mentioned before, you know, >> Avery Smith pop off the last couple days. Obviously, no pass yet, but what stood out to you about him? >> The way he moves uh and his uh and competitiveness. uh you know him and Mr. Shelly uh both those two guys really really uh good movers and and competitors. Good to see him having a you know some real consistency. It's fun when you see guys do something once, twice, you know, little thing. Some people call it a little thing, but then when you start seeing them do it, uh, you know, repeatedly with consistently, okay, you do that well, you know, what can you do well over and over again, you know, that's how you get from, you know, one point to another. I mean, nobody just gets there like that, but uh, you know, you can really see the progress, you know, with those uh, with those young corners. Jim, have you had any thoughts of a longer stay next season to start camp or in the middle of camp? uh, sounds good. It's good thought. Uh, I'd be for that, but like a week or five days or something like that. >> Yeah, could be, I guess. I mean, uh, I don't know. We got to get back to the bowl, too. you know, we got uh got a preseason game coming up here coming up here soon and uh I know USD will be be starting uh you know, they're starting their football and their soccer. So, uh it's uh just tremendous gratitude for uh you know, them being so excited to have us and uh and willing to have us and uh you know, the preparing the the facility and the fields and uh you know, letting us be a guest. So, I guess um I'm just much gratitude for that and uh maybe just not overstay our welcome, you know, uh five or seven days probably be the the better plan the way I was raced, you know, like let's uh let's just be grateful for for the time that we have here. >> First day in pads today. Just how do you feel like the the practice went overall for you guys? >> I thought it was good. I didn't think there was any um you know, missteps. I don't think there was really a transition period between no pads and pads. I I thought guys reacted really well, played fast, and um you know, it was just like we've been out there for a while. >> You started practice with like eight straight completions. Do you feel like it was smoother at all today than it has been? No, I think it's uh you know just the hard work that we put in throughout OTAAS and into camp and um you know the the guys that we have running routes are are making special plays and when they're out there doing their job and you know everyone's working together um I think we can accomplish some some pretty big things. >> We've seen you target uh Trey Harris quite a few times here early in camp. Just what kind of growth have you seen from him year one to year two? >> Yeah, Trey's been awesome. Uh he's he's so reliable and I thought he had a great year last year, but we're expecting big things from him this year. He's he's made so many big plays already and um just we have so many so much confidence in him. Um we're comfortable with him. We know exactly where he's going to be, what he's going to do, and he's going to make some great plays for us. You >> saw you hit Lad for a touchdown over the middle in the red zone and seven on seven. What potential do you think he has in this new scheme? >> Yeah, a ton. Um you know, I think Lad is is about as athletic as it gets and and we've talked about it all camp and all of OTAAS of getting the ball to the receivers in a position where they can turn up field and make something happen. Um Lad would benefit hugely from that. I think getting him the ball quickly uh with his athleticism, how he's able to break tackles, miss tackles, and um just getting him up field, getting him the ball, he's going to do big things. >> How much stock do you put in seven on seven or do you put more into like full team drills where the entire defense is out there? >> Yeah, seven on seven can be beneficial. I think it doesn't show the entire picture with a pass rush and timing, but uh as long as you treat it like a a serious practice rep, you can get a lot of work in. Um, so obviously you'd love to have an offensive line out there, defensive line, but you can't always do that. And so getting that emphasis with the DBs and the receivers is really helpful, too. >> Last year you were very, you said you appreciated coming down here and getting to interact with the fans here. Just second year in a row. Just what are your thoughts about uh the atmosphere today? >> I think it's a really cool trip. I've I've really enjoyed it and especially this year. I think we're so thankful to ownership for allowing us to come down here and spend a couple days and really be a part of San Diego. And um obviously the fans care so much and like we we love to go play football wherever and and to be able to play it down in San Diego with so much culture and history um you know especially with the Chargers. I think it's a really great experience for everyone, young guys, old guys, and um a lot of the new guys that really don't know the Chargers history, but be able to to kind of share that with them. >> The tight end unit, we've seen him make a couple plays. just how how beneficial is it to have guys that have complimentary skill sets and just different skill sets in general >> uh in the tight end >> tight end room. Uh yeah, they're they're all able to do so many different things. You know, with with Charlie and David, um you know, they're able to run pass block catch routes and he's he's so versatile, too. And to have, you know, three, four guys like that, um it really helps us as an offense because we're able to ask so many different things of them and and they're able to pick up the offense so quickly. and to have those guys um you know being able to turn the ball up field too. If I get them the ball in a position where they're able to turn up field, they're able to make break tackles, miss tackles, and um you know, it's it's definitely good to have those guys. >> There's a lot of fans from from Tijuana. What can you say about the fans from Tijuana to come support you guys here? >> It's awesome. You know, I I think this is such a cool area and for us to be able to share this experience with so many people that love football, love the Chargers. Um you know, it's a great opportunity. It's it's it's fun. It's cool to be able to reach out and meet with some of the people today and um you know I think it's one of those opportunities that we don't get a whole lot but we need to appreciate when we do. >> Justin obviously football is a physical sport. Um saw Sean go out uh hopefully everything is okay. It looks like something minor but when stuff like that happens is it just I mean how do you fight uh oh here we kind of go again or the heart you know skipping a little of a beat when your left tackle goes out like that? you know it's the unfortunate part of the NFL. uh injuries and adversity and it's how you deal with it and and we know that Rashan is doing everything he can to be at his best and sometimes, you know, unfortunate things happen. But, uh we know he's going to he's going to get back out there as quickly as he can. I'm sure he wanted to be back out there. He probably was trying to get back out there and they probably limited him, but uh you know, he's a competitor and and we've got nothing but respect for him. >> Did you get a chance to check in with him or have a chat with him at some point? >> Yeah, briefly. I talked to him a little bit. any update from him you could >> uh pro probably not from me if uh if you maybe if you ask him but uh I don't want to I don't want to speak for him. >> Well, you're smiling, so hopefully that's a good sign. >> He he said he wanted to be back out there, so I think that's that's okay. >> No med school for you. >> No, glad football worked out. >> Is your comfort level in the offense ball from OTAAS to where you're at now? And then what are some levels you need to get to, you know, before the season starts? >> Yeah, I think the more reps the better. Um, you know, I think in OTAAS, we we did everything we could to to master the footwork, master the offense, and now we're just going out there and playing fast and and letting the ball fly around and and I think that's what's important for camp is uh to just go play football like you're reacting and and playing in a game and treating those reps like real game reps. Um, and so I thought OTAAS went well picking up the the smaller details of the offense and all of the timing routes with with the receivers, but now it's kind of time to fine-tune those details and I think it's been really helpful so far. >> There's a competition for the starting spot at left guard. We've seen a bunch of different guys rotate there. How [clears throat] does that rotation at left guard impact continuity on offense, if at all? >> Um, I I think that's probably a decision for the coaches. I think right now my main focus is is playing quarterback and doing my role and u making sure that I'm playing in timing, getting all the motion, snap points, everything like that. And um you know, I'm sure there's a time and a place to discuss it, but uh with me right now, I'm focused on my job. >> What What makes um Mike McDaniel's play action game unique? >> Uh yeah, it's a good a good question. I think uh just the way he makes everything look the same where runs are the same as the pass concepts and um you know the defense the plan is to never really let them settle in and get comfortable and understand that you know here could be a run, here could be a pass. And if the offense is able to do all of those things, you know, the defense is always on their heels and not quite sure what's coming. And so we as an offense have the advantage of we know when the ball is being snapped, we know what we're running and um I think he really does a good job of maximizing that. >> Reed has said, >> sorry, >> Andy Reed has said a coach's third year he has found tends to be pretty determinative of whether it's going to succeed or not the way they want. What has Jim done in two years and what do you see from him this year that maybe is going to help you guys go where you want to go? Coach Harbaugh is given us everything. He's uh such a fantastic leader, such a fantastic coach, and um a guy that everyone on the team respects. He loves football. He loves his teammates. He loves the players that he coaches. And um everyone works harder, wants to fight harder and play harder for him. And um you know, we've got nothing but love for him, nothing but respect. >> So, how it feels? >> It felt good a little bit to get a little thuds, get off blocks. Uh you could tell it feel like football more. So, uh I'm happy to put the pads on for sure. It looked like uh Clink was getting after even you kind of were talking to DBs after the first period where Justin had a bunch of completions. Did it I don't know did it it felt like more intense today. Did it feel that way to you? >> No. Yeah, it definitely felt more intense and um I feel like every day we take the field. We we got a standard in our room and uh Coach Clint, Coach Fuller, and all those guys do a great job of expressing that and I feel like our offense is making a lot of plays and we just wanted to be tighter and make more plays. So we we know our standard so we picked it up and um it was a great practice. >> I know that standard is to win those reps um and nothing less than that. But are you do you have any can you find the appreciation and when when Justin's throwing the ball like that and >> definitely um I feel like he he's making those throws on time. He's throwing guys open. Uh so to be able to go against an offense like that, it's helping us and we can't even be a step slow. So uh that's why we expressing like hey if you can make the plays on those plays, you can make any plays. So, we're just trying to stay connected on the back end. >> Typically, this time of year, is the defense ahead of the offense or or vice versa? >> Uh, yeah, usually this time of the year, the defense, cuz I feel like defense, we're more reactive. Offense is more timing and um they're they're starting to find their timing and um it's going to be great. Like I said, they've been giving us great looks. Um and to be able to go against a complex offense like that, I feel like it's helped our defense a lot. Also, >> how'd you feel about the way you guys got after the quarterback today? obviously couldn't finish, but between blitzing and the guys up front, how'd you feel about it? >> Uh, I felt very confident about it. Um, um, just being able to put pressure. You know, we can't stay, we got to stay away from the gold jerseys, but so everybody can't really see it, but um, guys are rushing good. Keem, Khalil, everybody's rushing, bud. Everybody's rushing good. So, man, I'm excited when it when we do go live. >> Are you excited about a one of those rookies that's coming in? Just what have you kind of noticed from him? >> Uh, twitchy, explosive. uh he he can set the edge, he can he can kind of do everything kind of like Tulie, he can do everything. Uh so those guys are going to be very good and I can't wait to help rush with him. So yeah, I can't wait. >> First uh day in pads, obviously Mike McDaniel, I saw him come over to you. Did was he joining a little bit since the first day in pads or >> Oh yeah, he was he was talking so much trash after that first period, especially when they completed the boss. He's like, "All right, three. There we go. Three. Let's go. Let's go." So it's fun. It's competition and um I love going against those guys. >> In terms of getting after the quarterback, um what does a fraction of a second mean to you on the back end there? >> Uh it means a lot. That's that extra pump. That's from me being able to transition out of my pedal. Uh that's a difference between a tackle, a PBU, and a pick. So just those steps matter, every inch matter. And uh when you can get the quarterback to hold it, it gives it buys us more time to close to the man. Uh so it's just good. working with your coach um just before you guys took the field going over some calls. Yeah. >> Um where did that attent for you where did that attention to det I mean you're minutes away from going out on the field and you said like you thought to yourself, hey, let me get one more refresher before we start this practice. >> I feel like uh the details are so important and I feel like sometimes you can't never shy away from the details and um fundamentals I feel like uh is what's kept me in this league so long. So, just being able to make sure I'm able to make the calls, put us all on one page, and um be able to make sure my technique is good. >> You going to look at Kendall's pick? >> Oh, yeah. That was nice, bro. He he snagged it. That was nice. Her gunn it in there. It was nice. But like I said, it's competition, man. Um like if he's not that close, like it's a catch, so it's like, man, that's that's the windows he's throwing. And u man, it's it's good to go against. >> Do you know what the that quick whistle is after the snap? What do they >> that uh that's that's for the front so they don't go too crazy and and you know what I mean pile up on top of each other. But that that has nothing to do with the back end guys. We got to cover. We got to cover. We still got to cover. They they tell us ignore that whistle. So that that ain't for us. >> We seen Avery Smith, rookie, make a bunch of plays so far. Saw him with get a rep with the ones today. Just what have you seen from him through the the spring and summer? >> Oh man, confident swagger. He's throwing on the seat belt after he makes a play. Uh uh so I like his swag man. I like I like uh he's from Toledo, man. Uh he got a lot of confidence and uh he don't shy away from any competition, man. Uh he very smart, intelligent player, man. >> And wanting to rush with the other guys on the first play of team. You obviously play and got in there. How much do you like setting the tone that way? >> Oh, I love it. I love it. Uh obviously you can't set the tone by getting the quarterback to the ground, but I I can envision I this is my ninth year. I can envision making the play. Uh so, uh I love rushing the quarterback. I love covering. I love doing it all honestly. I've seen players when they retire, multiple players when they retire >> have been asked and you see these things online, who's the hardest guy, hardest hit you've ever taken. Yes, sir. >> And guys will say Derwin James this situation. Yes, sir. >> Do you see those things? Do you >> Yeah, I see. I see. I got >> I see I got social media. I got see I mean my brother's on it. They sending it all the time. But, you know, I try to just go out there and just continue to do my job because, you know, I mean, when people are saying that, that mean that you got a target on you, too. So, they're going to try to come with their best. So, always stay ready so you don't got to get ready, you know. >> Being back in San Diego for a second year, what's it mean to just like see this fan base and I know this was story history. >> Oh, man. The fans are loud down here. They was loud. They so much support. We look around, they packed it out today. We love We love the fans, not only LA, but everywhere, man. All over the world. But to see the fans come out and how much support we had, it meant a lot to a lot of players, especially coach Harball as well, too. >> I know it's your birthday, too. Happy birthday. As far as birthday presents go, putting on pads for the first time all season, where where does that stack in like gift rankings throughout the year? >> That's like the best birthday gift ever. Just going to go play football. I love playing. I My birthday always fail during the season or like when we in camp, whether it's college or high school. So, being able to go play football on my birthday, it feels good. talk about Avery Smith. Just do you feel like kind of the competitive culture you guys built in the room and just the team overall has helped like young guys, young DBs just come in and like contribute or make plays right away? >> Yeah, it goes back to Chris question when he said like how coach Clint, you know, everybody like the standard is the standard, man. And um I feel like ready a rookie, ready in year nine, ready in year five, I feel like uh everyone's going out there compete. We got a lot of depth, a lot of guys that can make a lot of plays. So, um, man, when they're number call, guys are stepping up. So, it's good to see. >> What What has Harbaugh brought to the teams since I mean, you were here before and after. What has he brought and why do you think this year it goes higher? >> I say he brought us a culture. He brought us a standard. He brought us a um he brought us a lot, man. Identity, honestly. And, um, to be able to be year three with him, it feels good. It feels right. And, um, I can't wait for the world to, you know, kind of see what we got building up this year. Did he do things that made you think this year will be even better? >> Uh just by him being consistent. Um uh the more the more um the more he imp implement like everything the standard and how he how he see the vision, how he see us, I feel like uh we just trying to you know live up to that. [music]

title: Jadeveon Clowney presser on August 4 | Full Q&A
text: I know. When you left here, did you imagine that you would be back and now that you are? >> No. >> But I'm glad to be back. Uh having fun. Great team, great defense. Trying to chase that Super Bowl with the Texans. I feel like it's a great opportunity for me, my family. Uh you know, just enjoying it. when it comes to that and playing with these guys Junior. What do you think third down look like? >> I mean, it's going to be very special, man. Uh, they got some dogs already. I know me coming in can help them guys, you know, so they don't burn out, make it look the same when I'm out there. Uh, I think we got to we can put stuff together and we can dominate up front. >> I'm just looking forward to that. >> This team is very talented. What is it about head coach that makes you want to play? It's energy. Uh same guy. He exciting. He come in there with a smile on his face every day. Just fun guy to be around and it's it's it it trinkles off into the team and everybody else can feel it and you know they make practice a lot easier here. Make the day go by fast. >> You've accomplished a lot in this league, man. Why why are you still out here >> and maybe just a little bit more why this is this is the right opportunity with a great team. >> Yeah, like I said, my whole thing was to chase the Super Bowl this year. Uh, no better place for me to do it here. I think they had great great defense last year. I said if I can go there, help my guys. It was about the money cuz I could have went other places for a little bit more money than this. But I'm like, it's year 13. I started here, go back here and try to win there and see how, you know, rest of my career go. But it's been a great run, man. It's been great. I've been having fun with it. >> Is this the last time? >> We don't know. Can't speak on I go year by year, man. you know, but I'm I'm going enjoy this one. >> What's the difference? What's the biggest difference between you when you walked in the first time and you now? >> I'm grown. >> Uh uh yeah, man. I I was a big kid at first when I first got here. I grew up different than a lot of these guys, man. I told people my when I was born, you know, my dad was in jail, grew up a single parent home, man. I grew up a lot different. So, I got here was never seen Houston. I enjoyed it during my time and yeah, it was fun. I got I came with some great guys, group of guys when I got here. But coming back now, you know, I'm a vet in the locker room, a lot older, a lot smarter than I was before and you know, just enjoying it, taking it day by day. >> So, what kind of what kind of OG are you are? Are you going to be more vocal or you just kind of >> I'm a more pull guys to the side. Hey, bro. You know, talk to them like that. But, you know, I speak up too when I see something. But you know, I like I said, man, I'm just here to help. Like if them guys need advice or something, I always say, "Hey, bro, do this or do that." They be like, "What you think OG?" I be like, "Hey, bro. That's how I think." This what worked for me. It might not work for you, but that's what worked for me throughout my career. And uh, you know, I just give them advice on every day how to take care of their bodies or, you know, what to do if I see something out there on the field, what to look for certain personnel or anything. >> So, it hasn't been long, but I mean, it's been long since you've been here. You haven't been in the building long, but how much of has the culture changed or things changed around here? >> Yeah, the building changed a lot. Uh, in a good way. Very, very good way. It's a lot lot easier, a lot relaxed in that building than it was when I first got there. Uh, coaching staff different. It's fun. It's a little bit more fun. The group of guys in that building is is great. It's just been easy to go back up in there than I than I expected when I got when I signed back. But like I said, that's that's because of Demo, the guy that's running the running the show. He put a lot of great guys around him, coaches, and uh you can feel the energy and all the other guys can feel it. So, I know a great thing is going to happen here for for me and the team. So, I'm just looking forward to the opportunity. >> Christian circle moment. Yeah. >> Has it kind of sunk in and have you gotten a lot of texts from people that know you've been wanting to play for the Texans for a while? >> I think it sunk in the day when I was jogging on the field. I was like, "Oh man, it's crazy to be back. All the fans saying, you know, cheering for me." I was just excited about that. It's just a great feeling. You know what I'm saying? That after all these years to come back and they still got love for you and u happy that you back here, man. Uh like I said, it's a blessing. My career started off rough. Y'all know injury after injury. First game of my career. I just been fighting back ever since. And to play 13 years, to be in my 13th season, I just thank God for that. Uh, man, it's just been a long ride, you know, and I'm glad to be here. >> Talk about the player you are now and what how do you see that fitting here? What does that look like? >> Oh, man. Like I said, I still got a lot to give. I can make plays. We all know that. >> Uh, just coming in giving my leadership, like I said, and I see Will lead and I tell him, "Hey, bro, you're doing a good job leading." You know, uh, Denil, like it's an older group. We're a lot older than what people think. And it's working because we all speak up. We all say stuff to each other. Nobody gonna let nobody slack off. You know what I'm saying? And that's the respect that we have for each other in that locker room and that group. So that's why I say I can see the talent. I don't been on seven other teams. So I know what it look like. So I know what a winning coach look like. So I know we're going to win a lot of games here. That's a fact. Uh it's the way we work and the way we hold each other accountable since I've been here since day one. So I'm just looking forward to it. >> This is getting a little bit different. And I know you live here and stuff. The heat, the sun. [laughter] >> Yeah. Uh thing is I've been training here for the last 12 years, but it still hit different. I did three plays today. I told him it felt like six or seven. But uh that's just getting back into football shape. All that running. I'm going text my trainer today and say, "Man, we did all that running for me to get tired today in like four plays." But but nah, that's football shape, man. I just got to work. That's what training camp for. You know, as y'all know, I've been missing training camp for some years. So, I was excited to get out here in training camp and knock the rust off earlier this season than I did in the previous year. So, I was looking forward to this getting to know the guys early instead of walking in week one. Hey man, learning the scheme on the fly. You know how many times I did that? I did it in Baltimore, Seattle, Dallas, Cleveland, no training camp. Walk out there and just play week one. And I look across the line, somebody telling me, "Hey, you know what I'm saying? >> [laughter] >> But but it's going to be a lot different this year because I'm I'mma learn the playbook before the season start. Man, it's it's going to be a lot lot smoother season for you guys. >> Excuse me. >> So you finally got your number 90 back. Was there any finagling with that cuz >> No, man. When I walked in, he was like, "Hey, you can get 90 back." I was like, I don't even know if I wanted at first cuz the last time I've been injured, I wore 90. You know what I'm saying? Ever since I left, I've been weighing all these other different numbers and it's been great, man. It's just fun to be back. Like I said, I'm excited looking for the opportunity. >> What did the first two days here look like for you? >> And then I u I want to ask too like u you know, why did you make the decision to start earlier uh versus what you had been used to? >> Uh like I said, I made the decision because I wanted to learn a scheme, man. I didn't walked, like I said, I walked into too many teams of the first week. And you know how hard it is to play when you don't know the scheme. You play a lot slower than you normally want to because you got to look across the field. Somebody got to tell you what to do. You know what I'm saying? I done been doing that for so many years throughout my career. So, I just said, "Let me just go to this training camp with these guys and grind with them so they know. I ain't just here for no play around. And I'm here to work with these guys and get to know them, build a relationship so they can have a great season. >> First two days look like >> first two days. >> Yeah, first two days. >> A lot of physicals, a lot of hand shaking and a lot of smiling. [laughter] >> Last year you played 44% of the snaps for Dallas >> and you end up having eight and a half sacks and I think it was like a sack every hundred snaps for pass snaps. What do you feel like your role can be here as far as how they utilize you and keeping you fresh? >> I'm just like I told them, man, I think it's not just my me being fresh, but Will and Denil being fresh, too. Also, man, that rotation could be great when you going to have guys just flying off the ball and no fall off and it look the same as like play one. You know what I'm saying? So, that's the that's the effect I was thinking in my head like, hey, them guys can go, I can go. They need a break, I'm in there and make it look the same. So we just keep putting pressure on the quarterback and giving our secondary chance to make plays. >> Do you remember your first game against CJ? >> Yeah, I missed two sacks on that joke. >> Yeah, I missed him. I told him I missed you on the sack one last year. My first That's what happened when you walk in week one and you rusty and you don't get no no training camp. So like I said, that's why I came here now. >> Trying to knock the rust off a little earlier so I can make some plays this season. title: Mike Tomon presser on August 4 | Full Q&A
text: Um, well, hey, good morning everybody. Appreciate you being here. Hope everyone uh is staying nice and hydrated. I can uh we can fire away. We can just jump into it. >> What are some of the um you know, I I think right now we're we're really excited about the progress. Um we're looking forward to the groundbreaking at the end of the year. We're uh as I was just sharing, we're excited to move this camp. You guys are going to love your new setup um to the uh to the Toro district in 2029. So, you know, we're focused on it. Um got a lot of momentum and we're working through with Howard Hughes and and the county. I will tell you, Aaron, um we'll have a foundational announcement here in the next couple weeks. So, kind of watch this space. Um, but we have a lot of momentum going on. Um, and excited to keep unveiling it as we go. >> Speaking of momentum, um, what can you reveal some of the things that you all have planned for this special season that you have coming up? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I think we have, um, going into, you know, our 25th season um, at Reliance. We have, um, Liberty White out coming out, which as as y'all may know is Mrs. McNair's um favorite game and so we're excited to celebrate her uh on that game and then we'll have a series of events to celebrate the 25 years um with the families including unveiling of a new rivalry jersey. So we have a number of different things that we're excited that all come together for this special season. >> Now sorry question was about the the stadium renovation andor new stadium. Is there any progress or timeline on that >> on the new stadium? >> So, stadium development here, you know, we continue to work um with the rodeo and the county. We've had really productive um conversations as we're looking at all options as it as it focuses here on Reliant. What I can tell you specifically or just reiterate is our focus is here with Reliant, with the rodeo. like those are our those are our two knowns as we're looking for what the best options are here. >> You learn anything about the stadium or how it operates anything like that during the World Cup? >> I'm pretty familiar with where the stadium is. I think I think the uh um you know the sports authority, the sports corp. I think the entire city did a really nice job bringing together with the World Cup. Thought Houston looked great. Um, so a ton of appreciation for all those running the venue that put us in a great spot. Um, and transforming it into a great stadium we can all be proud of. Um, at least on a world stage. >> Do you trade notes with those with FIFA at all? You know, when they're coming in, they're going to do all their things and they've got a different perspective on things. Did you did you learn anything from them specifically about just operations driven? >> You know, I think they're experts on how they like to hold events, you know, and so there's a specific way FIFA likes to hold an event. And so we've been working very closely with them certainly for really years coming into this uh and then really doubling down as we got into months. Um and I'd like to say we have a world-class team on our side that part of being a world class team is always learning. Um so we appreciate the engagement there for sure. Mike here was talking about the state of the stadium groups that got done this all season. Where as far as things you guys still want to see, but what are some of the things you guys do and upkeep with the stadium? >> Yeah. Hey, you know, the county runs the upkeep um on it and it's an old stadium at this stage as it relates to stadiums. Um and so they're they're making sure that they're investing to to make sure it's a safe place to to watch events. You know, what we're really excited about um as it relates to investment in the building is our premium experience this year. Um, you know, we look at the city of Houston as one of the real big benefits that we have as an overall organization and part of that has to do with the corporate community. You know, we have this robust corporate community and so we're excited to roll out options for that corporate community to to make sure this is a relevant place for them to come and conduct business to make sure it's something that everyone is proud of. And so with the BMW Lonear Ballroom and the M Club Blue, it is a new all-incclusive space that's tucked down in the, you know, the bowels of the stadium right where the opposing team is getting ready to take the field to be able for the first time to bring clients and fans to that type of proximity to such a special moment in the game. We're really excited to roll that out. We're also excited to announce a culinary partner who is Michelin recognized, James Beard recognized, rooted here in Houston. So, we're going to announce that later. But what I'd share with that is for the corporate community here in Houston or just, you know, super fans. Um, we'll have a unique place that they can entertain. I would also tell you to, you know, we're excited to to launch the the H-Town Loge Boxes, which is a semi-private Loge box in the bowl of the stadium. um where you know those who want to entertain but still be in the bowl itself. Here's an exclusive way to do that with four to six members. And so when you talk about investments in a stadium, I think those are two really big steps up um for our overall fan base. >> You mentioned you mentioned um you know still weighing your options. I'm curious what in particular are you focusing on in regards to that? In regards to stadium and and you have a specific timeline on when y'all would like to make a decision. >> So for the stadium, >> yes. >> Um, you know, we're going through the process and trying to make sure what's optimal. You know, we really we really feel that we're sitting on this pretty unique opportunity. I think as I've shared in the past, it's like right now we're sitting essentially on 350 contiguous acres um in what's soon to be the third largest city in the United States on some major arteries. And so right now it's an event-based space. Um over 750 events a year come through here. So that's a good halo. But we really feel that this can be something more than that. And so when you think about using and having this space being really kind of a 365 day a year destination, I think that's an option. And so those are the types of things that we're exploring together with the rodeo um and certainly the county. And so we're we're going through that process. Um you guys are well aware of all the different studies that have been conducted on different parts of the park to lead, you know, give us some light on to where to go. Um, and so we're uh we're excited on the progress at this point. Hey, it'd be great to have a decision yesterday. Um, but the reality is we have several years um until there's a real need to to have definitive direction on it. Um, so we're trying to make sure we're thoughtful with the time and our stakeholders. When you talk to the to the league and when you say give you some feedback, does that also include, you know, the prerequisites of what goes into being able to host the Super Bowl? They do they finally evaluate your stadium and say whether or not they can host the Super Bowl here again because there's a lot of state-of-the-art and new stadiums being built, you know, continuously around league. >> Yeah, there is. You know, it's a it's uh the NFL is competitive um sports franchises in the United States and globally. It's competitive and it competes on all sides. training facilities, your venue, the field, the equipment, how you put your team in a position to win. Um, and so you have to take in all of those pieces because it is so competitive. I think what's really important to us are big events like that. I think that's unique that we can draw those types of events to Houston. And so it's absolutely a consideration when I say being thoughtful with all the stakeholders there that that is a long list of very important stakeholders on how can we benefit this overall area and part of it is you know big events like that that help drive jobs that help drive the retail that help drive hotel nights etc. And so that's a big one and that's part of the reason that we're taking time to make sure we're being thoughtful on what's the best way to bring all that together. What do you consider the biggest hurdles for a grass stadium in here? It's obviously a multi-use stadium, multi-purpose, multi-tenant, cost, upkeep, all that stuff. What do you consider the biggest hurdles for grass inside NR? >> You know, two things. I mean, how the building's built at this point? Um, you know, there's new technology that allows that to come in um on a more uh frequent basis. We don't have that technology. Um, and we're a busy stadium. That's a good thing. Um, but we're a busy stadium. You know, FIFA shut down the stadium for over a month of like no activity getting that ready. We we don't have that luxury. Um, we have the circus coming in. Um, so we have different events that are coming in and we're a tenant in the building and so they're doing a great job keeping the the stadium busy and um we're just focused on making sure it's ready to play on Sunday or Thursday or Monday, etc. >> Now that you've been here a year, what do you think of the state of the team, the football product, kind of where the team stands as far as being competitive, being a contender? Sorry, Eric, you say that's right. You've been here for a year now. What do you think about the state of the team as far as being a contender, being a competitor? Uh what are you seeing out there? >> I mean Nick and Demo are doing everything uh I mean everything to take us to the next level. Um, we we have such a great approach of step by step right now. And I think you guys are here, you can feel the energy and the intensity that the team is approaching every single step in the process. And so with that, you know, you have a ton of confidence and excitement for u the season and and to get to the home opener. I know that Doug has a great creative mind and I also know he has a great creative team, but how much do how much info do you get to put in into some of the things that goes into, you know, the marketing side, uniform side, things like that? >> Did did Doug tell you to say that? >> Um, you know, it's it's a team engagement. Doug um and his team are, you know, I really think they're world class talents when they think about branding, how they think about branding. I think that'll be showcased coming up here with the rivalry uniform. Um, this will be the most Houston centric uniform that we've had to date. I think people will be really proud. Um, all Houstononians will be proud of what's represented there and what they've captured. Um, I would tell you he has great leadership on that side. They they they let me in the room. You I can weigh in. Um, as do as do the McNairs. So, you know, it's a it's a collaborative internal approach. We got a couple more. >> Mike, on the uniform question with it, uh, do you have a specific date that you're going to avail? Can you tell us when you'll have the role uniforms? Get that question a lot from fans. >> Yeah, I mean, we're we're working through it. It's kind of uh in flex of how early you can release it. You know, the league does a good job of trying to manage all the messaging the way through and so there are a couple moving parts. So, we don't have that yet. Um, but we'll be excited to share details when we do for sure. You mentioned all the options for the stadium. Said that focus on a renovation. Is a new stadium an option now or there? >> You know, we've been focused on a renovation. Um we uh but I I'll tell you we've been exploring all options. You know, there are a number of different studies that are either conducted or have come out that have um shed some light, but you know, we haven't really changed our our overall approach at this point. given his proximity to the locker room of three opponents. Uh the BMW space has a kind of a Wilson Gman alliance kind of thing. Talk about the creative process that goes into creating space like that for sponsorships and what goes into that. >> Yeah, I mean I think it comes down to fundamentals. I think the great thing is from a purpose standpoint, we are maniacally focused on cultivating and delivering a world-class experience. So you start going like well what is world class? And so you look around the globe, you look at other experiences that other venues are presenting and that starts to help inform you on those pieces. And then you start walking your venue, you know, you start looking at what's actually possible here. Um, and that's a big part of it as well. And then you have to look at being relevant to your market. You know, not every product is relevant to every market. We happen to have a world-class city. And so when we think about what is the top end, what is the most exclusive, um that makes sense on a global stage to bring that here to Houston. And then of course we want to lead and so we like to push the boundaries and we really feel we've done that. When you think about the consumer experience um and the partnership with BMW for Mub Blue to pick them up at their home in uh M series and bring them to the actual game, those are unique experiences that don't exist right now. Sports Business Journal came out and said that we [clears throat] would be one of the top five VVIP experiences um for 2026 this season coming up. And so we have to go execute it and we have a great team on the execution side. Juan Rodriguez and his team brought it to life after we had the vision and put the rigor behind it. But there are a lot of pieces that go into bringing these things together. >> You guys good? >> All right. Thank you everybody.

text: Great football. >> Uh, risk get richer, man. Risk get richer. Obviously a great player. Uh, he started his career here. First round pick for a reason. U had a really good career.
