I mean, it's something I always do. I think um I've just gotten more comfortable sharing it because I think uh my mindset kind of changed towards it because you understand that when it's people and underserved that are underserved and kind of overlooked. For me, being one of those people at a young age growing up, you know, you you don't want somebody to always be showing your struggle. But I think for me realizing a lot of the issues just in the US, across the world, I think us in the United States, we're so sheltered, you know, we have our own issues as well, but uh relative to just like how the world is. I think we just we're kind of in our own little world sometimes. We don't realize the basic things, you know, having food, water, you know, uh four walls and a front door. We take these small things for granted, myself included. Um, so I think it's just highlighting it a little more to give perspective to people who maybe don't have the opportunity to go different places and experience what other people across the world and even right down the street maybe where you think is a nice neighborhood or whatever and you go right around the corner and there's somebody dealing with something that you had no clue. Uh, so just kind of to open up everybody else's vision as well who may not have the opportunity or know what's going on around them or other parts of the world. >> I'm sorry. a little bit to that point. You've kind of opened up yourself to be a little bit more vulnerable in some interviews it seems like recently this off season too. Is there any particular reason as why you might feel a little bit more comfortable doing that? >> Uh yeah, I think it's just, you know, the older I get and the more experience you have in life, you just realize everybody is hiding something. Everybody's dealing with something. Everybody's going through stuff. There's no person even in this room or anywhere in the world that just lives in a utopia life. you know, we all have struggles and I think everybody is so worried about trying to, you know, put uh makeup on a pig and the reality is like, bro, like we're all human. So, there's something that you're dealing with that's different from somebody else but similar to the next person and it's something I'm dealing with that you don't know about, you know? So, I think for me, you know, especially being in the position that I'm in, you realize if if I'm able to open up and be vulnerable about that, it might influence other people who are like, "Dang, like I thought this guy signed his big old contract, you know, he's young. He got he got all this stuff going for himself. His life must be great." So, when you open up about your own experiences and the own things that you're dealing with, even in the midst of all these great things, it just puts it in perspective for other people who might feel like, man, you know, this person, if I was here, I'd be living a great life. If I was that person, man, I my life would be better. And just realize, man, we all just trying to figure out life. We only live one time. Uh we all go through things. So, I think it's more so just to again perspective for other people to realize like, hey, I'm no different than you. Uh I go through things good, bad, and different just like everybody else. >> Man, I I told I told you guys I think in OTAAS, uh one, you know, he went to Middle Tennessee State. I know like Georgia Tech likes to probably claim him, but that boy is Conference USA all the way. You know, we talked about it when we first got here. You know, for me going to FAU, you know, just you got love for those guys and he plays that way, too. He plays like with a chip on his shoulder, plays the game the right way, works hard at that position, it doesn't take a whole lot of talent. Like obviously talent will take you really far, but I feel like especially early on before you even know all the techniques and all that, it's more of a mindset. You're the first you're the first line of defense for the quarterback. Uh, and you've got to have the right mentality and I think he does that. >> Last week you uh, just to follow up on that real quick, last week um, you and him, you know, were entangled with each other. He drove you to to the sideline, but you got up and you were like excited. Is that the type of uh, mindset that you want to see, especially from your offensive lineman like that? >> Yeah, for sure. I think it's funny because it's like first day or I want to say it might have been the first day uh and we're we're going on and obviously we don't got pads on so I always feel bad punching him in the chest with no pads and he's bringing it and I'm like okay he's bringing it so I guess I got to make sure I bring it so uh it was just good because you know just the mentality in general like pads no pads know he's just trying to work hard and know most thing I always talk to him about is just working smart that's a different level of being a pro I think I'd rather tell you to slow down or be smart than to tell you, "Hey man, you got to pick it up." So, I feel like for to see him doing that, you know, I got up and I was okay, so I'm not mad at it. You know, I play the game hard, too. So, uh, for me, especially knowing him as a rookie and what he's trying to accomplish and what our team is trying to accomplish, I was happy with it. real something about real starting now that you guys have added to this defense relationship now's back this defense >> man I mean the potential is probably the same as every other team in the league that plays defense is to be the number one defense super bowl defense championship defense you know so all the typical cliche things you could say. At the end of the day, it's the work, you know. I think a year ago, talked about the same stuff and where we can go and all that stuff. We go as far as we work, you know, and obviously it's a lot of uh favor and just guys staying healthy along the way, but when you have all the pieces that we already had and then you add guys to it, uh obviously, you know, the sky the sky's is the limit. So, it's just about the work we put in every day and you know, you can't climb that mountain on day one. Uh but you also can't look back either. Uh so just taking it one day at a time, one step at a time and you know we're on the right track. >> Next one I got a little sensitive but um obviously you're a very guy you're very physical player obviously you know a lot of football has brought you but we all know kind of the danger that football can bring that nature. How do you kind of analyze not only what football has given but also the danger that can present? Yeah, I think the reality of, you know, what you're what I'm doing and the sport that we play, you know, I think that's that was something that back when you go back to 2024 with everything that happened with me, uh, and Trevor, uh, like it's a super fast, aggressive, violent sport. I don't think the NFL likes to use those words because they're trying to expand the game and flag football, which is great for my kids. They not playing tackle football until they older than what I was when I started. I didn't start till I was uh really 14 years old. I was 12 when I first tried and I quit uh for good reason cuz it's a physical game. Uh so I probably wouldn't even let my kids play tackle football until about 14 15 years old. But the reality of the game is it's aggressive. It's violent. Not even um go back to uh San Francisco. Coach Kyle get into a car accident and man like concussion all this stuff. I checked on him and I remember he's like, "Man, now I see what you guys go through with these concussions. It's crazy." And it's like that's what it's like. I mean, you out here, we are running as these are the best athletes all all over the world playing in in on one field, you know, and it's like you're going full speed running into each other. So, that's the type of stuff that can happen. So, uh that's just the reality of the game. And I think we all know what we sign up for. Uh but at the end of the day, like you know, you like I said, you try to play the game the right way, but at the same time, you want to see everybody leave the field. Yeah. >> Has it kind of sunk in and have you gotten a lot of texts from people that know you've been wanting to play for the Texans? >> I think it sunk in the day when I was jogging on the field. That after all these years to come back and they still got love for you and u happy that you back here, man. Uh like I said, it's a blessing. My career started off rough, y'all know. Injury after injury, first game of my career, I just been fighting back ever since. And to play 13 years, to be in my 13th season, I just thank God for that. Uh, man, it's just been a long ride, you know, and I'm glad to be here. >> Talk about the player you are now. >> How you see that fitting here? What that look like? >> Oh, man. Like I said, I still got a lot to give. I can make plays. We all know that. uh just coming in giving my leadership like I said and I see Will lead and I tell him, "Hey, bro, you're doing a good job leading." You know, uh Denil, like it's an older group. We're a lot older than what people think. And it's working because we all speak up. We all say stuff to each other. Nobody going to let nobody slack off. You know what I'm saying? And that's the respect that we have for each other in that locker room and that group. So that's why I say I can see the talent. I don't been on seven other teams, so I know what it look like. So, I know what a winning coaches look like. So, I know we're going to win a lot of games here. That's a fact. Uh, it's the way we work and the way we hold each other accountable since I've been here since day one. So, I'm just looking forward to it. >> A little bit different. I know you've been here and stuff. The heat, the sun. >> Yeah. Thing is, I've been training here for the last 12 years, but it still hit different. I did three plays today. I told him it felt like six or seven. But uh that's just getting back into football shape. All that running. I'm going to text my trainer today and say, "Man, we did all that running for me to get tired today like four legs." But but nah, that's football shape, man. I just got to work. That's what training camp for. You know, as y'all know, I've been missing training camp for some years. Like I said, I'm excited looking for the opportunity. >> What did the first two days here look like for you? I done been doing that for so many years throughout my career. So I just said, let me just go to this training camp with these guys and grind with them so they know I ain't just here for no play around. I'm here to work with these guys and get to know them, build a relationship so they can have a great season like >> first two days. >> Yeah, first two days. >> A lot of physicals, a lot of hand shaking, and a lot of smiling. [laughter] Bastard, you played 44% of the snaps for Dallas. Yeah. >> And you end up having eight and a half sacks and I think it was like a sack every hundred snaps, the cashar snaps. >> What do you feel like your role can be here as far as how they utilize you and keeping you fresh? >> I'm just like I told them, man, I think it's not just my me being fresh, but Will and Denil being fresh too also, man. So we just keep putting pressure on the quarterback and giving our secondary chance to make plays. >> Do you remember your first game against CJ? >> Yeah, I missed two sacks on that joke. >> Yeah, I missed him. I told him I missed you on the sack one last year. My first That's what happen when you walk in week one and you rusty and you don't get no no training camp. So, like I said, that's why I came here now. Trying to knock the rust off a little earlier so I can make some plays this season. >> Did you notice the difference between that game when you played him again in the playoffs and CJ? >> Uh, yeah. title: Full-circle moment: impact of an 'older, smarter' Jadeveon Clowney, Texans camp updates
text: Javian Clowney, proof that you really can go home again. A full circle moment as number 90 runs onto the field and practices with his teammates joining the Will Anderson Juniors, the Denil Hunters, and Zel Shiers, the Texans top ranked defense, and the conversation with him afterward. vintage JD just like our talks this off seasonason and after he signed his one-year $8 million max value contract but a lot of smiles a lot of enthusiasm a lot of football talk with JD Clowney and for him to be back as he said joining a fun team a great [music] team and chasing the Super Bowl he says it's special they've got the dogs already he says he can help those guys so you hear a lot from Javian Clowny you're going to hear from me and of course you'll get my practice just observations as well. But the big story today, Jinavian Clowney number 90 got the number for free as I reported getting it from Logan Hall. He said no Logan just gave him the number um as I'd reported. Wanted to respect the OG and that is definitely the OG. 13th year in the league, made a lot longer than people thought he would when he had lots of injuries, micro fracture knee surgery, lots of hip flexor injuries, and went through some things with maturity. That's one of the things we'll get into today with JD. You know, when he was playing for Bill O'Brien, sometimes late or, you know, maybe not ready to go, uh, and, you know, had some toughness playing with lingering injuries, nagging injuries, playing through them. had to feel great sometimes at that stage of his life to play. But you know later, these years later, wisdom, perspective, and change and right place, right time, as he said, as we reported, he took less money to be a Texan. So for him to be in this framework, he's excited to come here. He's got a smile on his face. and he said that everything, you know, get that taste of winning with the Baltimore Ravens and this is what he wanted. So his whole thing chase a Super Bowl and you know to have this place he could have went other places he could have made more money but he wanted to be here and that's a big overriding fact and I talked to Brian Cushing about him and a lot of people are just truly happy for Javian Clowney and what he's been able to do because what this has done this has given a great defense a real key chess piece think about third downs with Denil Hunter Will Anderson Jr. and Javian Clowney who might line up inside. Jade Clownie has got a proven knack for that. You could also line up wide. There's a lot of things you can do to make third downs a real nightmare for opposing quarterbacks. But having him here and like I said, he's a different JD. He's now a father of three. He lives here year round training with Ben Fairchild, an elite trainer. And you know, he had a great season last year. Had eight and a half sacks. And you know, he was getting like a sack uh rather [clears throat] four snacks every 100 snaps, pass snaps that is. And the only one that ranked ahead of him was Miles Garrett. But now he's fresh. As he said, he grew up, you know, he's a kid. His dad was in jail, grew up in a single parent home, grew up different. When he first was here, yeah, he said he enjoyed Houston. It was fun. And he says he's a lot smarter than before. He's a lot older, a lot wiser, and he says that he's willing to be vocal, willing to do a lot of things to try to pitch in and help the team. He's excited to play for this coaching staff. And this is more of a players coaching staff with Mik Ryan, a former player. And yes, I don't want to bury the lead. Bill O'Brien. Yeah, no love loss for JD, but he says no bitterness from the trade to the Seahawks. He was an unsigned franchise player. Brian Gain, my understanding was wanted to do a deal with JD. O'Brien felt otherwise. Just didn't feel like the maturity was there and it gave him pause about doing a deal for JD at the time. So, that was what it was. He said, but you know, no hard feelings. It was just something where, you know, he's a young guy, easygoing guy, and him and Bill, they just weren't good. But he was always hurt. And that was something that also the durability factor that gave them some hesitation to commit big dollars to Javian Clowny. So yeah, it's different now. And he said he started taking care of himself. As far as goals, he he does set some personal goals, but you know, make the sacks, all that thing. But it's about the Super Bowl. It's about winning. It's about helping the team and just being truly good. He said this isn't necessarily his last ride. he might want to play some more football. So, let's hear from Javian Clowney and then you'll hear some more from me and about my observations, a little more about Clowny and of course some practice footage and we'll talk a lot about a big day by Jaden Higgins and uh since you guys like to know the injury updates said he feels great. Had a collision with Dalton Schultz. Seems like they're both okay. Got up a little gingerly but they're all right. So, no big injury update there. Jaylen Nol still not practicing making progress. Pinky finger tank Dell knee not practicing. Jake Hmel is back to practicing. So they've got him back out there. And you know really MJ Stewart it's a little more it's going to go a little slower with this quadricep tendon and EJ speed of course out for the season. Jake Hansen the goal I'm told per sources is to get back for the first game of the season. So it's neck and neck if he can make it back for that point but they call him week to week with the ankle. All right here's your clowny and then more from me. But we're glad to do that. Uh having fun, great team, great defense. So I take that Super Bowl with the Texans. I feel like great opportunity for me and my family. Uh you know, just enjoy it. >> JD, when it comes to that and playing with these guys, Neil Hunter, Will Anderson Jr., what do you think third downs are going to look like with the three of you guys? >> I mean, it's going to be very special, man. Uh they got some dogs already know coming in can help them guys, you know, so they don't burn out. They can look the same when I'm out there. Uh and we got to get stuff together and dominate up front. I'm looking forward to that. >> This team is very talented. What is it about a head coach Ryan that makes you more playable? >> His energy. Uh same guy, his excite coming in with a smile on his face every day. It's fun guy to be around and it's it trickles off to the team and everybody else is doing it, man. You know, they make practice a lot easier here. I think the day go by. >> You you accomplished a lot in this league, man. Why why are you still out here? And maybe just a little more like this is this is the right opportunity with a great team. >> Yeah, like I said, my whole thing was to chase the Super Bowl this year. Uh no better place for me to do it here. I think they had great defense last year. I said if I can go in the guys about the money because I could have went other places for a little bit more money than I'm like 13 I started here go back here try to win there and see how the rest of my career go but it's been a great I've been having fun >> is this the last stop >> we don't know I go year by year you know I'm enjoy this >> what's the difference what's the biggest difference between you when you walked in the first time and you >> I'm wrong. Uh uh yeah, but I I was a big kid at first when I first got here. I grew up different than a lot of these guys. I told people and I know my dad was in jail and I grew up a lot different. So I got here was never seen Houston. I enjoyed it during my time and yeah, I came with a great guy coming back now in the locker room a lot older. A lot smarter than I was before. What kind of energy you are? But are you going to be more vocal or you just >> I'm a more cool guy to the side. Hey bro, you know, talk to him like that. But you know I speak up too when I see something but you know I like I said I'm just here to help like advice or something I always say hey do this and do that what you think like hey that's what work for me might not work for you but that's what work my advice every day how to take care of you know if I say something long but I mean it's been long since we've been here long how much culture change or things changing around here. Yes. Been a good one. Very very good. Lot lot easier, a lot relaxing in that building. My first goddamn coach staff different guys in that building was great. It's just been easy going back up in there. I expected I got outside. Like I said, that's me for the guy that run the show. A lot of great guys around here, coaches and uh you can feel the energy and all the other guys. So I know great things don't happen here for you and the team. >> JD, I was talking with Brian Kushing and uh he said he's very happy for you. The full circle moment. title: Kevin O'Connell Talks Physicality of Training Camp, Emphasis on Run Game, Jordan Addison's Growth
text: Um, you know, obviously first day of pads yesterday, uh, what jumped out to me was the physicality of just the group. Uh, even some young players, you know, where it didn't seem, uh, like the physicality was too much. I mean, you think back uh, you know, I'm a fan of how we handle uh, not only the offseasons, but the ramp up, acclamation period, all those things. But it's been a long time since a lot of these guys uh, as you look at guy to guy on our on our on our roster, especially some of these young guys since they've worn pads. Um there's always going to be different levels to the competition. Our guys are handling it the right way. Yeah, I think uh you know, you look at it from a standpoint we're we're we're stacking some reps now and you can see you know maybe growth from you know an early the first or second day to now. Uh because the beauty of of our offense is there's a lot of layered learning to it where one coaching point from an early install it will apply uh to how decisive you can be making a decision or you know your timing or your accuracy you're you're throwing the football with. uh and and he's shown improvement every single day. And most importantly, just the comfort level that comes, I think, with all the hard work he put in uh over the summer after kind of being exposed to a lot of this stuff in the spring. >> How do you feel like just the melding what you guys have wanted to do with the run game has gone through the first week? >> Yeah, I think there's been some, you know, really good hits. I think there's been some as far as productive plays in the run game. Um there's been other plays where we're really really close and it's one block uh you know here or there maybe a guy's angle. Maybe it's the combination. Uh maybe it's a combination of you know me putting together something that was uh you know trying to see what it looked like the angles whatever it may be. And it's uh our guys know right now we're in the stage right now where every play uh impacts the next. And that's what you're trying to build when you talk about marrying the run in the past. But what I have really liked, Alec, is uh, you know, the feel of it, guys running off the football. It's by no stretch perfect, nor does it have to be right now, but we're trying to build up to a place where those guys on the field have confidence in the call and and the schematics of it are one thing, but it's it's the fundamentals and techniques and and what it looks and feels like. And like I said a couple days ago, sometimes the best gauge of that is those guys on the defensive side. What's more important to run the football? A great offensive line or a great running back? >> Oh, I think you know a great running back, you know, always uh, you know, can can maybe take a play play that's blocked for four or five and and ring the bell. I mean, there's examples of that uh, not only around the league, but I think we got guys capable of doing that on our team. Uh, but to me, it's it's the it's an all 111 thing. You know, running the football isn't just about the O line, the tight ends. you know, Josh Oliver is one of the best in the game, you know, at those early down jobs of, you know, taking on a lot more than many many guys in this league can can take on from a physicality standpoint and really being a guy that we can put at the point of attack. Um, and really the defense has to recognize that and then they're they're adjusting and then we can run away from those things and get advantages other ways. But it's totally a group effort. Uh, the combinations, you know, Max Bredesen is off to a really really good start. I felt his pads popping yesterday um with some with some contact, you know, at the point of attack. So, um I think, you know, it's great to have both. It's great to have one or the other. And then how you pair it all together is that all 11 field receivers doing their jobs, quarterbacks running the show, making sure it's a premier look uh that we're running against. And you know, we package those plays with cans and it's in eitheror kind of world based upon certain criteras and things like that. and then details of the track of the back, the speed at which that mesh happens of the handoff. Can we be elite on the things we can control and then apply the the physicality and and the intent with a total understanding of the guys on the field of what we're trying to get done. Jordan Addison, what's sort of your threeyear assessment of his progress, growth, direction, whatever. He's, you know, obviously everybody sees the big the one-handed catch yesterday, but I thought the route itself to get the separation that he did, his understanding of the details of things, I think he has a better plan at the line of scrimmage, you know, this year. So if you think about like Von Miller did this a lot and I think the Vikings should do this with Dallas Turner. I think it'd be great for him to put him way out on an island. He can back off into interesting coverage roles, right? And actually have an interesting impact out there, but also because he has the speed, he gets this really big running starter can help him with the pass rush. Nick Bosa is always the guy that I talk about who like feasts on this. This is because I think he's like the superstar example of this wide nine thing. And then you'd have a lot of guys on the inside playing spill and kill. So you have defensive tackles that are going to spill stuff out, muck muck up every little gap and force those runs to bounce outside where your Von Miller or your Nick Bosa or your Dallas Turner is waiting. Um because that's where he lined up, right? These these really wide guys. Bounce them out to your guys spill and kill. And then of course you've got linebackers playing out that way. it gives time for the the the more they go east west the longer your safety has to like track that and make the play with 13 personnel that kind of screws that up because it makes more gaps to muck up. You can muck up A gap A gap B gap B gap but if you start adding C gaps and D gaps to the mix because you're going triple wing now suddenly that's more guys that have to be involved and you can't really do that wide nine thing anymore. You got to have linebackers in there. it causes this huge problem. So, Flores, also big lover of the tight front. Um there's a 5-0 front from uh the Patriots. They call it 50 because that's usually the pass protection that you get when you put five guys on down on the line like that. So, it forces them into their 5-0 protection or I don't know, it might be a chicken egg. I don't know who came first there, but it's it's five across, right? Um the Patardi world would name it after the mascot of whatever college he was at. who would call it like Panther or Spartan. Um, so the Vikings might call it Viking. I named it Ragnar because a Viking front means a different thing in a lot of places. So I I used the word Ragnar. When I did my like big thing on Flores, I I kind of made up a word that I thought made sense. And I would guess that because that front kind of gets cooked when there's more guys on the on the line of scrimmage, more more dudes just like on the ball in three-point stance ready to block. My guess would be that they're going to go away from those and back toward more classic 4-3 nickel fronts or 3 four fronts that put more guys over tight ends or ghost tight ends if there's nobody on that side, but put more guys kind of out there outside the tackles, but not so far outside that they're like part of the coverage. And I think that those fronts would help. Plus, obviously, you know, when you send your bigs, I send my bigs. So, you're going to have a you you could have four D tackles out there at some point if you get 13 personnel and and that's just going to be different depending on the team you're going up against and who they have. Um Oh my god, I ranted about that one for way too long. Okay, I will talk to you all tomorrow.

title: OC Bobby Slowik meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: I think everyone wants to know how you feel is doing so far. >> I've been really really pleased with Malik. Um just his work work ethic every day what he's doing just not with me with the players. Uh his relationships he's building with all of them from the guys up front to the guys on defense to obviously the skills. Um like he's really putting the time in. He's living in the facility, you know. Um he's in my office probably every few days and we're just hanging out and kicking it. So, I mean, he's he's all in on making sure mentally he's up to snuff on where he needs to be and feels confident. And then, you know, I think everyone can see when we're out in camp when he's confident, when he's letting it rip. Um, you know, he's threw some really nice balls. There's there's still a long way to go. There's still a lot of things we're working on as a whole offense, and that includes a quarterback position, but, uh, his his attitude and how he's attacking every day right now has has been fantastic. framework. >> Yeah, that's big time. I mean, we talk about it uh even in our quarterback meetings. You know, we it's always the fine line when you're in camp because the hardest thing to do when you're actually in season and you're memorizing a game plan and then you're going out and you're performing on game day, the athleticism, the moving away from contact comes easy. The hanging in there when you have to, maybe taking a hit and and letting one rip to first in the progression or second in the progression is way harder. So, they always will strain themselves to to really focus on things like that in camp. Um, but you know, he knows there's been a few in camp where we'd like them, hey man, like go run, you know, like the OP is there. Um, and then in the run game, we've we've used them here and there and that kind of is week to week dependent on what a defense gives us, what it presents to us, and how we can take advantage of that. But just be having the ability to do that and his willingness to do that is going to be huge for us. What's it been like working with Kevin Mulo and his influence on how you guys design this offense? >> Yeah, KP's been he's been great like just him. But I mean honestly the whole offensive staff I've had a joy working with the entire offensive staff. I think we got really good assistants like from all the way down to our QC's like those guys do a fantastic job. I think we have some of the best young guys in the league on offense growing coaches. I think our position coaches have been great. I mean, it's it's going to be huge for us on offense, developing the young guys. It's going to be a critical part of our season. And, you know, our position coaches are all in on that. And then, you know, you got guys like uh Patulo who's who can come in and help me with the coordinator process, kind of bounce around at whatever position group is needed on that day. Uh help supplement my coaching points, help give the position coach extra eyes, and then not only that, but he's helping me with scheme, you know. Um he's really done a good job learning what it is that we do and how I see the game and uh how we view things, what we try to attack. Um and he's been constantly talking with me all the time to make sure when we get in season like it's it's a full staff effort to put together a game plan. So having him is huge for me. >> Bobby, I'd like to ask you about the offensive line. We know that Austin Jackson has had minor problems that he's dealing with right now. Where are you in putting the line together and how important is it keep everybody intact, especially Austin given his injury yesterday? >> Yeah, I think really at every position right now our emphasis for our whole offense is competition. You know, like that's been the big thing all the way through. We got receivers with every which group, tight ends with every which group. We got backs with every which group. Probably the only place continuity is like huge if you can have it is up front. So the more we have all five guys out there obviously the better it'll service as we keep going through camp. But the reality of the NFL season is guys got to be ready to step up and jump in there. And I thought yesterday uh I thought Charlie was able to hop in with the ones and you know it wasn't perfect. Again, everybody needs to get better, but I thought he did a pretty good job in his responsibility on what he needed to do. And we're going to continue to mix it up, you know, as we kind of have guys that are in and out for a few days here and there up front. Um, this is kind of the part of camp for that group where I would say it's it's the most uh stressful. uh our defense now has as many presentations and looks as they're going to have and we have as many run plays and protections in as we're going to have. So now everything kind of settles down. Um and really from here on out it becomes all right, can we really hammer our combinations? Can we really hammer our technique? Can we hammer how we handle games? All all the finer points. Last time we spoke to you, you mentioned how chemistry will be a work in progressing. >> Yeah, I mean for sure. I think from OTAAS to now, you see just the balls in a much friendlier spot more often. He's letting it go earlier to a lot of guys. Um even guys he didn't necessarily get reps with in OTAAS. Um I think him and him and Malik Washington clearly have put together a lot of work. He's very confident in how Malik's coming out of breaks right now and he's continuing to build that chemistry, you know, with all the all the guys. And that's why it's so big that we keep mixing in who's going with him and kind of changing it up so he can keep to build that rapport. >> Talk a little bit about when the offense makes a few plays, kind of dial the exotics, dial the pressure a little bit. How is that competition between you guys callers out here? >> Yeah. What's fun about camp is is until we get to what we call call it periods, like unscripted periods where we're moving, he's calling it with no preparation, I'm calling it with no preparation. Um the the I guess the chalk battle is very limited. Very limited. Like there's some times we're in awful situations and we know it. There's times they're in awful situations and they know it. And we want to amp up the pressure on both sides and see like who responds, you know? That's that's really what right now is about. Um, it's not necessarily about the scheme, it's about who's going to respond to the different variety of presentations we give. >> Do you have to do you have to take some like negative pass plays with a grain of salt because Malik's not using one of his trademark skills in running the ball? >> Um, I mean, yes and no, probably. I don't want to, you know what I mean? Like I like I said earlier, we we got to get better all the way across board from protections to routes to to quarterback play to execution to I mean we just we got a lot of young guys. We got a lot of growing to do. We have a long way to go. Um I would say in a game, you know, I I think he's shown in his career like if he needs to make one guy miss and make a play with his feet and his legs, he'll do that. But I I think it's more productive for us as an offense to I mean we got to get better. We got to clean it up. asked this before, but how have you seen Washington improve from last year to this year? >> Uh, I'd say right now probably the the most noticeable improvement, like he's always had really good work work ethic. Uh, the the attitude has always been there. He's always just been hungry for coaching, but what he's done in OTAAS and now through like the offseason program when he was on his own to carrying it into practice is his footwork and how he's getting in and out of breaks is really clean right now. You know, you could tell he's really really bought in to how we want to get to break points, how we want to release. Um, and he's as good as he's looked since I've been here at that part of his game. That's been really fun to watch. >> How do you see that kind of I mean, >> same as we're seeing on the field right now. You know, I he just the ability to do that. He's already a great ball in hand player. Now, you get a chance to win and separate at the top of routes when we have bad leverage situations uh just with good good footwork. I mean, now you take uh chances that you would only have an opt to get the ball when it's premier. Now, he can win even versus non-premier stuff. So I think for him it's and for us as an offense it's huge. >> As it relates to as it relates to pre-nap motion, what do you view as some of the positive benefits and possible detriments? >> Yeah, I'd say you see both right now, right? Like we we really amped that up today. Today was a big on the move motion day for us. Um, and we didn't necessarily have as many pre- snap penalties as we've had in days before, but we definitely were not clean on our assignments, on our locations. Snap points strenuous for the quarterback. Like, it gets hard mentally. Uh, which is why it's huge. You do that all the time. If we do it well, it just helps us put the defense in positions where we help ourselves in our assignment. Uh, which obviously what they've done here in the past and what Mike does, uh, McDaniel has, he's been awesome at that. So, we'd be foolish not to take advantage of that. But it it takes a lot of work on our end, you know, and and making sure we're on the operation is is the biggest thing for us. >> Where is relative to his comfort level? >> Yeah, he's been great. They did it in Green Bay all the time. He's familiar with it. I'm I'm sure they did it, I think, even in Tennessee when he came in as a rookie. Uh we might have a few different ones that, you know, uh really within the last few years were created here, but he's he's been awesome on it. >> Bobby, regarding Um, we've seen him make a catch in traffic and and get hit by Jordan Brooks and hold on to the ball. We've also seen Juju Prince kind of strip the ball from him late. Tell me about his learning curve, his potential, and you guys have moved him around a little bit, right? >> Yeah. >> Tell me about that with Yeah, he's been doing a good job. You know, we kind of had to we've been moving him around with positions um really through camp. You know, he's he's played multiple. He hasn't just played one, which is a credit to him. that's hard for a rookie to do. Uh he's immensely talented dude. He's got long arms. He's fast. He's got really good feet. He's tall. Uh and and you know, we just need him to continue to grow in his technique and his fundamentals of what we see receiver play entails at the Miami Dolphins. And he's doing that. Like it it flashes. It shows when he does it. And then there's still, you know, there's still little things that you can get away with in college for all our young guys that in the NFL you no longer can do. You know, the catch tuck, how important that is, how fast that is. In college, you could probably catch wait on your tuck for a good two seconds with no issues. I mean, the way our defense is going at the ball right now, if it's not instantaneous, it might come out. Uh, if our footwork isn't clean on our transitions, we're probably getting tackled. If we have clean footwork on our transitions, now we got a chance to run through some stuff. So, it's just little things like that for all our young guys. We got to continue to grow. >> One more quick. How does he use his size as both a receiver and a blocker? Is that >> I mean, I know he's a rookie. Is he fairly polished at that or does he have a long way to go? Where is he as far as using that? >> Yeah, he's he's been great. He's been great. He's throwing it in there in the run game. All our receivers are doing a really good job embracing the run game. And we we've [laughter] we've put him in some tough spots so far since we put the pads on and they're all about it. And that's what we want. We want a tough, physical football team that's that's going to play with high effort and it's going to throw it in there and we're going to strain until the whistle blows. And and all of them, young guys included, are doing that. Uh and then the size and obviously as far as receiver route running goes, like the catch radius is just I mean he he makes some catches that probably most people can't, you know, so that's huge. >> What are your hopes for Chris once you are? >> Yeah, I I mean he's still a long way away. We we haven't even had a chance as coaches to to work with him aside from in the meeting room. So, we'll see when he's able to go. >> Couple days ins. >> Yeah, he I mean probably the number one thing I'd say right now is is confidence. I think he's just more confident in what he's doing, how he's doing it, the the posture he's in in in the in pass pro and in the run game, how he's firing off the ball, how confident he is in his assignment. Um, I think it shows in his play, you know, again, all the way up front. It's not perfect. Uh, he still he still has some things we got to continue to work on as well, but I think the confidence for him right now is as good as I've seen it. >> Final question. >> Do you think right tack was just a position of concern now? is being done. You have you considered, you know, cross training anybody being that Ken has that experience to tackle some other players as well. >> Yeah, I mean there's there's things we talk about as a coaching staff all the time. If this happens, do we do this? Do we get some guys that reps like here? A lot of times you don't really want to move a starter if you can help it because they're banking all the reps that you want at certain spots. But you really when you get in season uh you need to be fluid. That's just the reality of O line in the NFL. Uh different things happen every year. So, we try to cross trainin as many guys as we possibly can to be ready to roll. And we'll see where AJ's at.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: being dayto-day. Um, so hopefully he will not practice today, but hopefully that will not be very long, which I do not anticipate that being for very long. >> And we haven't seen Jamari Sailor, I always want to say Slayer. Jamari Sailor and Greg Doulich the past couple days. Um, can you give us an update on him? >> Yeah, same thing with them. I don't see it long term. I see them dayto day. I would say for Doulich just being truthful with you probably back in that Washington timeline and for Sailor more dayto day >> with with the depth that you have at at right tackle obviously they had some struggles yesterday um is this a good opportunity to evaluate what's there [clears throat] or or how comfortable do you feel practicing without Austin? Well, I think it forces us, to answer your question, it forces us to evaluate what's there, right? Um, you have no other choice at this point. Your roster is your roster, and it's a great time when he's not practicing to evaluate those other guys. >> Do you notice a different type of energy and excitement with the pads on the fans out there? >> Um, I could sense the first day on a Sunday, there was some cool excitement. I think it was cool for those guys to see. It was cool for me to run out and see the fans. It brought a little extra excitement and um you know pretty cool that they could see and it was a great day. There was a ton of people here. I mean I thought that was awesome. Even yesterday there was a bunch of kids in the left side of the bleachers that were cheering and what a cool opportunity for them. As far as the pads go on truthfully, you know, I think anytime you put the pans on and you change the stimulus a little bit, they they were a little quieter and stretched and you can see they're probably all thinking. I mean it's going to be a physical practice. They're trying to get their minds right. Some of them are young and they have some anxiety and they're anxious about it. So it was quiet when we first went out there and then I think usually usually when you play after you take that first shot it kind of all right I'm back and now this is what we do and how we do it and it feels normal. Um so I think it took a little bit of time to get going. Typical first day of pads pad levels usually really high. Things are pretty sloppy. Um you know just carrying your pads again being in full pads. they got thigh pads on, knee pads on, and they're just getting used to carrying that weight. But certainly the biggest thing that I noticed is the pad level um usually goes up because you really got to bend and play with great leverage. But we'll get used to it. I think that's why it's important you practice in front of fans, it's as close to, you know, a preseason game as you could possibly get. And then practicing with your pads on, it's how you actually have to go and play the game. So, you better get used to it. have uh yesterday it seemed like we saw a lot of uh blitzes and stunts and twists and things like that. What What does that is that the case and what does that tell us about how you look at the game? Were you worried about overwhelming your offensive line and pass protection, that kind of thing? No, yesterday in the periods it was a bunch of second, seven plus, and third down situations. And those are usually more downs where you will notice more pressure, more stunts. Um cuz usually they're more passing downs. And usually you get more exotic on passing downs than you do in rundowns. When you try to do those exotics against rundowns, usually get creased. So you try to pick and choose. And then we were in two-minute setting where, you know, in certain situations with the clock stopped or even clock running and you got to knock them out of field goal range where more pressure will show up. So that's probably why you saw that as far as early down football goes and we need to be able to play base downs. We need to be able to move and play technique. And I think the biggest thing for us right now is we need to figure out what works and what we can handle. So I'm trying to throw a lot at these guys. >> You've talked about coverage at all three levels for quarterbacks that you like. I'm curious, are there other non-negotiable qualities for a Jeff Halfley quarterback before that even starts? [clears throat] >> Yeah, I I don't ever want to stay blocked. If you ever show me a corner who's engaged with the receiver and he's letting that receiver block him and he stays blocked, that's not okay with me. Like, that drives me absolutely crazy because all that is is toughness and a mentality that there's no way a receiver is going to stay on me and block me. So, you need to learn how to block, release, and leverage the ball and get to the ball. I think when you look at a football team in general, um, the way I view a defense is when I turn on the tape, whether it's our team or another team, if the corners are physical and they're tackling, it's usually a pretty tough team. It's like when I watch wide receivers, if I'm watching a tape and wide receivers are blocking down the field and they're getting after DBs and linebackers and defensive ends, it's usually a sign that's a pretty tough team. So, corners who stay on blocks, that's not okay with me. >> Jeff, you mentioned early downs. Uh last couple years we've seen 12 and 13 kind of trending up. Yeah. As far as early down usage, but also like the passing rate there has been going up. I know Chicago was I think over 50% last year. >> Uh how hard is it to gauge when a trend like that is going to keep going versus when maybe it's capped out? And then do those conversations kind of come up when you're working with Sully talking about either personnel or scheme? Like how hard is it to thread that needle? So, going back with the trend, did we see more, you know, you look at Chicago, for example, I think one of the things Ben does is he self scouts himself and he stays extremely balanced, which I think a lot of the good coordinators do. Anytime I look at first and 10, second one to six, and a certain personnel grouping, if it's 50/50, then I have to play I have to play it balanced, right? If I know 12 personnel on P and 10 or 12 personnel on second three is heavy heavy run or boot for example, then there's certain blitzes that I circle and like and it kind of gives me the advantage there. So you got to be careful just like I got to self scout myself. If they look at me and in, you know, early downs I'm more base coverage and don't blitz or stunt then, you know, they're probably looking at it as these guys aren't a threat to blitz or stunt and we're going to take advantage of them. So I think there's a lot of self scouting there. Okay. I think it based on the personnel you have like like who do you have? Do you have three really good tight ends? Maybe you have three really good receivers. Who do you want to get on the field? Um certainly there seems to be more 12 and even 22 that's being run again. Kind of going back to how football used to be played and then if you look a couple years ago people were spreading it out more and getting into four open. So when that changes I'm not sure. Um, but even for us right now, I mean, Bobby does a great job of balancing it and mixing it up and ultimately it's going to come down to who we have, but I can't predict I can't predict what it's going to look like three years from now. >> I think offensive guys get bored and just want to keep changing it up and having fun. >> I have one more injury question for you. What can you share about Lonnie Johnson Jr. >> Dayto day? Um, he won't be out there today, but I don't think that would be longterm earlier. the one and I'll just get ahead of you and just be honest with you, is Konga, which I'm I'm sure one of you guys was going to jump in and ask me anyway, he's the one that will be longterm. He'll be out for the season. But all those other guys, I can look you in the eye and tell you it's dayto-day, but Congo will be done for the year. And that's unfortunate because he's a a young guy was working really hard and he'll have to view this as a red shirt year. >> With Kaden Proctor, obviously you guys thought a lot about him taking so high. Athletically, has anything surprised you because yesterday on that Datson interception to see a guy that big go all the way down there? >> Yeah. >> Has anything surprised you on the deal with him? >> Um, no. Nothing surprises me. It's exactly what we thought we'd get. Now, I haven't seen many offensive linemen run that fast and chase a ball carrier. And I was fearful of the defensive player who had the ball because if it was live, it would have been a very interesting hit. Um, but I think that if you really watch that play closely, him and Brewer both took off for the ball. And I think that says a lot about the buying of these players right now and the mentality that these players have where a lot of times, even early on when I'm showing the film to the whole team. And we're going to throw an interception, right? It's going to happen. And what do you do after the interception? How do you react on defense? How do you react on offense? On defense, you better catch the ball. And every single guy better go get a block. And if you pause the film and a guy's not getting a block, why? You don't care about that guy that just intercepted the ball. You don't want to score a touchdown, don't celebrate. Go block somebody and try to help him score a touchdown. On the other side of the ball on offense, I get it. Don't sulk. Don't just sit there and watch. Go after the ball and try to get it back. Cuz if you notice, yesterday there was one play we fumbled and Omar picked it off and then the running back Hank came in and Peanut punched it and he got the ball back. That sends a huge message. He was waiting for him to get off the ground like we're talking about and he threw a punch. the other one when we threw the pick and he returned it for a touchdown, Brewer and Proctor took off and I was almost like, "Oh my gosh." One, this is awesome. Two, let's make sure they don't really hit anybody. So, I just I think it sends a really loud message that, you know, I seem better than I hear that these players have bought in and they're giving everything that they have. >> What have you liked from Malik Willis the last two practices? >> Um, just more consistent. um the confidence and you know he's just getting more comfortable. The ball's coming out quicker. He's throwing more on his first hitch than being late on his throws. He's starting to, you know, have a better relationship with the guys. We're only through a handful of practices, but he's already, you know, grabbing guys on the side, talking to them. If a guy drops the ball, he's encouraging them. You know, you can see him, him and Malik are on the sideline talking about routes, how to do this, how to do that, what the defense is playing. I just think he's getting more comfortable. Still really early and and we all have a long way to go. >> A week into camp, um what's one thing you've been happy with holistically and one thing that needs improvement? >> I think the overall effort and how hard they're practicing. Um I think the improvement, you know, the little details, the the false starts, the pre- snap penalties that are going to make us go backward. And then just like every other coach right now, just it's the the overall execution and the mentals. And that's going to happen early in camp. What can't happen early in camp is the things that you can control as a player, right? And that's your attitude. That's your effort. Um that's how you show up every day. It's how you run to the ball. It's how hard you pay attention. It's what you're like in the meeting room. I mean, that's been outstanding. And a lot of the other stuff, we got a long way to go. Um but that's totally okay because it's early in camp and we got to coach. We got to coach hard. We got to coach better and we need to execute better. >> What has impressed you so far about Malik Washington? Um just his overall route running. You know I think um you know a lot of people might think of him as a bubble guy, a catch and run guy, a quick screen guy, a get him the ball on a hitch and let him run. Just him at the top of the routes and I think him really trying to master the route tree and the techniques that are being asked to do um and just his overall consistency of how he approaches every day. Regarding Zack Cer, this [clears throat] is a guy who had back-to-back 10 sack seasons, five and a half last year. How important is that sack total to you from Zack Cer and how important is it to determining whether he had a good season or not? >> Yeah, I think you got to look at this two ways. when I, you know, when I first just watched Zach's film, you know, I thought one thing and then when you get to know Zach and what you see what Zach does um throughout the course of the plays, especially when you get into those passing downs here, I'll give you a good analogy. I view Zach like a point guard, okay? Where a lot of people all they look for is how many points did they score? And a lot of people might say, "How many sacks did Zack get?" One, Zack's sacks are going to come. So, I certainly want that number up. But what Zach does is Zach sets up so many uh games and so many rushers for his teammates and he takes so much pride in that where if he knows the slide side or the man side, um he can he can call out those games and really selfish rushers just want to rush. Zach's perfectly okay with running a game, picking a guy, grabbing a guy, and having his teammate come through. and you can see how excited he gets about that. So, I view Zach one. Certainly, I'd like his numbers to be up, but at the same time, I think if we counted assists, I think he'd be one of the assist leaders in the NFL. >> Did you ever watch this film Christian? >> No, I've watched it. Clark had showed it to me and those two did a great job together. And I'm sure Christian really appreciate having Zack because he did the same thing. So, unselfish player. I think that's the coolest thing um that you don't know about Zach when you first watch the film, but when you get to know him and watch him, that's really cool to see. >> So, the other day, Jacob was talking about measuring when to go for the punch out opportunities. You know, third down, short of a stick, maybe hold back and make a tackle. How can you tell when you're in the scouting process on tape that a player is sharp with those instincts and how do you go about facilitating that once you get them in your building? >> Some guys are just natural at it. I mean, I think it's really important. One, when you look at any player in the draft, I think production is very important, right? Guys that have a ton of tackles, guys that have a ton of sacks, guys that have made plays. I think often people look at traits and not production. Well, you want both, right? I mean, a guy could be extremely athletic, extremely fast and long, but has made no plays, so he's got no instincts. The instincts show up, right? When you watch Jacob, and Jacob's got a certain timing, which you even saw in college, he knows when to throw it. He's precise with it. He's detailed with it. and he's caused force fumbles. So ball production as you look at players is important. Like if you're scouting a safety for me, one of the questions I always ask is how many interceptions does he have in his career? Right? That's important because if he has none and you watch the tape, is it because he's had no opportunities? But then you watch the guy's got eight to 10 and it's like I mean a guy who gets the ball gets the ball and that's important because in a game we need guys who can take away the football. you not only retained Bobby Slowick but made him do the OC. >> How much of that was continuity and what is he showing you in terms of getting the offense in gear for the season? >> Yeah, [clears throat] I think continuity just kind of was coincidence. Um when I went through the process, Bobby was really high. Whenever you get um whenever you get a chance to interview for a head job, you got to go in with a depth chart of coordinators, right? And it can't just be one. It's got to be thought out and you got to be detailed. And there have to be guys that are there's also a getability factor, right? I can't like list Kyle Shanahan as the guy I'm going to hire to be my offensive coordinator because there's no way Kyle's going to be my offensive coordinator. So, you start to list guys you think you can get. Um, and Bobb's a guy I had for the past two years on my list. One, I was with him. He worked on defense very closely with me in San Francisco. So, I knew how smart he is. I knew how he is around players. More importantly, I know him as a person. And he's the type of guy that I want. If any of you spend any time with Bobby, he's one of the best human beings that there is. Um, he has a great way to relate to players, be demanding, and he's a great teacher, and I think he's been trained by, you know, one of the best guys to call plays in a long time. Um, and that's important to me cuz he does things the right way, and I have complete trust in him to do what he thinks. Will I jump in from time to time and give him my thoughts and ideas? Of course. I think that's important, too. But I mean, I got total confidence in Bobby. >> I'm curious, how do you evaluate the interceptions in practice? Like with Malik, it seems like a lot of his have came from tipped passes, right? And so, how do you like coach that? >> Well, I think you got to look at everyone individually. Um, you know, did he did he throw a did he throw a ball down the middle of the field where there was a middle safety and just make a bad decision? Well, you know, that's on him. Did he throw a ball on time and it hit the receivers's hands and it bounced up and counts as an interception and five weeks from now you're not going to remember it. You're just going to count it as an interception, but next play, man, it happened. We got to catch the ball better. Did the protection break down and as he was releasing the ball, did his arm get hit? And was that the reason that the ball got tipped or is that the reason? So, there's so many reasons. Did was the ball supposed to be on time on his first hitch? was he's supposed to throw the ball right there and the receiver broke the wrong way and now the DB is sitting right there. But if the receiver broke the right way, you would have been in front of the guy. So, it's just hard. It's hard when I watch a game live. It's hard when you guys watch a game live. And what's our first reaction? The quarterback threw another interception. But that's not always the case, right? So, you got to look really hard at it. And I think Bobby and those guys do a great job and and Malik understands that, too. So in the moment, in the game, in the practice, whatever it may be, you got to just let it go and then you got to go look at the iPad, figure out why it happened and correct it to make sure it doesn't happen again or did the DB just like let's give the defense credit too sometimes. Did the DB just make an incredible play and you got to live through it and go. But there's a whole lot of reasons. >> What is it about the running back's room that keeps on drawing you in? Is it the personality, the versatility of the position, or is it just because that's where your coaching career? >> What do you mean, the running backs or the DBs? >> Running backs. >> Well, I'm I'm a DB guy, so I spend a lot of time with the DBs. What draws me to the running backs when you see me around them is I just one, I want to be around everybody. And two, you know, with Han there, I just I think we have one of the best in the game, and I like to be around those guys and support them. And then they're the other guys are all battling. So, it's been a really fun group to watch so far. You guys good? >> All right. Thanks, guys.

title: What Changed for the Saints' Offense on Day 5?
text: Today was the day. It was finally the day. Today was the day that the offense finally got going. It has been the practice that we've been waiting for since training camp started. We saw the offense humming in OTAs. We saw it humming in mini First three days of camp for whatever reason, four four days of camp for whatever reason, it was a little bit slow going. But on day five, the day when the pads came out, the offense freaking took off and just started humming. Like it just started humming. 11 of 14 passing for Taysom Hill. It was the day that knocked all the worry out of the building. Not that there was ever actually real worry over what it had looked like early on in training camp. We had noted that there were a lot of reasons for it. And I don't think that the offense is going to have all these huge issues where through four days it was like 47% completion. Today 11 of 14. I think today's a lot closer to what we're going to be seeing going forward. And you know, Jordan Tyson finally started to get going. And Chris Olave finally started to get going and AT Perry finally started to get going consistently. And all these little pieces just seemed to click today and the offense looked freaking great. They shut everybody up. They shut me up. They shut everyone up and they they made some plays. We're going to watch all that on today's show. And we're going to break down everything that happened on today's show. But we started with the first day of pads. This is presented by PJ's Coffee. Today was the first time that there was actually true physicality in practice. And there were a lot of things that I thought were exciting to see and worthwhile to see. And number one, day one of camp in pads, the first thing I'm going to look at is the offensive line and defensive line one-on-ones. And we have that video on our site, neworleans.football. If you want to watch it, go check that out. If you just want to support our show, go sign up to the site. It's the best way to do it. But the first thing I like to look at is the offensive line and defensive line one-on-ones.
