So, um, I just I just give thanks to God for just pouring into me, helping me to continue to grow as a man, as a person, be able to come out here, um, with with new strength and, yeah, just try to give it my best, you know, for his glory and to help out this team. >> With special teams as well, I'm curious as a kick returner, how do you feel you can help, you know, how you've grown there? Because we saw you do it a little bit last season. Um but just how you can kind of make even more of a role for yourself on this team through that opportunity. >> Yeah, I mean I think if the coaches whatever they want me to do if it's um returning kicks, you know, I'm going just try to give it my best um however I can help this team win games. But the biggest thing coming out here in practice when we do have opportunity to return kicks, um yeah, just just knowing what I'm doing, knowing what I'm supposed to look at and so yeah, when you see a crease, you got to hit it because it clears up fast. >> Yeah. Um, like I like I said, uh, just just getting better with the offensive system. Um, knowing where I'm supposed to be, um, knowing that knowing the blocking schemes and things like that. Uh, being able to get more reps in practice as well. Um, and so it it definitely it definitely helps out. You know, I'm just trying to continue to grow grow as a running back. >> Yeah. Thank y'all so much. >> What's going on? How y'all doing? >> Good. Good. >> How would you describe your first NFL. >> Uh, I'm saying so far has been pretty good. Just kind of get in where I fit in pretty much is see all the vets and how they kind of do things and then go out there and try to replicate it myself. >> Part of that has been protection, watching closely gets right in there with you. >> What was your first reaction to when he sort of >> Yeah. Um, I mean that obviously means a lot. Uh, especially on special teams. I have a head coach involved. Uh, like even on the whole team, but especially on special teams, he kind of just speaks to the team, speaks to, you know, whoever's on that unit, the importance of it, and just kind of finding your role for the team. >> What have you learned from Christian Ellis, Robert the summer with them? >> Um, I've learned a lot from them those two players. Uh, I'd say the main thing I've learned is pretty much a linebacker is going to be involved in one of the play if it's Mike or Will. So you can't have a off play or off game. You pretty much got to be at your top level every single play. And if one of the backers are not playing at the top level, it'll show on the defense. Do >> you have any rookie obligations? We talked to Baron. He said you had to get snacks. Braden last year said you had to get snacks. Is there anything that you're you're being asked? >> Yeah. Yeah. They got me getting snacks for the whole room. >> Is there any snack in particular you've had to buy more than others? >> Uh no. I ain't going to lie. When I first bought them, I just bought a whole bunch. I kind of just put a text in the group chat of what they wanted and just filled up the whole room with it. >> What's surprised you about your first NFL train? >> Um, I'd just say the biggest surprise I'd just say um the tempo of everything. I'd say it's a lot faster, but at the same time, you're not like all over the place. You're still um staying up. They don't want people really going to the ground. So, I'd just say the tempo of everything kind of just knowing where you're supposed to be, moving fast, but not really finishing to the ground. >> You have a favorite oneliner from Braves yet? >> Not yet. >> Do you feel like you've adjusted to that temple? >> Um, to be honest with you, not really. I always say I'm just trying to be better than I was yesterday. So, it's obviously better than what I started, but it's definitely not where I want to be at yet. There have been conversations about you maybe playing other types of roles in this defense. Safety, I know you played that in college, but are you just sort of focusing on linebacker right now? >> Uh, I'm pretty much just trying to find my role for the team, whatever that might be. Um, I know we got a lot of different packages in right now, so wherever the coaches feel like they can put me in and I'll play, I'll do it. In >> college, it's a lot quicker. The preseason goes by fast. Every realize you got another month to go before the first game of the season. How tough is that to get used to? Um, it is kind of tough, but at the same time, I kind of look at these preseason games as actual games, too. Um, in college, we didn't have those. We'd have like scrimmages maybe once or twice a week, but it wasn't like actually going to the stadium dressing up and stuff. So, I'd say that's pretty much the big difference. I think that's pretty cool. >> You talked about the tempo of practices themselves. How about the volume of the information you have to keep up with? How have you been able to handle that? >> Yeah, I'd say that's definitely been a lot, too. Especially being a linebacker, you have to know a lot, the fronts, the checks, and kind of get everybody else lined up in what to do. So, I'd say it's definitely been more than college, but I've been just trying to do the best I can to learn it. And another thing, too, is like there's a lot of kind of calls or plays that we got in, but a lot of them can kind of be like packaged together. So, when you hear a certain call, you can kind of just think of a base call and it kind of plays out the same. >> Mike asked you about special teams protection. Did you have experience in college on teams? >> Yeah. Uh my first year at TCU I was pretty much playing all the teams and then even the past couple years I was still on teams a little bit and it's kind of just one of those things of the more I was playing on defense kind of less I got on special teams but it's something I've done before and it's something I'm willing to do. >> Yeah. Uh me and Khalil been I would say doing good. uh came in same time. I remember just doing the Zoom calls and then even just the rookie stuff in the spring and then now here in the summer I'd say um he's a great player. Uh he's playing Mike so I say he's got a little bit more checks and kind of responsibilities calling out the defense than I do playing will. So I just say he's doing a great job in his role right now. >> Is there anything your first uh month in New England? What's been anything so different or things you're still getting used to? What stands out? >> Um I'd probably just say the weather. Uh, I've been in Texas the last couple years, so it's pretty much been hot and sunny every single day. And then since I've been here, it's kind of unexpected what you might get. It might be sunny today or like yesterday could just be pouring rain. Good to meet you, man. You, >> too. Thank y'all. It's like a snow day for you. >> I know. All right. Appreciate y'all. >> Thank you, Navy.

title: Mike Vrabel: "Off to a Good Start." | Patriots Press Conference
text: How are you? >> Good morning. >> Um, I know it's only been a couple days, but how do you how do you think Gabe Ais has fared both on the field and off the field where I understand you give him quite a bit? >> Well, I think that's all, you know, we got some time to make up. You know, we've got to make up for loss time, I think, a little bit with Gabe, but um, you know, I say he's working hard. I think he's, uh, he's into it. He's he's trying to learn. He's focused. A lot of these things are are new for him. And I think he's done a good job of controlling what he can control. And I see him in there meeting with with Smitty a lot. And and again, there's a return to play. You know, he'll have a few more reps than he did yesterday. And uh you know, these situations, he kind of has to just understand and it's good to see him get acclimated to the special team stuff and you know, so I think it's it's going good. I think we're off to a good start and uh hopefully that he can continue to keep adding things and you know figure out where he can help us uh defensively and and really uh special teams >> like from his perspective uh how hard is it to come into that this situation early and also how's his football acumen? >> Well, how hard it is? I think it's probably that's a great question for for Gabe. I mean, I you know, when he's here, we we've been trying to again get him moving along as quickly as possible, and that's just what the situation was. But I think that that, you know, he may be able to articulate that better. I don't I don't want to speak for him. Um, but we're excited to to have him out there. And, uh, you know, it's see how he responds each and every day. continue to add uh to the workload and then figure out, you know, I'm working with him on the side and on the punt because that's probably the toughest one there to for the young guys to to get going on. And so he's missed some of those reps and, you know, we want to make sure that, you know, he's he's doing that and getting caught up there. And so we'll see how that looks today. Uh you know, putting him in there with the team period with the punt. >> Sorry. >> What are the keys to effective punt protection? And how does the technique have to differ considering you're not just dropping back, you actually also have to get down field. >> Yeah, it's funny. We try to talk to him about being an offensive lineman and then they have to kind of be, you know, a linebacker, right? And you have to be able to to strike. And, you know, the biggest thing is being able to recognize whether it's pressure, whether whether it's holdup and, you know, how the help system works and not jumping out of there and creating gaps, but trying to come back and and stay square and and use uh, you know, use our length. Um, but then sometimes they're they're coming in there to hold you up and uh we feel like the best way to to do that is to be able to to strike and provide, you know, some extension and then you have to shed and, you know, work work your coverage lanes and uh, you know, unfortunately we gave up one last year uh, in Miami and uh, you know, it starts with a with a good punt, but then also having some interior guys. We know the gunner sometimes gets d they get doubled and uh they're not always down there to to force a fair catch or tackle. So, you know, being able to get the the PP down as as the third gunner we call it. um you know, but it's got to be a help system and we have to be able to protect inside out and but also, you know, be able to cover and and understand and locate where the ball is and those lanes change and so I think there's just a lot of things that are different from the way that that we punt in the National Football League and the way that you know a lot of the college players um have done it. Yesterday's practice seemed very competitive from our perspective and a lot of talking between the offense and the defense depending on who was winning whatever uh round >> can't win at the same time. I've realized that. >> Do you where do you draw the line at trash talk versus the competitive nature that you want these guys to have when building your team? >> Yeah, I think anything that is um authentic and and real. I don't think anything that's, you know, made up or fake. I think uh the competitiveness has been great. Uh I want that. I think we need that. Um I think that's part of building a team, but then also the the the line that we take them to is being able to, you know, take care of each other. Um you know, we're not not throwing punches. That's we're not into that. That that gets you eliminated from the game. Uh so that's not how we're we want to practice. We want to avoid those things. And but I'm all for the energy and you know the trash talk and the back and forth and being able to get back and you know then do your job. And if that affects doing your job the next snap, then I would try to do my best to to talk about it and explain like, hey, when you're doing this, you're not very good the next snap or you're not ready to go or the offense goes on the ball and we've got 12 men on the field uh because you're focused about talking to to somebody else and you know, then those things start to become an issue. But I'm I'm all for it as much as we can handle. >> Mike, you talked earlier this offseason about wanting to run the ball more consistently. Are you looking for that to come more from like the personnel changes with Elijah and Reggie and some others or more from Josh kind of tweaking the schematics of it? >> No, I don't I mean I think that it all that all is part of it and I don't think that there's one great solution other than you know a demeanor and I think every great uh running football team the the receivers have to be involved at at some level. I mean, you can't just sit there and and have your run game be comprised of RPOS's and relief throws because that just I I don't think is going to create a consistent, you know, you look at the teams that run the ball best. Uh their receivers are involved with with blocking force, whether that's the nickel, blocking [snorts] the nickel, blocking safeties, you know, they have to be able to do that. you just so I think there's finding a balance between uh what we feel like our team does best but then also you know using using Reggie using the tight ends using guys and and some of the personnel. So I I know that that's probably fairly vague, but I there's you have to have a mentality and a mindset to to want to run the football. And then I think this the scheme and what the players do best is critical. And then also um you know look at any of our explay runs. The [snorts] receivers are involved uh wi with getting support and then running by corners or running by free safeties. You can't block everybody but you know we got to get you know guys like Tayvon that can hit home runs. We we got to get him through the second uh and third level. Uh trying to break arm tackles and then see if he can run away from some people. >> AJ said yesterday that I think we're asked the same question. AJ said yesterday dislocated the thumb just you know how is he doing today? >> I think he's going to be okay. I think I think he's going to be okay. Now, I tell him the linemen do that every other snap, and you know, it's not a national story when a lineman pops his finger back in place, but we had a little bit of fun with that. And, uh, you know, I think that, you know, again, I appreciate what AJ and and Gonzo have done is just come in and compete and and try to improve. And you know, it's been a good battle and that's pro football and and I love watching it and I think that there's a great amount of respect uh that each of those players have for each other and understand that the work that they're putting in now is going to pay dividends in the season. And I think that that's all you can ask uh from from your frontline players is that they come out and they're um you know, they're focused on getting better each day and they're intentional with their work. And when they're out there, it sends a a clear and easy message uh to the rest of the team about how we're supposed to challenge and compete. And you know, I think it's like it's been a good competition. >> Like any guys returning today or being load managed? Uh, I don't think Reggie will be out there today and then there's some other bumps and bruises. I think Barmore is probably going to be managed today and uh will yesterday talking about how the offensive line and the defensive line you'll often have conversations with each other kind of looking out for little things tendencies help the other guy on the other side of the ball. How much do you guys as a coaching staff encourage those sorts of conversations maybe independent of what you guys are doing as coaches? >> Yeah, we do. I mean, that's all part of building a team, whether that's with the DBs, the receivers, splits, releases, technique. Um, you know, we can only game plan for one team is what we the message I try to tell them. And they see these guys every day. They know what it looks like when they're maybe in a certain stance or what they look like when they uh maybe in a tighter alignment or a little looser alignment or how they're going to set the game up or so. I think all those things are important, those conversations and the way that they um you know come out today to make the adjustments and watch the tape and and whether we are able to make corrections on things that one side of the ball is doing. I think this is good practice for the season. You know, we've talked about that. So, I hope that uh there we spend a lot of time together and I hope a lot of that time is spent, you know, talking about football. I understand it's not all going to be football. There's a lot of things for these guys to to get to know about one another, but I'm glad that they are talking football and you know the line of scrimmage for our football team like that has to be the you know where we begin our identity and it can't you know we can't ask you know some receivers or DBs to do it. Our our football team has to be led by by the offensive and defensive line and and the way that they play and their demeanor >> with um Christian and AJ. you you touched on it a little bit, but what does it mean for other players to see kind of them go up against each other the way that they do in pract? >> Well, I can only speak on my experience when guys were, you know, when when I would play and I think that that would be a great question for some young guys in the locker room that what they feel like and how they experience it. But, you know, as a coach, I would say that, you know, it makes it easy. It sends a clear message. I think that that exhibits a level of leadership that we're going to be out here and we're going to compete, challenge, but also, you know, take care of each other. You know, I think that's the biggest thing. And that's why practice is, you know, we want to be as fast as possible. We want to be as physical as possible, but but in the end, we're all working for the same goal, and we need everybody, and they're important, so we have to be able to take care of each other. Mike, >> how do you feel about the depth that you guys have at guard right now? I mean, I think that, you know, there's whether we're have injuries or things, but you know, I think that guys are working in there. James Hudson's getting some reps inside there and there, you know, but there'll be a time where you guys will see Caleb work in there. And so, we're just looking to find the best combination of guys for the for the season. So, um I think we're we're okay. I think the depth could always be better at every position. um just to continue to build competition and and finding, you know, the right, you know, mix of guys that that are going to help us for this year. >> Mike, you mentioned in the offseason the desire to get pop the ball a little bit more. How have you seen him evolve and do you feel like he's capable of of getting more touches and being more influential on the offense? Yeah, I think that that you know Pop was you know I think the most impressive thing was that he was ready um whether he got 12 snaps or he got 30 snaps. I think he some of his best plays were his ability to to not catch the football and go and finish and he made plenty of plays for us. Um but his attitude remained um you know really good and I know that every receiver wants to get the ball more and you know I think we'll continue to try to find ways for for Pop to help us. um and then look at to where he can continue to improve. But you know, nobody cares more about the team uh than Pop Douglas. I think that shows by the way he plays. >> Coach necessarily have a ton of real competition this summer, but how are you making sure he stays sharp? And what did you like from him this this camp so far? >> I think he's made, you know, majority of his field goals, you know, a high majority. Um, and uh, you know, I think that that's something that's a fine balance of, you know, where you want your kicker to be, you know, is if you feel good about the competition or the job that he did last year, you know, then I I'll just try to evaluate that, you know, each week. And I think he's, you know, continuing to work with Tom on his steps and the consistency and everything else. So, you know, I know that there, you know, Bryce doesn't have any competition either. We got to make sure that, you know, those three guys is the, you know, more specialist you add that the less that you add on the rest of the roster. So, we try to figure out what's best for the team and and we felt like those guys would would be okay without having to, you know, have some sort of competition. >> Always been [clears throat] pretty secure and consistent who he is and comfortable in his own skin. year two, you know, maybe not growth as a player, but as he fits within the program. Do you see any differences from him daytoday or his role this season? >> Um, no. I mean, he's still going to do the news on Friday, so that'll be consistent. Uh, he was trying to talk his way out of that yesterday, but he did such a good job that, you know, he's earned that role uh for another year. Um, you know, I think just some little things that he's trying to work on and, you know, build with with Elijah over there on the left hand side. Um, how critical that, you know, connection is in that relationship of of how they want to work their combination blocks or how they block games. and but you know it's a young player that you know we have to continue to you stay on and you know he wants he wants to do a good job and he wants to play hard for us and and do all those things. So just keep moving keep moving forward. >> Thanks guys.

title: 2 Minutes at Training Camp: Drake Maye wins 2-minute drill on Day 9
text: All right, it was a newsy Tuesday here at Patriots training camp. The ninth practice, the 11th day including the two off days. The Patriots and Pads yet again don't see this a whole lot. Five straight padded practices for them. Tomorrow though will be a walkthrough if we all get to breathe. In the meantime, let's get to that news. Drake May had his first two-minute drill of the summer and it was a big success. He finished 12 of 17 overall and it was a slow start for him. Four straight incompletions, one of five. Then gets into the two-minute drill. Low ball from Romeo Dobs and then starts to pick up the pace. A check down to Hunter Henry. Demario Douglas off to the left on a crosser. Then a big pass to Matt Collins over the middle before a slant to AJ Brown. Closes it up with the spike and a good 54 yd field goal for Andy Boragal. So a it was nice to see Drake May overcome some early adversity as much as you can have it including some pressure which we'll get to here in a second. title: Greg Bedard Wants to See MORE from Drake Maye, A.J. Brown & Patriots Offense
channel_name: Greg Bedard Patriots Podcast with Nick Cattles
text: This is the Greg Bard Patriots podcast with Nick Cavins. Hey everybody, welcome into the Greg Badard Patriots podcast here on the CLNS Media Network. Brought to you by our friends from Prize Picks. Uh Patriots concluded their ninth practice. I think it's fifth straight um in pads uh ahead of tomorrow walkth through. The next two days are closed to the public by the way. They will be opened back up um on Friday, which I think should be a full practice and possibly padded. Um headline from today is that Drake May and the offense uh started slow, one of four with a sack. Uh as I've reported, everybody's reporting. Then he finished 10 of 11 the rest of the way. Uh I had him for two, I think, uh one more sack after that. Um, the truth of the matter is I, you know, that all happened. Those are the stats. Uh, I wouldn't say it was great. I I it did certainly get better, but after the first period and actually went into the second uh period, going back over my notes in the second team period for Drake May in the first team offense started off Raandre Stevenson was stuffed twice. Uh, then I think there was a short pass to Hunter Henry. Then uh Trayvon Henderson was stuffed. There were a couple short passes and then I think that period ended with a sack. And at that point uh we were on the verge of uh grumpy Greg because the first team offense was not good with the red zone work in the bubble yesterday. Only two of their five possessions was quote unquote successful. One of them was exclusively on the ground between Stevenson and Drake May draw. Um, so I was getting ready to sharpen. I was sharpening my pencil, getting ready to rip the offense for how ineffective they had been on back-to-back days, but it did get a lot better uh, from there on out. Now, it wasn't the greatest show on turf or anything like that. A lot of the passes, actually all of the passes were on the short variety. Um, there were a couple deeper passes to uh, Deario Douglas and M. Collins when it came to the final team period which was a situational period where there was 105 on the clock. They started on the opposing 20 and they had to get a field goal. Both Drake May uh and Tommy Dvito's units executed that and got field goals from uh Andy Boralis. As has been the case the past couple days, Devito's um unit did a little bit better than um Drake May's, but uh look, it it got better. Um you know, it wasn't high-flying or anything like that for for Drake May in the first team offense. And I'm I'm contemplating calling uh AJ Brown Mr. Sevenyard slant. Um often against the backup quarterback who's not there. Christian Gonzalez is there sometimes, but um you know, would like to see them start to make a little progress, but this is what happens when you have, you know, a new center. Uh you have a uh left guard that's new and didn't play last year. Um you know, you have AJ Brown and Romeo Dobs who are new to the offense. Um these things take time, so I'm not going to go crazy about it, but I have been a little grumpy. I have been a little bit grumpy about the first team offense the past couple days. Let's see if a couple lighter days resets them. They're better on Friday ahead of two off days and then next week is when things really start uh with the Colts coming in for a joint practice. Uh one thing to note uh about linebacker, something may be going on, maybe nothing. I can't really tell. All I know is Christian Gonzalez yesterday, not Christian Gonzalez, Christian Ellis yesterday got dinged up in practice. Mike Rael sent him off, said, "You don't need to be out here." Chad Muma, uh, the veteran, been a couple places, I think mostly the Colts, uh, came in, finished practice next to Robert Splain as the first team linebacker. Um, and you know, Khalil Jacobs is a guy that we've talked about, undrafted free agent. He's been, I think it's fair to say he's ahead of KJ Britt at this point, who's running mostly with the threes, does get some other time. Um, but today in that final team period with the second team defense, Christian Ellis was out there with Khalil Jacobs, which is interesting. That leads me to questions often does like, you know, did the Patriots like what they saw on Amuma on film from yesterday's practice and wanted to give them more of a look. Now, I will admit I didn't notice who was playing linebacker with the first team defense. Um, I assume it's Spain. It could have just been a big nickel situation and ju just getting Ellis reps on the second team. I have a feeling Muma was probably out there, but I missed him. But something to uh to look at. And I feel like we've gotten to see a little bit of one of the lesserk known guys in that competition recently. >> Yeah. Jaylen Daniels, who is an undrafted free agent out of Kansas. The Buccaneers were definitely excited to get him as an undrafted free agent. There is all the undrafted free agents get pretty much the same three-year contract. And then if you know if they're cut somewhere along the way then that is no more. But there is a certain amount of guaranteed money that they can get from anywhere from zero to a certain amount. And Jaylen Daniels the Bucks gave him nearly the max. So it's an indication that they they were high on him and think they have something there. And we've seen a lot uh from him that's been impressive. And I I there was a play uh yesterday where the pocket was collapsing in front of him and he was backpedaling and with no ability to step into his throw through like a deep out to the sideline which is a very difficult pass >> because of the width of an NFL field. It's a surprisingly difficult pass. Absolute dart. um right on the right on the money to fellow undrafted rookie um uh Eric Rivers and I asked Coach Bulls about it after the practice like is he impressed with his arm strength and his ability to make off platform throws. So, this is what he said. >> Like his arm strength, he can make some very unconventional throws. Obviously, you want to see the normal stuff as well, but when he gets in trouble, he can get himself self out of trouble. And that that's big. >> I know that also uh something we've been excited to see is how Zack Robinson decides to use the tight ends in his offense. And we've gotten to hear from Kate Uten for the first time uh since he's gotten to be learning Zack Robinson's plan. So, what did we kind of learn about from Kade? What have we seen and learned about that? Kade's excited about it, uh, about the role. Obviously, last year, Zack Robinson in Atlanta ran 12 personnel, which is two tight ends. Uh, second most in the NFL percentage of plays and roughly double what the Buccaneers did last year. So, that doesn't with our receiver depth, that doesn't necessarily mean that's going to be the case, but I think we'll probably see an uptick in 12 personnel. And uh Cade will be the guy that's going to be on the field all the time, of course. And if you look at the analogous situations, Kyle Pittz, who was uh Atlanta's number one, probably not as good of a blocker as Kade either, uh had 88 catches last year, but no other player, no other tight end on their roster had more than eight. So, you would think Cade might have uh targets funneled to him if he's, you know, the main guy on that field, and he probably will be. So, here's what Kade had to say about all of that. >> I I'm really excited about some of the stuff he's he's calling and showing us um from what they did in Atlanta and some new stuff he's bringing here. Um just like vertical play action pass game. Uh just how we're we're marrying the run and pass and how the tight ends are involved in that. Uh, I think we can be a big part of it and um, you know, you got to earn it during camp. You got to show you can do it and so that's kind of what I'm focused on right now. >> Yeah, I'll be interested to see what that tight end room is going to look like under Zack Robinson. And also, of course, we're going to take a quick break. We have plenty more coming up here at practice, but we wanted to get to this interview that Tony Castro Cone did with Ruben Bane Jr. Take a look. >> What's up, crew? Tony Caster Cone here with the first round draft pick, Ruben Bane Jr. And uh Ruben, I was talking to your family a little bit during practice today. How cool is it to have them just drive four hours up the road and be able to see you here at training camp? >> It's amazing. Um knowing that for me, I always have my family come back and support me. I always have I have a very supportive family where we all support one another. So that gives me that extra drive and that extra juice when I need it throughout practice looking over in the stands and seeing them. And it's going to be the same thing when they come forward any Sunday, Monday or Thursday, whatever game that we may be playing on. I know I got my family behind support me. So, it's that same drive that I have for that I have when I'm on the field. >> They told me you started playing tackle football at age four. What's your earliest football memory? >> Um, my earliest football memory probably me trying to quit football. I was um I tried to quit football like four times when I was growing up, but my parents just kept me in it. Uh, and you know, to this day paid off, I say. >> Yeah. What made you want to quit? Man, I could have sworn I was going to be a basketball player, so I thought I was wasting my time. But, you know, I was a little bit too aggressive. So, my parents figured it was good for me to stay in this and just stay active. And, you know, football panned out well. >> I'm sure you've probably thought of this before, but can you put yourself back in the position of that kid that wanted to quit and imagine if someone would have told you you're standing here in Tampa Bay as a first round draft pick, how that kid would have responded. >> Uh, man, this is it's crazy because it's so many different eras. Like at first I wouldn't believe it because I'd be like, "Man, I'm I ain't doing that. I'm playing basketball." But as I grow older and I got into my teen years, this is all I could imagine of of playing football at the highest of highest level and playing to the the best of my ability. Um, being one of those guys I talked on forever ago. And this is all I dreamed of. So now that it's here, I mean, I thank God each and every day I wake up to be in this position. But it's something I worked so hard for, something I prayed about each and every day. >> That's awesome. Uh, one last one for you. You were on a national championship game uh team in Miami. You learned a lot about what it takes to get to that level. Have you seen any of those things with this group here in Tampa Bay that makes you think this team can make a run in 2026? >> Yeah, for sure. The mindset and one the connection we have. I feel like we very very polished. Um you know, there's always more work to do, but we always come in with the mindset to get better. And I feel like it it speaks volume when you got the vets pouring into the the rookies than the rookies to the vets. I feel like that little details like that is what's going to make us so good. And we all play as one. We've been playing as one. I feel like since the OTAAS and seeing everybody here actually participating, being well in tune with one another, that's what gave me the glimpse of like, okay, we're going to be a good football team. >> So nice to meet you, Ruben. Really looking forward to seeing your rookie season. Congratulations on all your success. >> Thank you. Thank you. >> All right. Thanks for that interview, Tony. And man, let me tell you, at the autograph thing, people were hyped to get to meet Bane. His line was very long. There was an awesome little kid who had on a Bane mask that also had a Bucks logo on it, which I was like, >> that's a quick turnaround for finding something like that. So, that was a lot of fun. I know everybody's very excited about Bane. And then also, everybody's very excited about Zack Robinson and what he could bring. And we got a chance to hear from him today. >> Yeah, because of the night practice kind of the whole schedule's flipped. So, we did our media stuff before practice. So, I can add in in addition to what we already talked about, some stuff that we heard from him. and he was asked um what where is their competition important competition on this offense because it looks like most of the starting spots are set maybe all of them right and he immediately said depth at wide receiver he said we know obviously who the main contributors are going to be but how is the rest of that going to shake out and then the first name he brought up which is not surprising given what we've seen all this time is TZ Johnson and how much TZ He's he says he's just an explosive play waiting to happen. He makes explosive plays every day in practice. And it's an interesting mind. It's an interesting thing to think about because if you consider Godwin, Chris Godwin in the slot, Umecha Ibuka as your Z and Jaylen McMillan having a big role like where is the opportunity for TZ Johnson when you also have Ted Hurst, you know, and uh and a bunch of other guys as well. But if he keeps making plays, you got to find him. Yeah. >> So, it'll be He played 495 offensive snaps last year, but that was out of necessity. And he did a great job with him. But now, uh, the Bucks receiving court, Mike Evans, isn't here, but otherwise very healthy and very deep, and we still seeing seeing him heavily featured. So, I find it one of the more interesting topics of how this camp is going to shake out. and not I mean I wouldn't expect TZ has anything to worry about in terms of making the active roster but what's his role going to be? >> Yeah. Yeah, I completely agree. That's going to be fascinating to watch. Well, of course, since we do a position group to talk about every day, we figured since they're about three feet behind us that we should probably do the offensive line. That seemed like the best one to choose with this indoor. I know they're usually like way right here behind us. So, I kind of like that we have a little more breathing room. >> They're giving us some respect is what I think about >> Exactly. They were afraid of us. They heard your comment about Luke earlier and that's what it was. with that. >> You know, someone I'm excited to see this year is Graham Barton. He got thrown into some wild situations last year, to say the least. So, uh, what have you been thinking about with him and looking forward to this year? >> Graham was the only guy of the Buck's intended starting five last year who played more than 12 games. That's how bad it went in terms of injuries. But it that didn't mean it was a seamless season for him because what you're alluding to is the fact that with Tristan Warf now ready to start the season, he got moved to left tackle for the first three games. A secondyear center moving to left tackle and holding his own. That's impressive. >> Yes, >> that's impressive. And it probably has uh Cody Mal was saying that it is helping him in the long run. That experience has helped him in the long run. So, um, we'll see, you know, if that's true, but it's interesting. And now Graham Barton gets to settle in at center from day one. He's not going to be asked to play left tackle. And he had kind of an upward trajectory with a promising rookie season after being drafted in the first round. Kind of flattened out a little bit last year. And I think that's because of stuff he was asked to do early on and the fact that all the people around him were injured. Now he's got his guys around him back. He's he's settled in center and I think we'll see that tra trajectory going back up again. >> Well, I know Luke Geti's trajectory had been going up in the years leading up to last year of him getting settled in his position, feeling really good about who he's playing against and next to. Um, so I know it was a bummer to have him miss a lot of time last year because of course you feel like him and Tristan out there, you feel really great about your ends. I know that Luke is a guy that I feel like we we feel great about going into this year that I'm excited to see, especially again in something like Zack Robinson's offense when he is an athletic guy that can really do some more things. >> I think Luke is rightfully seen as one of the better right tackles in the league. Now, uh he got a big contract just before last season to reward that and, you know, to make that seem obvious. Um the one little thing about Luke is that so far in three of his four seasons, he's missed at least four games. Now, I think it's been freakish stuff. It's not I don't I would not call him injury pro. Just he got a one year was concussion. Right. Right. >> But it would be nice to see him get better injury fortune and play 17 games and see what that looks like. But, you know, the Bucks love him. They love the tone that he sets and he's one of the better players in at his position in the league. And I should say there are 16 players at the offensive line position in camp right now. So, we're not going to talk about all of them. There's a lot of interesting stories. We're just picking out a few. >> And speaking of interesting stories, those were a couple of the starters that we wanted to hit on. But in terms of some of the depth on this offensive line and and some of the guys that we're looking at to make that roster, make the the guys that are active on game day. Ben Chukuma is such a fascinating story and was really fun uh last year to see out there. So, what do we feel like his expectations could be for this year when he came in last year with so little experience? >> Well, Tristan Warf currently sidelineed with a hamstring injury. Not a big deal, but he's not playing right now. both him and both Ben Chakuma and Justin School have been taking first team snaps and um like you said he was an undrafted free agent last year out of Georgia State. He had a very limited background like I don't remember what the exact number was but 14 career games something or starts something like that. Didn't really play in high school. So the fact that he made the active roster as a rookie with that background was impressive enough, but late in the season he actually started a couple games and held his own. So uh the funny thing is with all of that being very positive. Coach Bull said the other day that it's like night and day between last year at this time and this year about how much better Chuck Wum is. I mean, logically that makes sense, but still he was so impressive as a rookie that that's a really good thing to hear >> for sure. And then of course, uh, we did add an offensive lineman in the draft. So, what do we feel like his potential is and what made them say this is a guy that they wanted to look at? >> Yeah. Fifth round draft pick, Billy Shrath out of Notre Dame. Um, the general consensus on him was that had he not suffered an injury last season, missed about half the season, and he probably would have been more like a third round draft pick. So, if the health things work out, the Buccaneers feel like they got good value there in the third round. And we've seen the Bucks draft a lot of interior offensive linemen in the second and third round that went on to became starters. Maybe not day one, but at some point. And I think that's the this guy has that potential. Now, barring injuries, the Bucks probably aren't going to need him to do that. So the thing for him now is earning a roster spot, which is probably going to happen because extremely few fifth round picks don't make the team. But you can make the team and then be inactive every day because they want somebody else active on game days, you know. So the big next battle for him is is he one of the one or two, probably two, reserve interior offensive linemen who have a helmet on for game days. And so that's kind of what I would think his pursuit is right now. We'll see how that goes. >> All right. All right. Well, that's going to do it for us on this edition of Training Camper Report presented by Advent Hill. Thanks for joining us here in the indoor. The guys are off tomorrow, so we'll be back with another show Thursday morning. We'll see you then.

title: Kenny Gainwell & Payne Durham on Enhancing the Offense | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How y'all doing? Good. How are you? >> Good. Kenny, a week in the train camp how naturally it feels. How how well you feel like you know this new offense? >> Yeah, I think everything that um this offense has. It's about um you know, I'm getting the flow of it. Um you know, I have to take everything one day at a time at the same time learning and I'm processing everything, getting ready for it. you've been out there with Bucky in the offseason, but he didn't get to do as much team stuff. Now that he's full go and you guys are sharing the ball back there. What What does that feel like between the two of you uh coming in and doing that? >> Um I think it's it's a great thing, you know, getting getting both of us out there and, you know, him being back balling and I'm I'm super excited to see him um back on the field and um I think it's just I think it's just great to see us both out there on the field at the same time and you know, I love it right now. People talk about the similarities between your skill set and his skill set, but how do you see you guys um differ in some areas? >> Yeah, I mean um I think I think I'm a big big guy in between the tackles. Bucky is a you know a spread out guy and um both of us do basically the same thing when we get ready to run routes and stuff. So, I mean, I think it's just, you know, different sizes, um, body types, but at the same time, we both have to be ready for what's to come and, you know, we can go out there and attack it. >> Does that make you seek out contact maybe a little bit more? I mean, he's still a tough guy, too. He's just a smaller guy, but like I mean, knowing that you have a little bit more on your frame, does that make you more inclined to want to go in between the tackles? >> Um, no. It's just it's just situational ball. It's just situational ball when it come down to it. Ken, you had one heck of a catch against Alex Angelone last year in in Detroit. Curious if that's come up at all through training camp or OTAAS or anything. >> Um, no. Uh, we talked about it for a little bit, but um I don't think he like me talking talking to him about it. But at the same time, I think it's think it's funny to um see us both here on the same team working together um going out there helping each other to be better be better so that we can he can not have that happen to him again this year. >> You've had the chance now to work with Skip Pete. How has that been? How has he challenged you? >> Yeah, that's been great. I love Skip and you know that that attitude that he bring towards the game and the way that we practice every day. Um him bringing us all all the running backs in together, you know, helping us want to be great each and every day. And I mean, it's good. I love working with them. >> Kenny, you guys reached the key milestone of getting pads on. You guys feel like you're in a good spot here in training camp as you start getting ready for the preseason games right around the corner? >> I think we good. I think we still have more work to do. I mean, it's a it's a everyday process. We still putting things in, but at the same time, I think we still have more work to do. Everything is not going to be great. You know, first day of pass, but as we do this practice today and see where we go from there. >> Kenny, we we had Zack Robinson in here and he was talking about just your versatility that there's almost anything he could ask you to do in a football field. He's confident in doing that. Pittsburgh used you a lot of ways. Are they finding even more kind of creative ways to use you in this offense? >> Yeah, it's more creative ways. We going we going to get things going. Um, but I'm I'm a very smart person and you know, um, when you have somebody that's that's smart and you can put them in different situations, of course, you can get creative with them. So, I mean, just just waiting for those opportunities. >> Are there some packages, some some formations where you and Bucky might be on the field at the same time? And >> it's a couple packages that we'll be on the field at the same time. We have our pony package that that people have been seeing in a couple days. U, but yeah, it'll be a bunch of packages. I know that you weren't here like before they made some of these moves on defense to try to get bigger and more physical and and get back to kind of stopping the run, but when you put on the pads for the first time and you're going up against this defense, what are you seeing from those guys? >> I see them guys coming off the ball. They coming off the ball fast, too. And um I'm loving what I'm seeing and like I think it's going to be hard for them to run ball run the ball against us this year and I think that everybody staying healthy that'll make it be 10 times better. Is anybody jumping out at you on the other side of the ball? >> Uh, I'm really loving what I'm seeing from Ya. Um, he's he grabbed me one time yesterday and I was like, "Dang." [snorts] But, um, I'm loving what I'm seeing basically from everybody, but Ya stood out to me. >> Kenny, you come obviously from Pittsburgh. Danny Smith was there. Just what is he like as a special teams coach? What makes him unique? His energy just seems like he's a 72-year-old with the energy of a 30-y old. Yeah, I mean he have definitely a lot of energy, but he's very technical and detailed on what he want done and what he want the guys to go out there and do. Um, he know me as a player when it come down to return stuff, but um, I think he's high energy, high energy guy. He going to be chewing his gum on the sideline yelling at people, but he's he's definitely a high energy guy and we need that around him. >> You have some joint practices coming up against the Jets in a few days. What are you hoping to get out of that as far as testing yourself, but also um I guess testing in the scheme, testing yourself out in the scheme? >> Yeah, I'm definitely looking forward forward to going against other other guys, other people um their schemes and what they have set um for us and, you know, other linebackers, getting one-on-one, you know, routes, running with people and pass protection. Just seeing what other people have in their bag and, you know, just taking what I have and just go get try to get better at it. That's all for Thank you guys. >> Thanks very much. >> How are you? >> Great. How are y'all? >> Thanks. >> So, we just we just had uh obviously uh Zack in here a minute ago, [snorts] a new offense. Um something you guys seem to learn quite often, but um just how's it going? from a tight end position, you know, with some of the outside zones, the bootlegs and things, how do you feel that the tight ends will be utilized, especially in the passing game, um, or what the potential is there? >> Yeah. Um, I mean, to to go first, I think Zach and all the offensive coaches have done a great job installing it and, um, breaking down the installs to where it makes sense and kind of group things together and it's it's been a very seamless, easy transition for us. So, that's been awesome. Um, and then tight ends, I mean, we're getting used a lot. Um it kind of goes back a couple years ago to kind of how we're moving around and and how they're scheming things for us, but um you know, we're definitely going to have our opportunities to make plays and it's it's definitely a fun offense as a tight end to play in. >> What about with Bower Sharp, the rookie? It seems like he's, you know, making a lot of plays. Whenever the ball goes his way, he he finds a way to come down with >> Yeah, Bower's looking really good. Um he came in and he he's had the right mindset and um just put his head down and gone to work and he's done really well and continuing to grow and getting better every day. So, it's really cool to see. >> Pay the Atlanta had I think the highest level of of tw of 12 personnel last year in terms of just just using 12 more. I mean, obviously you guys had good depth and receiver, too, but is that exciting when you see how much how much the tight end's factored into what he did in Atlanta the last two years? >> Absolutely. Yeah. I mean, I watched Charlie Warner a lot. Um, I think he's a fantastic blocker and uh, kind of how they used him I think was really cool and and something that I would like to do and um, something that I think can can help the offense be successful. So, however they see fit to to go 12 and like you said, I mean, our receiver room is stacked. So, to get our best 11 on the field, however the coaches want to do it. Um, I I it's it's a really exciting offense that we're going to play in. >> What are some of the things that you are personally working on heading into this year? You know, you know, physically, mentally, aspects of your game, stuff like that. Yeah, last year I was used a lot um in motions kind of in blocking game a lot um in the back field going in motion, kicking out um climbing up to linebackers, stuff like that. So really just honing in on the technique of that um me and people have been working a lot just technique-wise um in the run game and then continuing to create opportunities for myself in the pass game. Um like we said in Zack's offense, there's a lot of movement, a lot of bootlegs, ways to get tight ends open scheme things. So really just all around everywhere in my game. Um, every year for me it's it's find things in the season that I can attack in the offseason and go from there. >> How hard is that to, you know, at your size go in motion, climb up on some of those linebackers that clearly are, you know, trying to not be blocked by you? >> Yeah, absolutely. They don't like it a whole bunch. Um, no, I mean, there there's a technique to it and some linebackers are better at avoiding. Some guys will will try to use power and go through you. Um, so it's really just scouting who you're playing, see what they like to do, and um, adjusting your technique weekly on that. >> With with how big of of, you know, big of a part of the run game the tight ends are. Obviously, last year so many injuries on the offensive line, Buckyy's hurt as well. Just how much are you looking forward to kind of having that rebound season with that group? >> Absolutely. Yeah. I mean, when we're on, I I think we're a top run team in the NFL. Um, having the the the boys up front back will be huge. And uh I mean even in parts of last year I think it speaks to our depth that we were able to kind of plug and play guys like you see Graham playing left tackle in the first couple games and how he kind of transitioned into that and I think it helped his game at center. Um so having everyone back um getting Bucky back and KG um and Shawn coming out in the Buffalo game and having a great offseason um I think it'll be really exciting to run the ball back to the standard that we know we can. And I know that you have a particular fondness for coach BS. And right now he's got his hands full not only getting stuff ready out on the field, but also you know you got Baker um you know not getting the contract extension he wanted. Vita's not out there practicing. Um just his unique way of managing those things where he's able to help really keep everything about football when it's out on the practice field. How does he manage to do that? >> Yeah, absolutely. Um, I I think first and foremost the team that we have and ourselves and those players, everyone's bought in on the mission of this season and uh the outside media is one thing. I mean, that's going to happen regardless, but that that hasn't spped an inch into our locker room at all. Um, so in that aspect of it, it's been very easy for Coach Bowls because there's none of it for him to coach off of. Um, but I mean, I can speak for days about Coach Bowls, what what he is to this team, this locker room, and the leader of men that he is. And um, I love playing for him. I I think he's the best. and really excited. >> Pay, um, training camp's obviously about setting the tone for the season, but it's also a great opportunity for you guys to give back to the community with the signings and the access to practice. I mean, what does like being able to give back to the community like that mean to you? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, it's huge. Um, we wouldn't I mean, military day yesterday, none of us could do our job if those guys didn't do their job. So, that one for me personally is huge. And then getting the kids out here just I remember being a kid going to things like that and how much it meant to me and how I still remember it. So, it's awesome being able to give that back and um just making someone's day. >> Thanks, guys. Good to see you. Yep. You, too.

title: Zac Robinson: Bucky Irving is a ‘Stud’ | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Oh, >> I was going to say we've asked you this kind of each step of the way, but with with five practices under your belt, just ask how you feel about being able to implement things and how how well they're taking what you're getting. >> Yeah, I think it's been good. You know, it's uh it's been a lot of great work against the defense. You know, you see a bunch of different looks. you're able to work through a number of different things just based on what those guys present each day. And you know, the installs, it's a quick install to kind of get everything in. And so, um, you know, we're at a point where, hey, got a lot of stuff in and you're trying to dial everything in in terms of, you know, formations, motions, alignment. You know, now we've got basically, you know, I would say 85% of the offense in. And so, we got to hone in on the details, fundamentals, all those things that, you know, all of our coaches are coaching in their position rooms. But um guys have done a great job and I know talking in the spring with guys and guys have been here in CG and bake and some of these guys like hey how much new to you know guys previous you know and so they've been saying it's 50/50 and so like there there is a lot of new u but there's also you know some good carryover from previous years so that's been good but getting a lot of great work in and we'll just continue to kind of hone in on what what we're going to look like once we kick this thing off. Coach, you you met Baker and coached him when he didn't have a job and he was there for a couple days and played with you at the Rams and um you know, anytime guys go through contract things. I know he addressed the team about it, he certainly had his his say, but you were a player like it just how how much do you think his ability to to kind of separate that and and what signs have you seen that Baker's Baker, man, when he when the lights come on? >> You said Baker's been Baker. um you know the contract stuff's been out there but haven't been able to tell you know he's he comes in he's the exact same guy every single day competitive wants to know what's on the script what we got what the defense is doing and uh you would not be able to tell at all that that's going on he's been I know he said it but he's he's been all balling he means it and that's exactly what he's been every day as as you uh implement things to have TJ to have the MPC to have guys that you work with that were with you in Atlanta how much does that help just to have more people that have been there and know what you want to to help pass that. >> Yeah, it's been huge. You know, those guys obviously we worked through a lot of things the last couple years together, kind of getting into our own rhythm and flow and then um it's been a lot of fun to just kind of keep collaborating and then also learn some new stuff that um has been done here that you know we could possibly carry over into the season as well. So, uh that's been great. And then the the coaches that have been here um it's been really fun to work with carbs again. And obviously we had some time in LA and being around B-Mac and obviously I was around Skip in LA and um you know first time being with Peele and Castle and Blaine. So like it's been a really cool collaboration. I mean you get in there in the offseason you're like okay what do we want this thing to look like? And it's a lot of work that goes into it. Everybody's got their hand in it. So it's been a great collaboration between the whole group. Um but having kind of a mix of some of the guys that you know been around and also just some new thoughts that that we can always take and and try to learn from. So, uh, been been a blast working with these guys. Look forward to, you know, just keep continuing this thing and obviously getting into the season and what it's going to look like knowing that from, you know, this day to September 28th, it could look completely different. So, uh, it's been a great great collaboration between the whole group. >> We've talked to the offensive line and they've stressed, you know, working on the wide zone concepts this season. Uh, the Bucks have had success with gap in the past, but how do you think that transition is sort of going now? And what about this offensive line, their skill set make you think that, oh, this is going to be a great fit for this team? >> This offensive line is incredibly versatile. Um, there's really nothing these guys can't do. Watched it for, you know, past couple years on tape, just on crossover tape. Obviously, I've seen the gap stuff, seen the zone, seen the duo games, seen number of different variations, perimeters. So, uh, you know, it is a a well-rounded group that, um, they're taking everything in stride and exactly what that's going to look like once we start kicking this thing off. You know, kind of to be determined, but we're working everything right now. We'll start honing in on what we want to be, you know, truly here in in a couple weeks once we kind of reset after um, you know, the Jets practices and you're looking at, you know, just a handful of weeks before you actually play a game where you want to, you know, kind of hone in on what you think you're going to be. So, uh, those guys can't say enough about just the investment they that they put in, how smart they are. Um, it's a it's a great group to work with. They're incredibly physical, you know, feeling what it feels like in pads with those guys, you know, especially in some of the pass protection stuff as well. Um, it's a firm, you know, group up front. So, uh, been great working with those guys. Look forward to just keep building, keep getting reps, and, uh, ultimately kind of figuring out where we go with it. >> You didn't have a chance to work with Bucky much in a team type setting. now that he's out there just what have you noticed about him and just uh you know the fit that that he's going to have with Kenny and what you're trying to do? >> Yeah, Bucky is a stud. I mean, watching him in 24, explosive play waiting to happen. Obviously, you guys saw it up close every single game, but um he's just got such a great attitude, great spirit about him. Team [snorts] guy, always has a smile on his face. So, just the person has been just cool to get to know him. You know, still getting to know a lot of these guys. you only have so much time in the spring, but uh kind of, you know, feeling the personalities of guys now. Buckyy's been great and obviously the talent speaks for himself. Uh the way that he runs the football and just his feet are always in the ground. So, he's always able to change direction and obviously that keeps him so balanced to to break tackles and uh the versatility he has in the pass game, you know, run game. Uh you know, he's he's done a great job. It's been a blast seeing him just kind of cut some of these runs and you you start seeing it. So, uh, the compliment between really him and you mentioned [snorts] Kenny, um, he's done a great job since the spring. Obviously got the bulk of the reps there and, uh, got a good feel for. And then, shoot, Tux. Tucks obviously made a lot of plays and Josh Williams has had a great camp as well. So, we have some backs that are that are exciting that have a versatile skill set and we'll just kind of keep taking it uh, where it goes. But, those guys, it's a great group of guys, man. But, Bucky, he he gives me a smile every time I look at him. He's he's a stud. >> Zack, how's your chemistry evolving with Todd? I mean, obviously that connection is going to be important, obviously in critical moments on game day. So, how is that starting to develop now? >> It's been great. Todd is awesome to work with. Um, obviously has so much experience. Um, seeing how he sets up practice and the situational work uh that we're getting has been has been cool. It's been a little bit different than places I've been, but we're getting a lot of great work and it's very intentional with the reps and why we're doing things and why we're working all these situations now for when those come up. But he's such an easy guy to obviously pop in and ask any questions about. Um, you know, there, like I said before, it's a lot of defense in training camp. Going against it in games is one thing and then you see it up close and realizing, uh, the issues that, you know, they can present to an offense. Uh, I've always got questions for, you know, for him and it's been cool. You know, his office is right next to mine. So, uh, it's been a good relationship and and, uh, look forward to just continue to build throughout training camp before the season starts. When you go into a new place, you have these ideas of what you want to implement, but then you've got to kind of get under the hood and really see what you're working with. And sometimes those ideas may evolve a little bit. Is there anything that maybe you thought you knew about this offense or that you thought you wanted to do, but then as you kind of got to know the guys more or got a feel for things more, maybe you decided to pivot a little bit? >> It's a great question. And like we talked about the first day of camp, it's a great time to try things out and kind of, you know, figure out what we what we can do and and maybe something that, like you mentioned, we thought we were going to do, but we're not going to end up doing it. And so, uh, we're still in that process, though. And, and right now, we're, like I said, we got the bulk of the offense in um, and then really tailoring it down to, you know, get those reps that we need to get reps at. Uh, in order to get good at something, you have to have some sort of identity, obviously, to be a good offense. And uh that's what we're focused on right now. But uh there hasn't been anything since we got here like, "Oh, I don't think we can do that." Or there's been some ads, you know, that you get you go through the spring, get summer break to kind of take a look at the stuff from the spring and you're saying, "Okay, hey, maybe we can do this or this or maybe we need to add this formation to get this person in this spot." So football is always evolving and it really never stops. And so, um, like I mentioned before, from now to the middle of the season, things could evolve and take a life of its own and you just are in a discovery state. Uh, and that's where it's awesome to have really smart players as well. So, those guys can handle a lot of stuff and, uh, us as coaches just have to make sure we don't give them, you know, too much where we can hone in on things and make sure that we're fundamentally sound and, uh, the things that we're all all coaching. >> What does Gain Lo's play style bring to the offense? >> Yeah, he's super versatile. Um [snorts] he's great with the ball in his hands. He's very smart. Um he's great pass protector. Uh there's really nothing on the field that you can't put him in a situation and it seems like you coach him up one time on something and boom, he's got it. So, uh that's been a luxury to have. And so we'll we'll continue to just find out, you know, where we can put him in the best spots along with the rest of those guys with Bucky and uh the rest of those guys. But [clears throat] um but yeah, Kenny is he's really smart. Obviously, you see it on tape when you watch guys. You get a good feel for um you know, just how smart, how instinctual they are, how they see the game. Then you get to talking to him and you're like, "Okay, that matches up with, you know, how he plays." But um he's another one that's just got a you know, energetic, you know, kind of spirit about him. And uh he's he's been a blast to work with and looking forward to just kind of continuing this thing going. >> You don't have a ton of offensive starting spots that are really up for grabs, uh but a lot of backup spots. Are there any backup jobs right now that you think are are particularly intriguing in terms of showing off the depth you have? >> Yeah, I think the the the wide out position, it's really deep. You know, I know we know the guys that we're going to be really counting on and then it's finding who those other guys are going to be and and I know Tez has had a great camp. You guys have seen that have been out of practice. He's making explosive plays every single day. you feel his juice out there and um he's done a great job, you know, from the spring to now with the offense and getting lined up in the right spots and um he's he's doing a great job. And obviously, you know, Ted's coming along. He's still still young, still learning, still, you know, figuring everything out, but he's he's been uh he's been sharp so far. And um you know, you got Cam and Sills and you know, some of these other guys that are all competing. They're doing a great job. All of them have made plays throughout camp. the ball's really been kind of going everywhere as you guys have been out there. A lot of guys are getting involved. So, um it's been great. And then the tight end room, you know, finding out with Bower and and um you know, and Co and those guys and Culp seeing how that's going to shake out. But, uh so early in camp still, but it's been cool to see just the versatility throughout you know, all those position groups and and uh you know, the different things they can do. >> Zack, this offense has been through a lot of change the past few seasons with different offensive coordinators and a lot of injury. How has that kind of resilience and just willingness to do whatever it takes and like able to pick up things quickly? How has that helped them to pick up your scheme pretty quickly? >> You said it, it's a resilient group. Um, from the moment I got here, guys coming up to my office, introducing themselves like you could just feel the group like they want to be great and that's uh obviously they've they've experienced that as well. So that the evidence is there for for them to, you know, play at a very high level. And um but you feel it every single day from those guys, whether it's the offensive line, setting the tempo, you know that Baker's going to bring it every single day. And and you know, guys like Jaylen McMillan, um obviously resilience from, you know, his injury last year and uh coming back and and and how he looks right now. Um you know, all those guys. So it's it's a it's a really cool group. Uh but that word that you mentioned, resilience, um it's definitely helped with just kind of like, all right, hey, whatever we got to do is whatever we got to do, and you definitely feel that from those guys every day. >> What are some of the biggest things you've seen from quarterback Jaylen Daniels, uh you know, as a offensive coordinator and a former quarterback and maybe what are some of the biggest things that you're working on with him, you Chandler Weber and the rest of the staff? >> Yeah, he's he's done a great job. He's really smart. He's, uh, you know, coming into a completely different scheme, obviously from a college scheme that he played in. Um, he's taken it all in. He's getting a decent amount of reps, you know, throughout practice, but his arm is explosive. You guys have seen it out there. Uh there's not a throw he can't make or a throw he doesn't believe he can't make, which obviously that's finding the right balance um with a young cap. But uh he he's he's done a great job and and um you know, he just continues to learn to play the position and you know, hey, when when can I hang in the pocket and go through my reads? When can I bail and and try to make a play? Obviously, he's got some unique ability outside the pocket. But that's the biggest thing with all those young guys, you know, is just, hey, play within the scheme, play within the timing and the rhythm of the offense, get the ball where it needs to go, and then if it does break down, that's where you use your god-given ability and make a play. But, uh, Jaylen's doing a great job. And his arm, like I mentioned, it's uh it's it's one of the better ones I've I've been around. >> What's Faker doing now that's better than when you saw him a few years ago? And and where does he need to still improve? Yeah, I think he's he's gotten, you know, drop back pass is always for every quarterback. Those those passing downs, that's the toughest downs. And um his ability to continue to progress and move on from one to two to three. If three's not there and you got to move, go do your thing. But uh that's probably the biggest thing is just those those reps in the pocket on third downs in those tight situations. since he makes so many plays outside the pocket, but then his ability to click through things and and find a find a completion on the backside, that's NFL football. Everybody's got to got to do it. And so that's probably the biggest growth also being, you know, in a system that he's comfortable with a lot of the, you know, the reads. And so he's had, you know, built-in reps, uh, you know, throughout the last handful of years. But, um, Arm, you know, looks even better than I remember it from LA. And, uh, he's throwing the ball accurately. Chandler's done a great job just tightening up his footwork and uh getting the fundamentals, you know, over and over. I mean, if you guys talk to Chandler, uh there's nobody that likes, you know, footwork more than him. And so, uh those guys have had a great relationship, good working relationship. So, uh there's there's a lot of things that he's definitely grown, but I would say the drop back pass is is probably it. >> Two more questions. >> You see Baker kind of respond to disappointment a few times, right? in LA. He was just trying to get his career back on track and he was a little worn down, beaten down by that. And then of course here he doesn't get the new contract that he wants. Just how have you seen him respond to that? >> Like I remember watching him at University of Oklahoma or at Texas Tech for that matter, he he believes in himself and whether other people believe in him too, he really doesn't care as you guys know. And so uh he he's the same guy every single day. one of the most competitive just people I've been around and uh being back out at practice in these settings and seeing that and really the ownership he takes as if something doesn't go right, you know, he's he's got a great ownership about him of of you know, hey, my bad, you know, and that's that's all you always love that from your starter, you know, you always love that from your leader. If those guys have accountability and ownership, it bleeds to the rest of the group. And so, um, but yeah, it's been so fun to just see again, you know, just being out there and feeling the juice that he brings. He's of course talking to the defense and um you know just he's the guy that's getting the whole thing going and and we wouldn't want to have anybody else. >> What is the key then for for somebody that because he's talked before he's been open about the fact that yeah sometimes he does have negative selft talk turning those disappointments into something that can actually catapult you forward. >> Yeah, I think you know you probably have to talk to him a little bit more about it but he's um you know he's just he's been through a lot. you know, obviously he was your number one pick and then um kind of gets kicked to the curb in Cleveland. Not sure if it was warranted or not, but is what it is. And then he like you said, me was able to reset himself in LA and uh just take off from there. But, uh his his mentality is that, you know, kind of underdog mentality he's had since I'm sure he was eight years old starting to play football. That'll never leave that guy and and um it's a good thing. and just channeling it the right way, you know, just channeling everything the right way and and using that um that chip that he has um in in a positive way. >> Okay. Thank you, coach. >> Cool. Thank you, guys.

title: Robert Saleh, Anthony Hill Jr., Amani Hooker, Tony Pollard & Cordell Volson | Tennessee Titans
text: Uh, I'm sorry. We had a couple of injuries. I think it was Craig from [screaming] We had Denmark. Um, the other two from that. >> There's a couple guys there. We're going to check all the injuries. I'm not exactly sure what they are. Um, I don't know if they're going to be dayto-day, if it's just going to be something that happened in practice, but we'll get more for you guys uh tomorrow. >> It was a a friskier fireworks type of practice today. Uh, is that, you know, you kind of pulled everybody together after the couple the second scrum. What was your message and did they react after that? >> No, they did a good job. It's a second day of pads. It's hot. It's muggy. Um, you're expecting it. Uh, especially with the way the O line and Dline get after it. And so, it's just a just a reminder that we got work to do. It's okay. Like, uh, I got brothers. We fight all the time, but at the end of the day, we're still take care of one another. Make sure we're getting getting the work done that we need to get. >> Did Jeff leave practice on his own or did you tell him? >> No, he was uh our our policy is if you if you throw a punch, you're ejecting the game. Uh, same thing with practice. If you throw a punch, you're out of practice, but rather than going to the locker room, he went to the other fields. He still got his work in. So, the projected reps and the work that he would have got in, he got in off to the side. >> That's always, you know, Jeff, our O line and D lines, we want them playing with edge and uh, we want them to tow the line. We want him to tow the line and be gnats and and we just got to learn how to draw the penalty, not give the penalty. And uh but we're always going to tow the line of violence. We're going to we're always going to tow the line of being aggressive and and um call it instigating if you want. It's just the nature of who we're going to be. But uh but we've got to be disciplined enough to make sure that we always find our way back to the huddle without giving the other team freebies. >> Now that you had the corrective measures here, do you anticipate having to go through that again? >> Yeah. [laughter] These guys are I mean they're they are absolute animals. Their mindset when they put helmets on. And guys, you got to understand like the the mindset of these men when they're when they're in uniform, they're they're different. They're different. That's why they play the sport. And uh you know, you're you want them to be able to express all that emotion. They just have to learn how to be disciplined with it. So we're we try to let them go to like I said, we're going to we're going to edge what they're capable of, but they're they've got to find the discipline. Good to see different guys stepping up today. We saw some new players make make big plays. >> Yeah, there was there was a lot of really cool plays on both sides of the ball. I think Anthony had a couple of picks. Um it it was good. It was back and forth. It's kind of what you want to see uh from from uh both sides of the football. >> A little bit easier today, >> man. You know, just just doing my job. Like at the end of the day, you do your job, good things happen. >> What's been the biggest area of maturity for you from when you started to now?
