I'll say like just my eating habits, learning how to eat right, be a pro, get recovery, just doing all the little stuff that just helps me on the field. >> Comfortable you're feeling on the field each day. >> I feel it's like it's small details, you know, you're going to mess up on, but just trying to find like a a big picture and something that you know you can work on every day has really helped me out a lot. So, just trying to get better at little things every day to just try to help me be become a better football player. >> What was the change in your diet? Uh, so me, I'm a big candy person, so I had to cut off I had to cut off the Mike and Nikes and all that stuff. So I cut it off and it worked. So I just tried just kept doing it like you know it's just something that's hard but you know it's better for yourself. So >> how many Mike? >> Not like not really a lot but just just cutting like just cutting it off like you know just to just for myself like I'm a big I like sweets so I had to limit myself. Maybe we do once a week not three. So it's just little small details and you know it it worked. I lost I lost around like six six seven pounds like just cutting off sweets and just trying to eating right at the house just cooking myself like we not going out. I'm just been cooking myself. >> What's your best meal? I >> I like chicken fried rice. I can cook that really good. Like I make good smothered chicken. I made like some some fajita fajita beef and tacos. You know, just you know it takes a lot of time and I don't like doing the dishes but it it worked out. It worked out. Were you a big drop and cover guy in college or is that something that's kind of been added to your game more since you got here? >> I'll say it's it's probably been the biggest improvement that I had to do in college. I did it a decent amount, but not to this level that I had to do it here. So, I kind of had to kind of use some of the stuff I did in college, but take it to another level. So, just kind of relying on the vets and kind of relying on some of the guys that been here to kind of help me through some of that stuff. Is today's success kind of an indication that some of those finer details you were working on are maybe starting to click a little bit at this point in game? >> I'll say like what I learned so far being in NFL, like take the don't take the good too good, don't take the bad too bad. So like even though I made those two plays today, like we got to come back tomorrow or or Thursday whenever we practice again and scrap it. Like so you never want to get too high with the high, too low with the low. So I'm just going to come ready to play next practice and hopefully the same result happen. Who who took the ball on the second? >> That's a good That's a good question. Like I couldn't see. I was so far away, but it was it was a heck of a play and thank thank you whoever it was. Thank you. >> What do you have along the Lions Nuggets? What are your expectations for this season? What are >> uh I really just want to help the football team win. Like that's all my goals is. As long as it's special teams, if it's defense, whatever it is, I just want to help the team win. What do you think your biggest strength has been so far in this game as you begin to ad? >> I'll say my versatility. Like I'm a guy that I feel like I can play a lot of different spots on the football field. So just continuing to kind of work on that, cleaning up details like hand placement, just getting to my landmarks in my drop. So just keep working on little stuff as I get closer to the season to help me out. >> Was up here. He said he he was working on like a final one specific role for you helping you. How has that work? >> It's been it's been pretty good. Like I've been focused on playing Mike right now. So just being able to hone in or focus on one spot has really helped me kind of develop and understand what I have to do in that in that role. >> What you been able to learn from some of the other guys in your room, James Williams, Cedric Gray, and any others? >> Like just little stuff like hand placements, working on the uh recovery, getting massages, hot tub, cold tub, just every little thing off the field and just on the field. Just keep playing fast. And you know, you're going to make mistakes, but just keep playing fast. was talking about your learning curve on special teams. First off, did you play much special teams? >> No, I didn't play a lot of special teams. I was a I did some punt return, but I didn't do a lot of it, but it's crazy. A lot of the stuff that we do here kind of translate to just playing linebacker. So, it's like just keep it simple. You know, the biggest learning curve for me right now is plant. So, just trying to get better at that every day and just just taking it day by day. >> What's in terms of camp in the NFL and camp in uh in college? I'll say camp in the NFL, it's it's way longer days. I feel like the days are a little longer and the practices are a little bit more physical. Like it's a it's a different learning curve. Like the the quick snap, get on the ball fast. You have to know your assignment. It's just little small details that just makes camp in the NFL a little bit harder >> between offense and defense. So far in camp, >> I think it's been good. I think we've been very competitive back and forth. Um you can see, you know, yesterday defense had some plays. today. Offense and defense had some plays, but um it's been good competition. >> What are some things you wanted to focus in the end of the camp and end of the season? >> Um getting the playbook down, a new scheme. Um trying to see what France San Fran defense last year was doing. Some of their safeties were moving and um just trying to get up to speed on all the playbook so I can play fast. >> Feel it fits with you, what your strengths are? >> I think it fits very well. I mean, being able to communicate with guys, putting guys in good positions to, you know, make plays all across the board. What's the biggest changes for you guys in the secondary with this new scheme? You know, everybody obviously can see the switch back to a 4-3 for them run guys, but what's the biggest changes for you guys? >> Um, just just technique-wise. I mean, every defense plays certain, you only play certain amount of coverages, but there's small little details of technique-wise that are a little different from past, but I mean, that's just getting reps in and just being able to communicate. on this. >> I know there's a little stuff in every camp, but just as you kind of see this for a year or whatever, how do you process why that happens? Is it good? Is it bad? Is it just part of football? >> I mean, it's part of football. I mean, it can be a little bit of both. We're trying to We're all brothers trying to protect each other. Um, as long as we like to have it happen in between the whistles. Um, because, you know, in a real game, you get kicked out, penalty, penalties, penalties, and you can hurt the team. So, we want to make sure we at least protect the team. How nice has it been to see the number [screaming] of times guys have gotten their hands on the ball or come up with a turnover the last couple days? Uh, >> it's been great. I mean, that's that's what we preach here and being able to create turnovers and get the ball back to our offense and short fields, it's going to turn to points. You >> hear so much about the guys up front playing faster, more direct in this defense. Safety, I don't know if you're supposed to be as downhill as they are, but are you playing faster too? How does that work? >> Yeah, I mean it it goes hand in hand. And I mean if the defense is playing Dline's going to play fast and we have to be able to be fast and react off them as well. So it's it's it goes hand in hand. You >> had a pick yesterday. I think there were three more from the defense today. How contagious is that? How good is it that when you guys can make those plays practice? >> Very contagious. I mean that's just how this league is. You know, you want to be able to get hot and stay hot as long as possible as many days as possible. Um, we had a nice array of guys getting interceptions, whether it's DBs or linebackers across the board, and that's what we want to see. >> How encouraged are you off? >> I'm very encouraged. Um, the energy in the building, um, how detailed the coaching staff is. Um, even our strength staff and training staff. I mean, everyone seems like they're all bought in, and that's what it feels really good. >> Kind of struggled a little bit today. How, you know, how are you seeing uh the things starting to come together now two days into that? >> Um, I mean, I feel like we're doing a good job competing, you know, going back and forth with the defense. You know, things were a little chippy today, but you know, that's expected when you first few days in past just getting getting back used to things and um, you know, it felt good just just being out there. >> What did say to you guys when he kind of gathered you practice after things got chippy? >> Um, just just reminding us, you know, we got the same goal. We're on the same team at the end of the day. You know, we're expected to come out here and compete. It's going to be tough. It's going to be hard, but we got to realize we're working together. See, >> you guys were able to get strong a couple of inside runs today. How do you like the way all three centers have been able to help finish? >> Um, I feel like we've been doing a great job, you know, um, filling in O line, just being able to, you know, get the run game going, getting all the different backs going, and just, um, being on the same page with the O line and the running backs. Tony, after the last couple years, how motivated are you to get this turned around and enjoy some wins around here? >> Um, I mean, it's it's always motivation behind winning. Everybody wants to win. Um, once you've, you know, had such a hard time winning and struggled with it for so long, it just it just fuels you to just just go harder. >> What's been what's been some things you've enjoyed about Nick Singleton's game and him coming in the league? What have you noticed about how he's playing? He had some nice runs today. >> Just how physical he is as a runner and you know just seeing him day by day get more and more comfortable in the system, more and more comfortable with the plays and you know it's showing on the field he's making more plays day in and day out. >> How do you like the the dynamic of this this running back room you got yourself and Taj >> playing in contract here. You got a young excuse me a young youngster Singleton and in the middle you got Chestnut and M. Um, I mean, we have a very competitive room, but you know, at the end of the day, we all work together. You know, we all cheer for each other when we're out there on the field. You know, um, we help each other out, give each other pointers and things. So, you know, we're all competing, but at the end of the day, we're working together at the same time. >> How's this offensive scheme doing some of your strengths? >> Um, I feel like we do a great job, you know, playing to guys strengths on this on this um, in this offense. you know, just getting guys in open space, you know, getting guys running routes that can catch the ball and, you know, just not just using guys that as a running back or just using you at one position, you know, moving you around on the field. >> You specifically play your >> um I feel like we do a great job, you know, just being able to line up in the slot, line up at receiver, make plays out wide. Um the different motions and sweeps that we have with the offense, just a lot of misdirection, especially with me and Taj in the back field. So, I feel like it plays great into that. >> Tony, when you when you see the dynamic between Cam and they evolve, I guess what gives you optimism that that could be like a a unit that or you know, TANM that can really gel to to get Cam to continue to ascend. >> Um, I mean, those are two guys with, you know, very strong personalities and, you know, they they do a great job of of meshing together, you know, working together. you know, they have times when they may butt heads, but it's all, you know, constructive. You know, it's all constructive criticism and, you know, nobody takes anything personal. So, everybody's able to take coaching and just be themselves without letting it get to them and have them down. >> There's always talk about the the age clip with running backs. Kind of what are you doing to protect yourself from that? Prevent yourself from from age so quick. >> Um, I mean, you got to stay going. You got to keep your body in motion. You know, offseason really isn't the offseason. Um, you may take a few days off or a week off, but you got to do a good job of just keeping your body going and just and just stay moving. >> Um, just doing little things. You know, they do a good job with the offseason program. They give us packets to work on at home, do things on our own, and just doing that and then just doing whatever you do on your own. On top of that, >> Cam says he feels more like situationally aware when he's out there on the field. Is that something you can see being in the back field with him? Uh definitely just the growth, you know, from his decision making on the field. You know, he's young. He still makes some decisions that, you know, we correct, but just seeing him check the ball down and just when it's not there, not trying to force anything, taking the check down, taking the short routes and letting his his players make plays on their own. >> What What techniques and things are you looking to hone in when it's kind of tough to do chemistry at this point of the season? >> Yeah, I think first and foremost, um you know, learning the system inside and out. I think that's a big thing coming to a new system, you know, learning the the little little tells or the little tricks that have maybe been um added to the system over the years of having the system. Um and then once once you know all those little tricks and then it's just playing fast from there. >> And then for you in particular, you're coming back after not playing us so long. What were some of the biggest challenges that you've encountered so far? Yeah, I think um you know some of the biggest challenges is like you said, I just didn't play football all last year due to the injury and and so now just um you know kind of getting back into the game, the flow of the game, the speed of the game um you know right now maybe a little little slower to react to some things that I would like to be just cuz um you know it's been so long since I played but um day by day it's coming back. >> How do you feel? You came here in March and you've been here for what three four months now. How's the culture? How's the team? How's everything as you kind of envision it when you got here? >> Yeah, so far so good. Um, I've loved being here. Uh, love our head coach. Love love love coach Dable. Uh, love learning from Carmen Isaac in the O line room. I think we got a really special group in our old line room. Uh, dudes that work really hard and and love being here and love each other. >> What's kind of your mindset as you try to win that job? >> What's what's your mindset as you try to win win a starting job again? Yeah, I think my mindset is just show up every day and find a way to get better. Um, you know, and and while I'm doing that, help help those around me. Uh, because because at the end of the day, Wii is greater than me. >> I know you grew up small town working for your family's company. How has that kind of prepared you for moments like this when you're trying to earn a starting job? >> Yeah, I you know, you know, growing up it was didn't matter how you felt. You know, you got up and you went to work and and that's that's the same way here. um you know there's going to be days where things don't go go the way you plan them to but um how do you how do you respond to that? You know, I remember my dad, we were it was it was during CO um was in college and we had a had a bit of a break for for CO and you know, I was helping him out and one of those days where where several things went wrong and um you know, I looked at my dad and I was like, you know, how how do you deal with this every day and he just looked at me and he said, you know, son, if it was easy, everyone would be doing it. Um, you know, so that's just something that that I carry with me and and um, you know, know that I get the opportunity to play this great game and and not take it for granted. >> What are you kind of trying to show each day just in practice kind of make a case for yourself? >> Yeah, just just continual improvement. Um, you know, learning the system more and more every single day, being physical, playing extremely hard, um, controlling the things that I can control. Those are the biggest things, you know, my attitude, my effort, how hard I play. Um, you know, and I control what I can I control what I can control and the rest will take care of itself. >> For you going from established offense in Cincinnati, Super Bowl expectations, that sort of thing to maybe more of a team that's trying to establish something here. >> Um, you know, not really. I think at the beginning of every season, you know, you have to establish what your identity is as an offense. Obviously, you know, in Cincinnati wi with Joe and and Jamar T, their chemistry, you know, so they obviously had had some some of that figured out, but um you know, I see some of our receivers and see the way Cam makes some throws and um I know that we can we can do some of those things as well. >> Do you feel like in the process of trying to establish that? >> You know, I think I think every day we we gain a little bit more of our identity. Um you know, it's a it's a whole new offense, whole new staff. Um, everyone's still still getting to understand each other and um, you know, we're we're continuing to build our own identity and that's what camp is for. >> Offensive line at this point, but how have you guys been able to find maybe a little bit of a rhythm in the running game just in a couple weeks? >> Yeah, you know, I think um, coach coach uh, Karm does a great job of of really detailing our run game. um detailing the technique we need to use as well as the scheme and and having good schemes in pa in place and and coach Dable calls calls some some great runs at the right time and and we're able to be efficient. I know the offensive line works in unison together all all five positions, but what's it like playing next to the center Austin Schlotman and a mix of right tackle, whether it's JC Laam, Austin Deculus, Brandon Krenshaw Dixon. What's that been like for you? >> Yeah, you know, um I think that that gets overhyped sometimes if if you will. Um because we're all in the same meeting, we're all having the same conversations. Um, but then you just got to understand maybe maybe AD will set something a little bit a little bit different than than JC will. Um, so just knowing who you're who you're with and and having that communication. I think that's the big thing. Um, when you play next to one person for a long time, you can kind of read each other's mind a little bit, but um, we're a lot of us are new here. So, um, you know, we have to have that open communication and then once once [snorts] the spots get solidified a little more, then then maybe we can move on to the, you know, the next >> chemistry. As far as um, >> when we develop chemistry, I think it's a lot of it is just knowing how we're going to fit some blocks together. Um, you know, how we got a sore protection, how we're going to get, um, you know, the defensive end funneled into us. um knowing knowing kind of situations when we want to get on players versus when we want to set off. Um you know, I think I think that's the big thing when it comes to chemistry. You kind of know um what the guy's going to do without him having to say it just because you've been through that situation time and time again. >> More questions for >> All right. Thanks, guys. Have a good one. You too.

title: Brian Daboll, Gus Bradley & John Fassel Speak at Titans Camp | Press Conference
text: lot accomplished. Got a long way to go. Um but uh I think the guys came back in shape, ready to work, had a good understanding of the playbook and the things we did in in the off season. Just trying to build every day grind. It's going to be a grind here for the next couple weeks. Uh a lot to work on. Uh but pleased with where we at at the start here. >> Robert Salah had talked about the three pillars of quarterback in his red zone, third down, and two minute. What's your take on that? Do you feel those are the three pillars as well? >> Yeah, they're important situations. You know, how you perform early downs um can really help you in those situations as well. Uh skipping third downs, u being able to run the ball in the red zone, uh two-minute, you know, you're you're getting ready to, you know, deal with a bunch of D linemen that, you know, you know, you got to throw the ball. We're putting them in disadvantaged situations. um hired a new analytics guy. Benny's done a really good job of, you know, going through some of these situations. I've sat down with him, talked to him, you know, percentage-wise, you know, where we put the ball, how much time we have left, how many timeouts, how many teams have done it in the last 5 years. Sometimes it's 10%, 9%, 20%, 30%. Uh you have to give young quarterback, really all quarterbacks, as many of those situations as you can. Uh red zone, same thing. We've done a lot of work down in the red zone and and third down. You know, the longer the the yardage, the lower their percentage, the more looks you get. Uh the harder it is to protect. Um you know, the easiest thing for a defense is know when you have to drop back pass. Uh and they can tee off. So again, it it kind of goes all together. Those situations are are critical. Uh but so is first and second down. What's your maybe Cam's best traits are as a player and maybe and how much is the offense or what you're going to do going to be geared around that? >> Well, we're going to try to gear it around around Cam, but but also the other guys, too, and what they do well. Um, it's a team game. It's the greatest team game there is. It takes all 11. You know, you can watch a clip from a practice and it looks really, really good and there's 10 guys doing the right thing and one guy just not and and the play could not be as productive as it should be. Uh, so we'll try to, you know, continue to grow scheme-wise. Uh, you know, with Cam, he his job is to, you know, lead the offense, to make good decisions with the football, uh, to throw it where he speaks to throw it, to get us out of bad plays if we don't have the right look, uh, to make the right decisions uh, on a playby-play basis. And that's that's not an easy thing for a quarterback. There's a lot of things you go through. But again, you know, back from OTAAS to now, he's grown every day. We're continuing to evolve the system and he's done a nice job. >> Trabiscy told me he's been in some situations where he might make a positive play. Yeah. >> But still in the film session he'd be told he he was wrong, he didn't go where he was supposed to, things like that. And that you are very counter to that. How how important is it for you that your quarterbacks and Cam don't feel that way when they find something good, even if it's not necessarily what you were looking for? Um, break it down for me again. Sorry. >> So, you find something that's not necessarily what the play called for. >> Yep. >> It's positive. >> They do they do something else. They hit a play and maybe it wasn't the right read. Again, some of those are are that a boys, you know, they have to play the game. We're standing on the sideline. Um, there's rules to every play for every position. Um, a lot of things happen for the quarterback and he might see he thinks one thing. It's it's a lot easier when you're going through with the clicker and you're rewinding it 12 times, but things happen in, you know, a split second. They have to make a decision. So, you know, our job as a as a, you know, a coaching staff is to make sure that we're making corrections. Things are going to happen out here. Um, but there are non-negotiables relative to effort and technique and ball security and things like that that, you know, we demand. >> But there's some freedom built into what you're >> Yeah. Look, they're not we're never going to make them robots. Um there's part of it is feel. Part of it is an instinctual feel that I think you know the quarterbacks that have been out here have a pretty good um understanding of that. They're they're athletic. Uh they can make some loose plays. Um and we're going to build off of uh again whether it's a mistake or they thought they saw something. Our job is to go back into the classroom and and make sure we're all on the same page. Um, and they might have a different vision of it, you know, Paul, from being back there in the pocket than I have on the sideline. Usually the first thing I'm going to say to those guys when they come off to the sideline is, "What'd you see?" Unless it's just a complete, you know, shouldn't do that. >> Cam has said he's grown a lot in understanding the the why of what you're calling. How have you seen that show up when he's operating on the field? >> I just think it goes back to the meetings. Um, and you you build you have to build a good relationship with these quarterbacks. Um, it's a high pressure job. Um, I think they all love it, but there's a lot that goes with it. And we have to have good give and take in the meetings. I'm always going to tell them what I think and they don't always have to agree with me. And at the end of the day, we come, you know, come together with a good resolution uh that is best for the team. Um there might be times where camp says hey I'd like this this and this and I look at and I say I don't really think that's good because of what they're doing here. Then he'll look at and say yeah you're right. Uh there might be other times where I say I think we should do this and he's like what do you think about this and that's all the quarterbacks and that's Shay and that's Cade. Um maybe it doesn't hit your head that way and then you look at it and say you got a point here. So let's go ahead and tweak this and and see what it looks like tomorrow in practice. Um, and that's what these are for. >> Giants didn't do a ton of motion last year. Uh, I guess compared to to the rest of the league. Was that kind of a one year specific for you? Do do you tend to change a lot or do you not favor that in general? Maybe compared to >> Again, I think it it depends on um who your quarterback is, what you feel comfortable with, how we play. We play with a lot of tempo. Um, we were up at the ball, shot clock was very very high. uh gives a quarterback a bunch of time. You know, you can have long long calls and and huddle up, which we'll do. Um and that takes some more time. So, you know, the last thing that I want for the quarterback is for them to be breaking the huddle at, you know, 7 seconds and scrambling to the line and then, you know, the young quarterback just throws it and he has no time to decipher what he needs to see. Um and then you're, you know, you're all mad and you know, part of that is on you, too. So, again, it's a I think there's a balance. I don't think you go one way or the other. Um, you have to do a variety of things in in today's game. But again, it depends on, you know, how we do in training camp and and what the quarterbacks feel comfortable with, what we feel comfortable with as a staff. Um, you know, there's different ways to try to attack a defense, wear them out, limit some of the pass rush. Tempo is one of them. There's a variety of other things. You can shift, you can move, you can get underneath center. Um, and we have all that in in our package, if you will, and we'll just keep growing with it. >> Can you kind of go into detail? The quarterbacks have touched on the fact that they don't all get the same plays called for them in the same period, so that they you can run more of the playbook, but knowing that each quarterback may see it a little bit differently, how do you use that as a teaching tool when you go into the film room and the practice study? >> Well, well, the first goal is that they don't see it, you know, much differently. um that we're all kind of seeing it through the same set of eyes from the vision of the play when you design it to the person that's sitting behind center. I think it's important to have continuity with that. Now, something may happen where you fix it, but you know, we have a variety of plays and I think part of training camp is to to figure out what you're really good at and you know, camp can't sit up here and take, you know, all the reps in a period. Mitch is out there, Will's out there. And you know what we'll do is we'll do walkthroughs too at night where some of the things that you see let's just say Mitch and Will getting today. Cam has repped that last night in a walkthrough setting against the defense. So he's still training his eyes. It's not full speed and there's no substitute for practice full speed but mentally you're getting the rep and seeing the different things that you know the defense may do. We'll do a pressure period uh where he's got to set protections and we just try to, you know, accumulate as much tape as we can as many plays and examples of things that can happen and then you're teaching off of that. You know, it's a rarity that you come out here and, you know, you call the same play four times and you get the same thing, which is good, which is what you want. So, you can teach off the different looks defensively, the spot drops of the defenders. Maybe they're playing two high, one high, maybe it's a pressure look, maybe they're bringing everybody. Um there's a lot of things that go along with it. third down situations that I know in the past you were able to help Josh Allen be able to extend plays but also minimize the turnovers. How did you do that and how can you spin that over to camp looked like yesterday? You know throwing across his body? We know that's something he likes to do but how do you balance that? >> Uh again the job of the quarterback is to make the right decision. So you know Cam is a very talented passer of the football. uh he can put it wherever he needs to put it. Uh those guys that have a lot of talent um you know that have a strong arm, they have a lot of confidence. So at the end of the day, something like that, um you got to make the right decision and that's that's what these things are for. Uh you know, you can hit some big ones, use your legs if you need to use your legs. Uh again, third down is is you know, a hard down. Once you get to third and four plus just say it's it's significantly an advantage of a defense. Um and that's any defense. So try to stay out of those situations, but when you're in them, everything's not going to be perfect. There's a lot of bullets flying. Uh different pressures, disguises, looks. Um and it's not always going to be perfect on third down. Try to end every drive with a kick should be the mentality of uh of our quarterback. >> Go ahead. >> Sorry, you're good. What was your feedback to him after those those two interceptions this year? >> Um, look, he's he scrambled out on a couple of them. Uh, he thought he had something and he tried to put it in and you can see it for a split second being open and those close up. You know, you it's it's everything is a riskreward for the quarterback. um situation we're in, decision you make on a throw. Uh you know, throwing back across your body when you're rolling one way. Uh it might work a couple times. Um but lesson learned. Um you know, on those two plays, which is good. This is why why we're doing it. Uh but I I don't ever, and I said that with the other quarterbacks I have. Um I want them to have an aggressive mentality. I want them to go after it. Um, but at the end of the day, we're charged with making the right decision. All of us. >> Off of that, what have we seen from Cam and his ability to kind of reset and correct in that moment when he makes those decisions? >> He's great. Yeah, he's, you know, we talk about every play has its own identity. So whether we have a, you know, a rip pass down there to Rid, which what an outstanding catch by Rid yesterday. But, uh, then the next play reset. Everybody's got to get back in the huddle. When we do huddle, reset, move to the next play. if we have a poor play because that's going to happen. You know, you take a look at, you know, offenses around the league historically, you know, four yards on first down, half the deal on second and whatever it is, convert third and fourth. The success rate, if you look at it, is not very high for any offenses. The top of them are just around 50%, maybe a little bit more than that. So, there's going to be ups and downs for everybody in this game. So staying composed, focusing on the next play, have that next play mentality, good or bad. You know, you can you get pretty excited, too. I've had guys that, you know, throw 80 yard bombs or 60 yard bombs and they're so fired up and then the next play isn't what it needs to be. So, uh, just putting a a string collection of good plays together offensively is is what our goal is. Um, and you know, it's a work in progress so far. >> A great deal goes into being a very good screen team. How much of a screen team do you want it to be? >> Oh, I I think it depends on you're definitely going to have the screen as an element of your offense and it depends on the type of defenses you play. Some some teams are read and react defenses where they're not just up the field penetrating up the field and it's a little bit difficult to screen some of those defensive linemen. Others are one gap penetrating defenses. Maybe it's a perimeter screen, maybe it's a tight, like the screen game has to be a part of your game, but you also have to do it relative to who you're playing and and what you think is good. And um you know, Luke Stalker has, you know, put him kind of in charge of our screens and installing our screens. Our tight end coach done a fabulous job with it up to this point. Um but it's just part of the package. It's like you want to be under center and throw run actions. You want to be shotgun and go no huddle. You want to run screens, you want to run outside, inside. There's there's a collection of plays that obviously every offense can put together and we try to do what we think is right for for that particular game. >> Putting in work that we don't see whether it's watching film, texting you at all hours, stuff away from the building. What have you seen in that regard? Yeah, I'd say I get here pretty early uh every day and most of the time he is in the in the team room sitting there watching tape, you know, with maybe a couple other guys that he pulls along. So, I think that shows his teammates that he's very serious about football, which he is. Um they're in with the huddle in the in the film sessions. They show he shows that he's a competitor. I think the players, you know, the job of a quarterback is to earn the respect of your team, earn the respect of your coaches, earn the respect of the players, earn the respect of the fans, and that's that's what you sign up for when you play quarterback in this league. And, uh, he's been, again, I've said this since I've been back here, whenever it was, March, April, he's he's been great. um student of the game, learns from his mistakes, leads, competitive, tough, you know, fiery, there's a lot of good qualities to work with >> of pads. But, you know, overall, I think, you know, if you just to give an introduction, uh really pleased with how our guys have handled everything. You know, OTAs, you get kind of a feel for where they're at, how they learn. But, uh the one thing that I will say is I think these guys have a really really good football IQ. like they they are able to pick things up quick. Um, you know, you they pick different times to try to challenge them, overload them with information, but they really don't flinch on it. They take it all in. It might not be executed perfectly, but that what they're what we're trying to get to, they understand that part real well. So, just as a unit, the fast and violent part of it, that's what we're always shooting for. And if they can understand what we're doing in the package, it seems like those qualities kind of show. like Michael Robinson. We saw him in OTAAS and then again yesterday. It seems like he's been in position to make plays, but he's been on the wrong end of a lot of What do you say to a guy like that in in that situation? >> Well, that that's why you have training camp, right? But he is skilled, you know. I think the biggest thing looking at him, he learned and he said, "Hey, if he goes out there and he plays man, he's he's been very effective in man coverage over the course of the time that he's been here, you know, and seeing him on film." So, we're trying to broad that now to say, "All right, now let's have that same type of temperament with our zone coverages and some of the different things that we're doing." So, there's going to be guys out here, I mean, we know it's kind of it's not a straight line. We start here, we're going to get better every day. There's going to be some ups and downs for some guys. And I think as a coaching staff, we're really watching. It's not so important that we understand that down days could happen. We're really looking to see how they respond to those days, you know, because we're trying to pick the 53 right guys and we know there's going to be challenges during the season. So, we need those right guys to handle those challenging times. >> There are plenty of great players in this league who are better suited for like a a read and react style defense. What What's the difference for a guy that is better for this attack style defense? >> Well, I think if you would ask a Dlineman, they you know, they all want to attack. you know, they all want to be aggressive up front and you have more of an attack style and um you know, every team is different their philosophy. They'll be attack at times third down, other times they ask them maybe to two gap. So, this is generally more of an attacking style defense. So, you know, but for some guys that haven't been in the system, there is a learning curve to it, especially if they have been more of a read react team. So to get them to understand that just trust their instincts, get off the ball and you know and and they understand football well enough they'll be able to do it. So I think it takes a little bit of time for that. >> So what are some of the biggest trade-offs? Because if it was, you know, some some magical fix for defense, every great defensive can run it. So what what is the give and take? >> Well, I think when you look at defensive line, you know, a lot of teams will look at spacing, you know, and how do you minimize that spacing? So, you know, I think you got to have a a Dline coach that's really convicted in it, you know, and we have one in Aaron White. I mean, he's coached it for years. I mean, that that's his baby. He believes in it. And if there's, you know, you got to know the warts in the defense and know some of the things that how teams try to attack you and then have some answers to it, whether it's by different calls or a style that you kind of have the D lineman play. So, you know, there's a big pitcher part of it as well. I know the Niners didn't do a lot of blitzing last year. What were you guys do there? >> Well, I it's it's I'm sorry to cut you off. Um I I think in the NFL, it is all about affecting the quarterback and how how do you affect the quarterback? So, I mean, in the ideal world for us, it'd be like we want two waves of Dline group. You know, here comes the first wave, here comes the second wave. We can rotate them, we can keep them fresh, and then it's that fourth quarter rush that's critical, right? So you try to, you know, have your first group out there at that time and you hope that you rotate enough and kept the level of the standard of play. Plus, I also think for the D linemen, they know I'm going to be out here for these two series or this series. They go, they know another group's coming in, they regroup and they come again. So that part of it now, yes, we want to pressure at u, you know, and opportune times. You know, we need a big play, things like that. Now, it still comes down to affect in the quarterback. If we can't do it with the four guys or the, you know, the rotation that we're doing, then you can see that percentage go accordingly. >> Were you satisfied with the pressure last year? I know you guys had a ton of injuries in San Francisco, too, but were were you okay with with the level of pressure? >> I I think that, you know, you go by a game, you know, sometimes the teams that you're playing and then you also, you know, it's not just tying it in to the front end, it's also the back end. You know, it's like, hey, can we hold up in man coverage? Can we hold up isolating guys? Can we hold up with single safety middle? Can we hold up? You know, you kind of put it all together that way. So, every team's a little bit different. I will say this, we really like the Dline. You know, I think they're really coming along. We feel like, shoot, there's some guys there that, you know, I' I've mentioned to you guys before setting the standard and the pace. I think, you know, when we look at the group right now, that delineignment that they're doing that thus far, thus far for us on >> that second level, the defense with James Williams, seems like he's come come along the last couple days. How do you see his role within this defense? >> Well, I I'm especially excited about him. I mean, he's changed his body type. He's, you know, they were 34 scheme and he did some things. He was 240 plus pounds. He's lost 20 pounds. Um, and that's what we asked those guys to do as linebacker groups, set included. We said, "Hey, get a feel what we're asking of you to do in OTAAS and mini camp. Have a general idea of where you think your body needs to be at along with our discussions and come back in training camp, you know, and act accordingly." That's what James has done. He is, you know, we like those guys that have played safety in their career and move them down the linebacker. We feel like we can get them to use their hands and punch and get off blocks, but that pass coverage part of it, that safety background that he has, I think is, you know, allows him to be a little bit more instinctive. >> Watching him coming into the league, like it gave me the Telvin Smith vibes. Is that something that that you see? >> Boy, you're going back there. >> Yeah, I mean, he's a little bit bigger, you know, um, than Telvin, but Telvin had that length and size. You hate to compare guys to it, but I just think for him it feels like he has a a pretty good understanding of the defense right now. So, it helps us because we can see when he is playing fast. What does that look like? And you're you're seeing it too, right? You've seen him make a couple plays out there. You're seeing him like, shoot, he's understanding it pretty well, well enough for him to play fast and show us that skill set. >> Mike seems almost obsessed with get off. They work on get off a ton. guys almost consider that the start of the pace and what's the big game. >> Yeah, there's no doubt up front it it's all about that part of it getting off um you know multiple drills and I mentioned to him before he's a great defensive line coach. He does a great job with our scheme and you know he's very uh convicted on that part of it and it's not going to change. you'll come here five weeks from now and it'll be the same thing. But it's building that mindset consistently, you know, to get off get off. And that's I I've had conversations with Jeffrey about it. He's excited about that part of it. >> How's Anthony coming along? >> He's done a nice job. We've got him at one position right now, the mic position, because there's quite a bit on that plate. But, uh, I' I've seen him as far as handling the defense, you know, addressing the defense, taking charge of the defense, and then there's a lot of things happening in practice, right? And it doesn't seem to phase him. Uh, he's not there yet, but, uh, the progress he's made. He's really done a nice job this off season till now, changing his body type, you know, becoming a pro and how he goes about doing things. I shouldn't say becoming. I think he always had that mindset. I think we're just challenged him to take it to another level. He was such a playmaker in college. How do you I'm sure you want that at this level, but how do you balance the accentuating that versus the stuff in life where you happen to know everything and know the responsibility of other guys too right now, >> right? We we have a lot of dislikes in our defense. So, there might be multiple packages. title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (August 4) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Mike Om Omar and Andy have uh drafted a lot of offensive linemen but with high picks in the last couple of years. That's what I was referring to. But, you know, I think I think you asked me um someone asked me the first day, you know, about the position flex and and it's you really see it in the drill work. Mike, what what was it you you think uh Rico D is such a good fit in your offense and just early on how he's fit with his new teammates? I >> mean, Rico is a hell of a football player.
